Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 7, verse 4:

As for the fa' (فاء), it is laid down to indicate sequence (ta'qib, immediate succession), and it may also indicate causation (tasbib) and ordering (tartib). Both of these return to the meaning of sequence, because what follows them always comes right after what precedes. Causation is like "I struck him, so he wept." Ordering is like ﴿We destroyed them, and Our punishment came upon them by night or while they were resting﴾ (Qur'an 7:4). The fa' here is used for the ordering of the wording, because destruction must be mentioned first, since giving it precedence is more fitting, even though the coming of the punishment preceded it in actual existence.

From this is the saying: a man ruled, then his father ruled, then his grandfather ruled after that. Here thumma (ثم) is used for the ordering of the speech, not the ordering of meaning in existence.

This is the meaning of the statement of some grammarians: that it comes to indicate order in the report, not in the thing reported. However, in my view there are two other interpretations of the verse that are better than this:

The first: that by "destruction" is meant the intention of destruction, and the verb is used to express the intention, which is common. So the coming of the punishment follows the intention in the way that what is intended follows the intention.

The second, which is more subtle: that the ordering is the ordering of detailing after a summary. So the destruction is mentioned, then it is detailed in two types: one of them is the coming of the punishment "by night" (bayatan), i.e., at night, and the other is its coming "while they were resting" (al-qa'ilah), i.e., at midday. He specified these two times because they are the times of their comfort and tranquility. So the punishment of God came to them at the time when they were most at rest and calm, in accordance with His custom, may He be exalted, of seizing the wrongdoer at the time when his hopes are fulfilled, when he is at ease, rejoicing, and content with what he is in.

Similarly is His saying: ﴿until, when the earth took on its adornment and became beautified, and its people thought that they had power over it, Our command came to it by night or by day﴾ (Qur'an 10:24).

The point is that the ordering here is the ordering of detail after a summary, and it is an ordering of knowledge, not of external occurrence. The mind first grasps the thing in summary, then seeks its detail afterward; but in external reality it occurred only in detail. So reflect on this point, which is hidden from many people, to the extent that some thought the ordering in the verse is like the ordering of reporting, i.e., "We informed you of this before that."

(The Eleventh Category)

The category of people who mixed righteous deeds with evil ones: they performed good deeds and major sins, and met Allah persisting in them, not repenting from them. But their good deeds outweigh their evil deeds, so when they are weighed, the side of good deeds prevails. These too are among the saved and the successful. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the weighing on that Day is the truth. As for those whose scales are heavy, they are the successful. And as for those whose scales are light, they are the ones who have lost themselves, for what they used to wrong Our signs.﴾ [al-A'raf: 8-9].

Hudhayfah, Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, and others among the Companions said: People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection in three categories. Whoever's good deeds outweigh his evil deeds by even one, enters Paradise. Whoever's evil deeds outweigh his good deeds by even one, enters the Fire. And whoever's good and evil deeds are equal, is among the people of al-A'raf.

This weighing takes place after retribution, when the wronged have taken their rights from his good deeds. If something remains of them, then he and his evil deeds are weighed.

However, here there is a question: if evil deeds are weighed against good deeds and the good deeds prevail, does the outweighed side become entirely nullified, so that the effect belongs to the prevailing side and he is rewarded for all his good deeds? Or do the evil deeds equal to the good deeds drop from the good deeds, and the effect of the excess remains, so that he is rewarded only for that excess? There are two opinions on this. This is the view of those who affirm weighing and wisdom. As for those who deny that, it carries no weight for them, and the matter is left entirely to pure divine will. According to the first opinion, the effect of the evil deeds is entirely eliminated by the prevailing good deeds. According to the second opinion, their effect is a reduction in his reward, not in the occurrence of punishment for him. The second opinion is preferred because, if the evil deeds did not nullify the good deeds preceding them, and the action and effect belonged to all the good deeds, there would be no difference between their existence and non-existence, and there would be no difference between the doer of good whose entire deeds are good and the one who mixed a righteous deed with an evil one.

This may be answered by saying that they did affect the reduction of his reward, necessarily. For if he had occupied himself at the time of committing them with good deeds, it would have raised his rank and magnified his reward. And if that is so, then the first opinion is preferred, since when good deeds overcame evil deeds, the effect of the defeated, outweighed side weakened, and the judgment belonged to the dominant side, the defeated being absorbed by it, just as a small amount of impurity is absorbed in a large quantity of water, and water that reaches two qullahs does not carry impurity. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 7, verse 16:

The majority of exegetes and grammarians said: the preposition "ʿalā" (on) has been omitted, so the verb takes the accusative. The intended meaning is: "I will sit in ambush for them upon Your path."

The apparent view is that the verb is implied, since one who sits upon a thing is attached to it. It is as if he said: "I will certainly cling to it, lie in wait for it, and make it crooked for them," and similar expressions.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: "Your clear religion."

Ibn Masʿūd said: "It is the Book of Allah."

Jābir said: "It is Islam."

Mujāhid said: "It is the truth."

All of these are expressions of one meaning, namely the path that leads to Allah, the Exalted. The hadith of Sabura ibn Abi al-Fakih has already been mentioned:

"Indeed, Satan sat in wait for the son of Adam on all of his paths," and the hadith continues.

So there is no path of goodness except that Satan sits upon it, seeking to cut it off from the one who travels it.

**Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on Surah 7, verse 17:**

And His saying: ﴿Then I will surely come to them from before them﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas said, in the narration of 'Ata' from him: "From the direction of the worldly life (al-dunya)." In the narration of 'Ali from him: "I will cast doubt on them about their Hereafter."

Likewise al-Hasan said: "From the direction of the Hereafter, denying the resurrection, Paradise and Hell."

Mujahid said: "'From before them': from where they can see."

﴿And from behind them﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "I will make them desire their worldly life."

Al-Hasan said: "From the direction of their worldly life: I will make it appealing to them and desirable to them."

And there is another narration from Ibn 'Abbas: "From the direction of the Hereafter."

Abu Salih said: "I will cast doubt on them about the Hereafter and make it distant for them."

Mujahid also said: "'From where they cannot see."

﴿And from their right﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "I will confuse for them the matter of their religion."

Abu Salih said: "The truth: I will cast doubt on them concerning it."

And from Ibn 'Abbas also: "From the direction of their good deeds."

Al-Hasan said: "From the direction of good deeds: I will hold them back from them."

Abu Salih also said: "﴿From before them, and from behind them, and from their right, and from their left﴾: I will spend it upon them and make them desire it."

Al-Hasan said: "﴿And from their left﴾: [the direction of] the evil deeds; he commands them to them, urges them upon them, makes them desire them, and beautifies them in their eyes."

And it is authentically related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "He did not say 'from above them,' because he knew that Allah is above them."

Al-Sha'bi said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down mercy upon them from above them."

Qatada said: "Shaytan has come to you, son of Adam, from every direction, except that he has not come to you from above you. He cannot come between you and the mercy of Allah."

Al-Wahidi said: "The saying of those who said that 'the right' is a metaphor for good deeds and 'the left' is a metaphor for evil deeds is good, because the Arabs say: 'Put me on your right, and do not put me on your left,' meaning: 'Make me among those who are foremost with you, and do not make me among those who are behind.'"

And he recited a verse of Ibn al-Dumayna:

> ﻿O daughter of Lubna, if you placed me on your right hand, would I rejoice, or would you place me on your left?

Abu 'Ubayd related from al-Asma'i: "It is with us 'on the right,' i.e., in a good position, and the opposite of that is with us 'on the left.'" And he recited:

> I saw the sons of paternal half-brothers, when they united against me, taking my share among them in the left.

That is, they put me in an evil position.

Al-Azhari related from some of them concerning this verse, ﴿I will surely come to them from before them﴾:

"That is, I will lead them astray until they deny what has preceded of the affairs of the past nations; ﴿and from behind them﴾ regarding the matter of the resurrection; ﴿and from their right and from their left﴾, meaning I will mislead them in what they do; for the acquisition (al-kasb) is spoken of as: 'This is because of what your two hands have earned,' even though the two hands have not produced anything, since they are the origin of action, so they were made an example for everything done by other means."

Others, among them Abu Ishaq and al-Zamakhshari, said, and the wording is that of Abu Ishaq: The mention of these directions is for emphasis in affirmation, meaning: I will come to them from all directions; and Allah knows best. I will act upon them in misguidance from all their directions.

Al-Zamakhshari said: "Then I will come to them from the four directions from which the enemy usually comes. This is a parable for his whispering to them and his enticing them as far as he is able and capable, like His saying:

﴿And incite whomever you can among them with your voice, and rally against them your horses and your foot soldiers﴾ [al-Isra' 17:64].

This agrees with what we related from Qatada: 'He came to you from every direction, except that he did not come to you from above you.'

This view is more comprehensive in benefit and does not contradict what the early generation (al-Salaf) said, since those sayings are by way of illustration, not restriction."

Shaqiq said: "Every morning Shaytan sits in wait for me at four watchposts: from before me, from behind me, from my right, and from my left. He says: 'Do not fear, for Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.' So I recite: ﴿And indeed I am most forgiving toward one who repents, believes, does righteousness, and then remains guided﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:82].

As for from behind me, he frightens me with the loss of those I leave behind, so I recite: ﴿And there is no creature on the earth but that upon Allah is its provision﴾ [Hud 11:6].

From my right, he comes to me through women, so I recite: ﴿And the good outcome is for the righteous﴾ [al-A'raf 7:128].

From my left, he comes to me through desires, so I recite: ﴿And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire﴾ [Saba' 34:54]."

I (Ibn al-Qayyim) say: The paths a person takes are four and no more. He sometimes takes a course to his right, sometimes to his left, sometimes ahead of him, and sometimes he turns back behind him. Whichever of these paths he takes, he finds Shaytan lying in wait for him upon it. If he takes it in obedience, he finds him upon it holding him back and cutting him off, or hindering him and slowing him down. If he takes it for disobedience, he finds him upon it carrying him, serving him, helping him, and promising him. And if he happens to descend downward, he would come to him from there as well.

Among what bears witness to the correctness of the sayings of the early generation is His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿And We appointed for them companions who made attractive to them what was before them and what was behind them﴾ [Fussilat 41:25].

Al-Kalbi said: "We imposed upon them companions from the devils."

Muqatil said: "We prepared for them companions from the devils."

Ibn 'Abbas said: "What was before them: the affairs of the worldly life; and what was behind them: the affairs of the Hereafter."

The meaning is: they made the worldly life attractive to them until they preferred it, and invited them to deny the Hereafter and turn away from it.

Al-Kalbi also said: "They made attractive to them what was before them of the affairs of the Hereafter: that there is no Paradise, no Hell, and no resurrection; and what was behind them of the affairs of the worldly life: what they were upon of misguidance." This is the view chosen by al-Farra'.

Ibn Zayd said: "They made attractive to them what had passed of the corruption of their deeds, and what they would go on to do of it." The meaning according to this is: they made attractive to them what they had done and not repented of, and what they intended to do and did not resolve to abandon.

So the saying of the enemy of Allah, ﴿Then I will surely come to them from before them and from behind them﴾, encompasses the worldly life and the Hereafter; and His saying, ﴿and from their right and from their left﴾:

The angel of good deeds on the right urges its companion to do good, so Shaytan comes to him from this direction and holds him back from it. And the angel of evil deeds on the left forbids him from them, so Shaytan comes to him from that direction and incites him to them. This explains what was summarized in His saying: ﴿By Your might, I will surely mislead them all﴾ [Sad 38:82].

**(Benefit)**

Regarding the use of the plural form "al-shama'il" (the lefts) in His saying, relating the words of Iblis: ﴿Then I will surely come to them from before them and from behind them and from their right and from their left﴾:

The plural here corresponds to the multitude of those he wants to mislead. It is as if he swore that he would come to each one of them from before him, from behind him, from his right, and from his left. It would not be good here to say "from their right and from their left" (in the dual sense for the group). Rather, the plural here corresponds to the whole with the whole, which requires the distribution of individuals. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿So wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows﴾ [al-Ma'ida 5:6].

(Section)

The first of Satan's guile and deception was that he deceived the two parents with false oaths: that he was sincerely advising them, and that he only wanted them to remain forever in Paradise. The Exalted said: ﴿So Satan whispered to them to reveal to them what was concealed from them of their private parts, and said, "Your Lord has only forbidden you this tree, lest you become angels or become of the immortal." (20) And he swore to them, "Indeed, I am to you of the sincere advisers." (21) So he brought them down by deception.﴾

Al-waswasah (the whispering) is the inner speech of the soul and a hidden voice. From it the sound of ornaments is called waswas. A man is called mūwaswis (with a kasra on the waw), and it is not pronounced with a fatha, as that is a grammatical error. He is called mūwaswis because his own soul whispers to him. The Exalted said: ﴿And We know what his soul whispers to him, and We are closer to him than the jugular vein.﴾ [Qaf: 16]

The enemy of Allah knew that when they ate from the tree, their private parts would be exposed to them, for it is an act of disobedience, and disobedience tears away the veil that lies between Allah and the servant. When they disobeyed, that veil was torn, and their private parts were revealed to them. Thus disobedience exposes both the inner and outer shame. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) saw in his dream the adulterers and adulteresses naked, their private parts exposed. Likewise, if a man or woman is seen in a dream with exposed private parts, this indicates corruption in their religion. The poet said:

*I see one who has no shame,*
*and no trustworthiness, walking naked among the people.*

Allah, glory be to Him, sent down two garments: an outward garment that covers and conceals the nakedness, and an inward garment of piety, which adorns the servant and conceals him. When this inner garment is removed, the inner nakedness is exposed, just as the outer nakedness is exposed when what covers it is removed.

Then He said: ﴿Your Lord has only forbidden you this tree, lest you become angels﴾ [al-A'raf: 20].

That is: "except out of aversion that you become angels, and aversion that you become immortal in Paradise." From this point he entered upon them, for he knew that they desired immortality therein. This is the greatest door of his guile through which he enters upon the son of Adam. He flows through him like blood, until he reaches the soul and mingles with it, and asks it about what it loves and prefers. When he knows that, he enlists it against the servant and enters upon him through this door. Likewise, the enemy's allies and protégés among mankind, when they wish to achieve their corrupt aims against one another, enter upon them through the door they love and desire, for it is a door that never fails the one who enters through it in his need. Whoever tries to enter through another door finds that door sealed to him, and he is barred from the path to his goal.

The enemy of Allah saw that the two parents were inclined and drawn to remaining forever in that abode, in everlasting bliss. So he knew that he could not enter upon them except through this door. He swore to them by Allah that he was indeed of the sincere advisers to them, and said: "Your Lord has only forbidden you this tree, lest you become angels or become of the immortal."

Abdullah ibn Abbas used to read it as (مَلِكَين) with a kasra on the lam, and said: "They did not aspire to become angels, but they aspired to become kings, so he came to them from the direction of kingship." The evidence for this reading is His saying in another verse: ﴿He said, "O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 120]

As for the well-known reading, it is asked: how could the enemy of Allah lead Adam, peace be upon him, to hope that by eating from the tree he would become one of the angels, when he sees that the angels neither eat nor drink? Adam, peace be upon him, knew Allah, himself, and the angels better than to hope to become one of them by eating, especially from what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, had forbidden him.

The answer: Adam and Eve, peace be upon them, did not hope for that at all. Rather, the enemy of Allah lied to them and deceived them, and tricked them by naming that tree the tree of eternity. This is the first of deception and guile, and from it his followers inherited the practice of naming forbidden matters with names that souls love. They called wine "the mother of joys," and its brother "the comfort of the palate." They called usury "dealing," they called unjust taxes "sovereign rights," they called the most hideous and vile injustice "the law of the chancery," and they called the greatest disbelief, which is denying the attributes of the Lord under the guise of transcendence, and they called gatherings of immorality "gatherings of goodness." When he named it the tree of eternity, he said: "Your Lord has only forbidden you this tree out of aversion that you eat from it and become immortal in Paradise, and do not die and become like the angels who do not die." Adam, peace be upon him, had not yet known that he would die, and he desired eternal life in Paradise. Doubt arose from the enemy's words and his swearing by Allah with all the strength of his oaths that he was sincere toward them. Thus doubt and desire combined, and fate assisted him. When Allah, glory be to Him, had completed His decree, heedlessness overtook them, and the enemy kept watch over them, as it is said:

*They were awake, while Allah willed their heedlessness,*
*so that the decree decreed from eternity might take effect.*

However, this answer is objected to by His saying: ﴿or become of the immortal﴾ [al-A'raf: 20]. It is said: the deceiver who cheats must inevitably include in what he deceives with and schemes of contradiction and falsehood that reveal his deception. We have no need to correct the words of the enemy of Allah or to excuse him. Rather, one excuses the father only regarding how this was accepted by him and entered his hearing. He did not assert to them definitively that if they ate from it they would become angels. Rather, he left the matter between two options: one of them impossible, and the other possible. This is among the most eloquent kinds of guile and deception. For this reason, when he made them hope for the possible matter, he asserted it to him and did not leave it in doubt.

So he said: ﴿O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?﴾ [Ta-Ha: 120]

Here he did not use the particle of doubt as he used it in His saying: ﴿except that you become angels or become of the immortal﴾ [al-A'raf: 20]. So reflect on this. Then He said: ﴿And he swore to them, "Indeed, I am to you of the sincere advisers."﴾ [al-A'raf: 21]

This statement contains several kinds of emphasis:

First: his emphasis by oath.

Second: his emphasis by *inna*.

Third: placing the object before the verb, to indicate exclusivity. That is, "my advice is specifically for you two, and its benefit returns to you, not to anyone else."

Fourth: his use of the active participle, which indicates permanence and constancy, rather than the verb, which indicates renewal. That is, "sincere advice is my attribute and my nature; it is not a passing matter for me."

Fifth: his use of the emphatic *lam* in the answer to the oath.

Sixth: that he portrayed himself to them as one among the sincere advisers, as if he were saying to them: "Those who advise you in this are many, and I am one of them," just as you say to someone you are urging toward something: "Everyone is with me on this, and I am among those who advise you to it."

*He strove toward it until he went beyond its limit,*
*and multiplied, and she doubted, though had he wished he could have lessened it.*

The enemy of Allah bequeathed this guile to his allies and party when they deceive the believers, just as the hypocrites used to say to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when they came to him: ﴿We bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 1]. They emphasized their statement with testimony, with *inna*, and with the emphatic *lam*. Likewise His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿And they swear by Allah that they are indeed of you, but they are not of you﴾ [al-Tawbah: 56].

Then the Exalted said: ﴿So he brought them down by deception﴾ [al-A'raf: 22].

Abu Ubaydah said: "He abandoned them and let them go, from lowering a bucket (tadliyah), which is sending it down into a well."

Al-Azhari mentioned two origins for this word. One of them: "Its origin is a thirsty man who lowers himself into a well to drink water, but finds no water there, so he has lowered himself into it through deception. Thus lowering (tadliyah) was used in place of enticing with what brings no benefit, so one says: *dallahu*, meaning he enticed him." From this is the saying of Abu Jundab al-Hudhali:

*I cut off, and I do not protect, and whoever I protect*
*is not like one who was lowered by deception.*

*Uhussu*: meaning I cut off.

The second: "*fa-dallahuma bi-ghurur*, meaning he emboldened them to eat from the tree. Its origin is *dallalahuma*, from *dalal* and *dalalah*, which is boldness." Shamir said: "One says: *ma dallaka 'alayya*, meaning what emboldened you against me." He recited the line of Qays ibn Zuhayr:

*I think forbearance has emboldened my people against me,*
*and indeed a forbearing man may be treated as ignorant.*

I say: The root meaning of *tadliyah* in the language is sending down and suspending. One says: *dalla al-shay'* into a pit, when he sends it down by suspending it. And *tadalla al-shay'* means it lowered itself. From this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So they sent their water-carrier, and he lowered his bucket﴾ [Yusuf: 19].

The majority of lexicographers say: one says *adlā dalwahu* when he sends it down into the well. And *dallāhā* (lightened) when he draws it out of the well. So *adlā dalwahu, yudlīhi idlā'*, when he sends it down; and *dallāhā, yadlūhā dalwan*, when he draws it up and brings it out. From this is *al-idlā'*, which is seeking access to a man through a kinship tie. In the greater derivation, *al-dalālah* shares this root, which is reaching a thing by making it clear and revealing it. From it is *al-dall*, which is what points to the servant from his actions. 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud used to imitate the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in his guidance, his *dall*, and his bearing. So *al-hady* is the path upon which the servant stands, in his character, words, and deeds; *al-dall* is what shows from his outward state the inner reality; and *al-samt* is his appearance, dignity, and gravity.

The purpose here is to mention the guile and deception of the enemy of Allah against the two parents.

Mutarrif ibn 'Abdullah said: "He said to them, 'I was created before you, and I know more than you. Follow me, and I will guide you,' and he swore to them. The believer is deceived only through Allah."

Qatadah said: "Some of the people of knowledge used to say: whoever deceives us by Allah, we are deceived." So the believer is generous and gullible, while the wicked one is base and treacherous. In the Sahih it is related that Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him, saw a man stealing, and said: "Did you steal?" He said: "No, by Allah, besides whom there is no god." Jesus said: "I believed in Allah, and I disbelieved my eyesight."

Some have interpreted this to mean that when the man swore to him, he considered that he might have taken from his property, and so Jesus took it as theft. This is far-fetched. Rather, Allah, glory be to Him, was in the heart of Jesus, peace be upon him, greater and more magnificent than to be sworn by falsely by anyone. So when the thief swore to him, the matter lay between suspecting him and suspecting his sight, and he attributed the suspicion to his sight, because the man had exerted himself in swearing by Allah. Just as Adam, peace be upon him, believed Iblis's truthfulness when he swore to him by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and said: "I did not think anyone would swear falsely by Allah, the Exalted."

(Section)

As for his guile against the two parents: Allah, glory be to Him, has related to us His story with them, that he never stopped deceiving them, promising them and holding out to them the hope of eternal life in Paradise, until he swore to them by Allah with all his strength that he was sincere toward them, until they were reassured by his words and answered him in what he asked of them. Thus there befell them what befell them of removal from Paradise and the stripping of their garments, and that happened through his guile and deception, by which the pen had run and fate had preceded. Allah, glory be to Him, turned his guile back against him, and He covered the two parents with His mercy and forgiveness, restoring them to Paradise in the best and most beautiful condition, and the consequence of his deception returned upon him.

﴿And evil deception does not encompass anyone except its own people﴾ [Fatir: 43].

(Section)

*I see one who has no shame,*
*and no trustworthiness, walking naked among the people.*

Allah, glory be to Him, sent down two garments: an outward garment that covers and conceals the nakedness, and an inward garment of piety, which adorns the servant and conceals him. When this inner garment is removed, the inner nakedness is exposed, just as the outer nakedness is exposed when what covers it is removed.

The enemy of Allah saw that the two parents were inclined and drawn to remaining forever in that abode, in everlasting bliss. So he knew that he could not enter upon them except through this door. He swore to them by Allah that he was indeed of the sincere advisers to them, and said: "Your Lord has only forbidden you this tree, lest you become angels or become of the immortal."

The answer: Adam and Eve, peace be upon them, did not hope for that at all. Rather, the enemy of Allah lied to them and deceived them, and tricked them by naming that tree the tree of eternity. This is the first of deception and guile, and from it his followers inherited the practice of naming forbidden matters with names that souls love. They called wine "the mother of joys," and its brother "the comfort of the palate." They called usury "dealing," they called unjust taxes "sovereign rights," they called the most hideous and vile injustice "the law of the chancery," and they called the greatest disbelief, which is denying the attributes of the Lord under the guise of transcendence, and they called gatherings of immorality "gatherings of goodness." When he named it the tree of eternity, he said: "Your Lord has only forbidden you this tree out of aversion that you eat from it and become immortal in Paradise, and do not die and become like the angels who do not die." Adam, peace be upon him, had not yet known that he would die, and he desired eternal life in Paradise. Doubt arose from the enemy's words and his swearing by Allah with all the strength of his oaths that he was sincere toward them. Thus doubt and desire combined, and fate assisted him. When Allah, glory be to Him, had completed His decree, heedlessness overtook them, and the enemy kept watch over them, as it is said:

*They were awake, while Allah willed their heedlessness,*
*so that the decree decreed from eternity might take effect.*

However, this answer is objected to by His saying: ﴿or become of the immortal﴾ [al-A'raf: 20]. It is said: the deceiver who cheats must inevitably include in what he deceives with and schemes of contradiction and falsehood that reveal his deception. We have no need to correct the words of the enemy of Allah or to excuse him. Rather, one excuses the father only regarding how this was accepted by him and entered his hearing. He did not assert to them definitively that if they ate from it they would become angels. Rather, he left the matter between two options: one of them impossible, and the other possible. This is among the most eloquent kinds of guile and deception. For this reason, when he made them hope for the possible matter, he asserted it to him and did not leave it in doubt.

So he said: ﴿O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?﴾ [Ta-Ha: 120]

Here he did not use the particle of doubt as he used it in His saying: ﴿except that you become angels or become of the immortal﴾ [al-A'raf: 20]. So reflect on this. Then He said: ﴿And he swore to them, "Indeed, I am to you of the sincere advisers."﴾ [al-A'raf: 21]

This statement contains several kinds of emphasis:

First: his emphasis by oath.

Second: his emphasis by *inna*.

Third: placing the object before the verb, to indicate exclusivity. That is, "my advice is specifically for you two, and its benefit returns to you, not to anyone else."

Fourth: his use of the active participle, which indicates permanence and constancy, rather than the verb, which indicates renewal. That is, "sincere advice is my attribute and my nature; it is not a passing matter for me."

Fifth: his use of the emphatic *lam* in the answer to the oath.

Sixth: that he portrayed himself to them as one among the sincere advisers, as if he were saying to them: "Those who advise you in this are many, and I am one of them," just as you say to someone you are urging toward something: "Everyone is with me on this, and I am among those who advise you to it."

*He strove toward it until he went beyond its limit,*
*and multiplied, and she doubted, though had he wished he could have lessened it.*

The enemy of Allah bequeathed this guile to his allies and party when they deceive the believers, just as the hypocrites used to say to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when they came to him: ﴿We bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 1]. They emphasized their statement with testimony, with *inna*, and with the emphatic *lam*. Likewise His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿And they swear by Allah that they are indeed of you, but they are not of you﴾ [al-Tawbah: 56].

Then the Exalted said: ﴿So he brought them down by deception﴾ [al-A'raf: 22].

Abu Ubaydah said: "He abandoned them and let them go, from lowering a bucket (tadliyah), which is sending it down into a well."

Al-Azhari mentioned two origins for this word. One of them: "Its origin is a thirsty man who lowers himself into a well to drink water, but finds no water there, so he has lowered himself into it through deception. Thus lowering (tadliyah) was used in place of enticing with what brings no benefit, so one says: *dallahu*, meaning he enticed him." From this is the saying of Abu Jundab al-Hudhali:

*I cut off, and I do not protect, and whoever I protect*
*is not like one who was lowered by deception.*

*Uhussu*: meaning I cut off.

The second: "*fa-dallahuma bi-ghurur*, meaning he emboldened them to eat from the tree. Its origin is *dallalahuma*, from *dalal* and *dalalah*, which is boldness." Shamir said: "One says: *ma dallaka 'alayya*, meaning what emboldened you against me." He recited the line of Qays ibn Zuhayr:

*I think forbearance has emboldened my people against me,*
*and indeed a forbearing man may be treated as ignorant.*

I say: The root meaning of *tadliyah* in the language is sending down and suspending. One says: *dalla al-shay'* into a pit, when he sends it down by suspending it. And *tadalla al-shay'* means it lowered itself. From this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So they sent their water-carrier, and he lowered his bucket﴾ [Yusuf: 19].

So *adlā dalwahu, yudlīhi idlā'*, when he sends it down; and *dallāhā, yadlūhā dalwan*, when he draws it up and brings it out. From this is *al-idlā'*, which is seeking access to a man through a kinship tie. In the greater derivation, *al-dalālah* shares this root, which is reaching a thing by making it clear and revealing it. From it is *al-dall*, which is what points to the servant from his actions. 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud used to imitate the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in his guidance, his *dall*, and his bearing. So *al-hady* is the path upon which the servant stands, in his character, words, and deeds; *al-dall* is what shows from his outward state the inner reality; and *al-samt* is his appearance, dignity, and gravity.

Qatadah said: "Some of the people of knowledge used to say: whoever deceives us by Allah, we are deceived." So the believer is generous and gullible, while the wicked one is base and treacherous. We are his descendants, and whoever resembles his father has not been wronged; and whoever's disposition is repentance and seeking forgiveness has been guided to the best of dispositions.

(A subtle point)

Wary of what had already escaped, Adam benefited through the trial. He disobeyed with complete knowledge, and his might did not turn him back from ﴿Prostrate yourselves﴾. Rather, what delivered him was humility: ﴿Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves﴾.

(Subtle point)

Just as He combined the two garments in His saying: ﴿O children of Adam, We have sent down to you clothing to cover your private parts, and as adornment; but the garment of God-consciousness, that is best. That is among the signs of God, that they may remember﴾, He - glorified is He - mentioned the adornment of their outward and their inward, and alerted them through the sensory to the non-sensory. And understanding this degree is beyond understanding the mere wording and its placement in the basic usage of the language. And God is the One sought for help.

So He combined the two adornments: the adornment of the body through clothing, and the adornment of the heart through God-consciousness (taqwa), the adornment of the outward and the inward, and the perfection of the outward and the inward.

(Section)

His saying ﷺ in the hadith: "Indeed God is beautiful and loves beauty."

It encompasses the beauty of garments, which is the subject asked about in this same hadith, and it includes by way of generality beauty in everything, as in the other hadith: "Indeed God is clean and loves cleanliness," and in the Sahih: "Indeed God is good and accepts only what is good," and in the Sunan: "Indeed God loves to see the trace of His blessing upon His servant." And in it, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas al-Jushami, who said: The Prophet saw me and I was wearing worn-out clothes, and he said: "Do you have any wealth?" I said: "Yes." He said: "From what kind of wealth?" I said: "From all that God has given: camels and sheep." He said: "Then let the trace of His blessing and His honor be seen upon you." So He - glorified is He - loves the manifestation of the trace of His blessing upon His servant, for it is among the beauty that He loves, and it is part of thanking Him for His blessings. And it is an inward beauty; so He loves to see upon His servant outward beauty through the blessing and inward beauty through thanking Him for it. And due to His - glorified is He - love of beauty, He sent down upon His servants clothing and adornment that beautify their outward, and God-consciousness that beautifies their inward. So He said: ﴿O children of Adam, We have sent down to you clothing to cover your private parts, and as adornment; but the garment of God-consciousness, that is best﴾.

And He said concerning the people of Paradise: ﴿And He will give them radiance and joy, and reward them for their patience with a garden and silk﴾.

So He made their faces radiant with brightness, their insides joyful, and their bodies clad in silk. He - glorified is He - loves beauty in sayings, actions, clothing and appearance, and dislikes ugliness in sayings, actions, garments and appearance; so He dislikes ugliness and its people, and loves beauty and its people. But two groups have gone astray on this matter. One group said: whatever He created is beautiful, so He loves all that He created, and we love all that He created, so we do not hate any of it. They said: whoever sees created things with their eyes sees them all as beautiful. And their poet recited:

"When you look at existing things with their eyes, all that existence contains is lovely."

They argued with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Who perfected everything He created﴾, His saying: ﴿The handiwork of God who perfected everything﴾, and His saying: ﴿You see in the creation of the Most Merciful no imbalance﴾.

According to them, the knower ('arif) is the one who openly declares the absoluteness of beauty and sees no ugliness in existence. These people have lost zeal for God from their hearts, and hatred for God's sake, and enmity for His sake, and denouncing wrong, and striving in His way, and establishing His limits. They see the beauty of forms, male and female, as part of the beauty God loves, and so they worship through their immorality. Sometimes some of them exaggerate until one claims that his object of worship manifests in that form and dwells in it; and if he is an incarnationist (ittihadi), he says: "It is a manifestation of the Real," and he calls them "aesthetic manifestations."

(Section)

Against them is the second group, who said: God - glorified is He - has condemned the beauty of forms and the perfection of stature and physique. He said concerning the hypocrites: ﴿And when you see them, their bodies impress you﴾, and He said: ﴿How many generations We destroyed before them, who were better in furnishings and appearance﴾.

That is, in wealth and appearances. Al-Hasan said it refers to forms. In Sahih Muslim, from him (the Prophet): "Indeed God does not look at your forms and your wealth, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds." They said: It is known that He did not deny the seeing of perception, but denied the seeing of love. They said: He has forbidden us the wearing of silk and gold, and vessels of gold and silver, and that is among the greatest beauties of this world. And He said: ﴿And do not extend your eyes toward what We have given pairs of them to enjoy, the splendor of the worldly life, to test them therein﴾. And in the hadith: "Simplicity is part of faith." And God has condemned the extravagant, and extravagance occurs in food and drink just as it occurs in clothing.

The resolution of the dispute is to say: beauty in form, clothing and appearance is of three kinds. Some of it is praiseworthy, some of it is blameworthy, and some of it is neither praised nor blamed. The praiseworthy is that which is for God's sake and helps obedience to God, the carrying out of His commands and responding to Him, just as the Prophet adorned himself for delegations; and it is analogous to the dress of weapons for fighting, and the wearing of silk in war, and pride in it, for that is praiseworthy when it includes raising God's word, supporting His religion and enraging His enemy. The blameworthy is that which is for the sake of the world, leadership, boasting, arrogance and a means to desires, or when it becomes the servant's ultimate goal and furthest aim; for many souls have no aspiration other than that. As for what is neither praised nor blamed, it is what is free of these two intentions and stripped of these two qualities.

The point is that this noble hadith contains two great principles: its beginning is knowledge (ma'rifa) and its end is conduct (suluk). So God is known by the beauty that nothing resembles, and He is worshipped by the beauty He loves in sayings, deeds and character. He loves that His servant beautify his tongue with truthfulness, his heart with sincerity, love, repentance and trust in God, his limbs with obedience, and his body by displaying His blessings upon him in his clothing, and purifying himself from impurities, ritual defilement, filth, unwanted hair, and the foul, and through circumcision and trimming the nails. Thus He is known by attributes of beauty, and He makes Himself known through beautiful deeds, words and character; He is known by the beauty that is His attribute, and worshipped by the beauty that is His law and religion. So the hadith combines two foundations: knowledge and conduct.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 7, verse 29:

As for His saying, ﴿As He originated you, so you will return﴾, Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "As He wrote for you, so you will be."

Mujahid said: "As He originated you, so you will return wretched and happy."

He also said: "He will resurrect the Muslim as a Muslim and the disbeliever as a disbeliever."

Abu al-'Aliyah said: "They return to His knowledge concerning them: ﴿A party He guided, and a party upon whom error was justly due﴾ [al-A'raf: 30]."

This includes affirming His knowledge, His pre-eternal decree, and that creation will inevitably return to Him. That this is the intended meaning of the verse is not certain, for the verse implies two rulings:

The first: that He will restore them as He originated them, following the Qur'an's custom of proving the Return (al-ma'ad) from the origination (al-bada'ah).

The second: that He, glory be to Him, guided one party and led another party astray. So the whole matter belongs to Him: their origination and their restoration, and the guidance of whoever among them He guided and the misguidance of whoever among them He misguided. Among their associates there is none who does any of that.

As for the angel being commanded "to write the wretchedness and happiness of the servant in his mother's womb," and the saying "The wretched one is whoever is wretched in his mother's womb," this is a truth that none of the People of the Sunnah disagree with. Indeed, their word and the word of the Companions before them agreed upon it.

As for the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, concerning the boy whom al-Khidr killed: "that he was sealed on the day he was sealed as a disbeliever," it is like that exactly.

And "disbeliever" is a predicative state that is anticipated (hal muqaddarah), not a simultaneous one (muqarinah); that is, he was sealed with his disbelief destined, for otherwise, in the state of being a fetus and a child who does not understand, he has neither disbelief nor belief.

If it is said: "If that is so, why did al-Khidr kill him?" The answer is what he said to Musa: ﴿And I did it not of my own accord﴾ [al-Kahf: 82]. Allah the Exalted commanded him to kill that boy for a purpose, just as He commanded the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to refrain from killing women and children for a purpose. So in everything He commands there is a benefit, wisdom and mercy witnessed by people of understanding.

(Benefit: the wisdom for which the children of Adam will be resurrected uncircumcised)

When Allah, glory be to Him, who is the Truthful in promise and never breaks His promise, promised that He would restore creation as He originated them the first time, it was part of the truth of His promise that He would restore them in the state in which He originated them, with their limbs complete and perfect. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The Day We fold the heaven like the folding of the written scroll; as We originated the first creation, We will repeat it — a promise upon Us; indeed We are ever doing it﴾ [al-Anbiya': 104]. And He said: ﴿As He originated you, so you will return﴾.

Also, circumcision was legislated in this world to complete purity and cleanliness from urine. The people of Paradise do not urinate or defecate, so there is no impurity that would touch the foreskin requiring caution against it, and the foreskin does not prevent the pleasure of intercourse or hinder it. This holds if they continue in the state in which they are resurrected. Otherwise, it does not follow that because they are resurrected thus they must remain in that state, for they will be raised barefoot, naked and uncircumcised, then clothed, and their creation will be extended and increased afterward, as the creation of the people of Paradise and Hell will be increased. Otherwise, at the time of their rising from the graves they will be in the form in which they were in this world, with their characteristics, appearances and conditions, and each servant will be raised upon what he died upon. Then Allah, glory be to Him, will bring them into being as He wills. Whether that foreskin which completed their creation remains in the graves or disappears is possible either way, and it cannot be known except through a report, to which one must turn. And Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, knows best.

(Section)

Ibn Abd al-Barr narrated with his chain of transmission from Musa ibn Ubayda, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi on the words of Allah: ﴿As He originated you, so you will return: a group He guided, and a group upon whom misguidance was decreed.﴾

He said: "Whoever Allah originates His creation upon guidance, He will bring him to guidance even if he acts by the deeds of the people of misguidance. And whoever He originates for misguidance, He will bring him to misguidance even if he acts by the deeds of the people of guidance. Iblis was originated upon misguidance, and he acted by the deeds of the people of happiness among the angels, then Allah returned him to what he was originated upon of misguidance," and so He said: ﴿and he was among the disbelievers.﴾ "And the sorcerers were originated upon guidance and they acted by the deeds of the people of misguidance, then Allah guided them to guidance and happiness, and caused them to die upon it as Muslims."

What is related from Muhammad ibn Ka'b here shows that the state upon which they were originated is what was written, that they would end up in; and that they may act, before that, otherwise. And whoever is originated upon misguidance, i.e., it was written that he would die misguided, may before that be acting by the deeds of the people of guidance. Accordingly, one who is born upon the sound natural disposition (fitrah), which inclines toward guidance, is not prevented from having things come upon it that change it, so that he ends up at what the decree had preceded, as in the authentic hadith:

"Indeed one of you acts by the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is only a cubit between him and it, then the Book precedes him, and he acts by the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters the Fire. And indeed one of you acts by the deeds of the people of the Fire until there is only a cubit between him and it, then the Book precedes him, and he acts by the deeds of the people of Paradise and enters Paradise."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said regarding His words: "As He originated you, so you will return": "As it was written for you, so you will be."

Mujahid said: "As He originated you, so you will return: wretched and happy."

He also said: "The Muslim will be raised as a Muslim, and the disbeliever as a disbeliever." Abu al-Aliya said: "They returned to His knowledge of them: a group He guided, and a group upon whom misguidance was decreed."

I say: this meaning is sound in itself, indicated by the Qur'an, the Sunnah, the reports of the early Muslims (al-athar al-salafiyya), and the consensus of Ahl al-Sunnah. As for whether it is what is intended by the verse, there is room for discussion. What appears from the verse is that its meaning is that of its counterparts and similar verses, in which Allah, glorified is He, argues for the second creation by the first, and for the Return by the Origin. He brings the argument in extremely concise and clear form, saying: ﴿As He originated you, so you will return,﴾ like His words: ﴿O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, then indeed We created you from dust,﴾ and His words: ﴿And he presents to Us an example and forgets his [own] creation,﴾ up to the verse, and His words: ﴿Does man think that he will be left neglected? Was he not a sperm-drop emitted [in ejaculation]? Then he was a clinging clot, and He created [him] and proportioned [him], ... Is not that [Power] capable of bringing the dead to life?﴾ and His words: ﴿So let man look at what he was created from. He was created from a fluid ejected, emerging from between the backbone and the ribs. Indeed, He is Able to return him.﴾

That is, to return man alive after his death. This is the correct understanding of the meaning of the verse. It remains to be said: how does this connect with His words ﴿a group He guided, and a group upon whom misguidance was decreed﴾?

It is said: what compelled those who held that view to interpret the verse as they did is this.

Whoever reflects on the verse will know that the (other) view is more fitting for it. The connection is that the verse includes the foundations of the religion in knowledge, action and belief. So His command to justice (qist), which is the very reality of His law and religion, is in it; and it includes monotheism, for it is the most just of justice, and justice in dealing with creation and justice in worship, which is moderation in the Sunnah. It includes the command to turn to Allah and establish His worship in steadfastness; and it includes sincerity toward Him, which is worshipping Him alone without partner. This is what the verse contains of action. Then He informed of their origin and their return, and this includes the createdness of creation and its restoration; that is faith in the Origin and the Return. Then He informed about the decree (qadar), which is the system of monotheism, saying: ﴿a group He guided, and a group upon whom misguidance was decreed.﴾ So the verse includes faith in the decree, the Law, the Origin, the Return, the command to justice and sincerity. Then He concluded the verse by mentioning the state of the one who did not affirm this report and did not obey this command: that he took the devil as a protector instead of his Lord, and that he is in error while thinking he is guided. And Allah knows best.

If it is asked: what is the difference between His words ﴿So among them are those whom Allah guided, and among them are those upon whom misguidance was decreed﴾ and His words ﴿a group He guided, and a group upon whom misguidance was decreed﴾?

It is answered: the difference is twofold, verbal and semantic. As for the verbal: the words separating the verb from its subject in His words ﴿upon whom misguidance was decreed﴾ are more numerous than in His words ﴿upon whom it was decreed﴾, and it has been mentioned that deletion (of the feminine marker) is better where there are many separators. As for the semantic: the "min" in His words ﴿And among them are those upon whom misguidance was decreed﴾ refers to the nation and the community, which is feminine in form. Do you not see Him saying: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger﴾?

Then He said: ﴿And among them are those upon whom misguidance was decreed,﴾ meaning: among those nations are nations upon whom misguidance was decreed. Had He said instead "dalla" (they went astray), the feminine marker would have been required, though the meaning of the two statements is the same. And when the meaning of the two statements is the same, affirming the feminine marker is better than omitting it, since it is present in what has the same meaning as the other statement.

As for ﴿a group He guided, and a group upon whom misguidance was decreed﴾: "fariq" (group) is masculine, and had He said "fariqan dallu" (a group who went astray) it would have been without the feminine marker. Their saying ﴿upon whom misguidance was decreed﴾ has the same meaning, so it came without the feminine marker. This is a subtle Arabic stylistic feature, in which the Arabs leave aside the grammatically required form of a word when it carries the meaning of a word that does not require that form. You find them saying "huwa ahsan al-fityan wa ajmaluhu" (he is the best of the youths and the most beautiful of them), because it means "huwa ahsan fata wa ajmaluhu" (he is the best youth and the most beautiful).

Its parallel is their correction of "hawl" and "waʿur" (forms) because it means "ahwal" and "aʿwar" (the one-eyed and the squinting). Their parallels are very numerous. If carrying the meaning is good where analogy does not permit it, what do you think of it where both analogy and usage permit it? And better than this is to say that they intended "the best thing and the most beautiful," and they put "al-fityan" (the youths) in place of "shay'" (thing) to indicate that it is the best thing of this kind. Had they confined themselves to mentioning "shay'," it would not indicate the category being preferred over.

From this is his saying ﷺ: "The most tender of them toward a child in its infancy and the most careful of them with regard to what is in her hand" (ﷺ), narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim and Ahmad. This indicates that the implied phrase there is "the best thing and the most beautiful," since it is "the best youth." For had the implied phrase been "the best youth," the parallel here would be "the most tender woman toward a child," and it would be said "the most tender of them and the most careful of them." Since he turned to the masculine, this shows that they intended "the best thing of this kind and the most careful."

(Fa'idah)
The Most High said: ﴿O children of Adam, take your adornment at every place of prayer, and eat and drink, but do not be excessive; indeed, He does not like those who are excessive.﴾ The fundamental rulings of the Sharia have all been gathered in it: it combines command, prohibition, permission, and information.

(Another Fa'idah)
Some of the earlier physicians among the imams of medicine said: Whoever wants the health of the body should reduce his food and drink, and whoever wants the health of the heart should abandon sins.

Thabit ibn Qurrah said: The body's comfort lies in little food, the spirit's comfort in few sins, and the tongue's comfort in little speech.

Sins are to the heart what poisons are to the body: if they do not destroy it, they weaken it, and inevitably so. When its strength is weakened, it cannot resist diseases. The physician of hearts, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, said:

I have seen sins kill the hearts,
and persistence in them brings about humiliation.
Abandoning sins is the life of the hearts,
and disobeying them is better for your soul.

(Lata'if, a subtle point)
Sahl al-Tustari was asked about a man who eats one meal a day. He said: The meal of the truthful ones (al-siddiqin).
He was asked: What about two meals? He said: The meal of the believers.
He was asked: What about three meals? He said: Tell his family to build him a manger.

[Section: The fourth of the corruptors of the heart is food]

Food corrupts the heart in two ways. The first is what corrupts it by its very nature and essence, such as the forbidden things. These are of two kinds: things forbidden for the right of Allah, such as carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, predators with fangs and birds with talons; and things forbidden for the right of people, such as what is stolen, seized by force, or looted, and whatever is taken without the consent of its owner, whether by compulsion or out of shame and sense of obligation.

The second is what corrupts it through its quantity and by exceeding its limit, such as extravagance in what is lawful and excessive fullness. This weighs the heart down from acts of worship and occupies it with the labour and burden of providing for the belly and seeking it, until it attains it. Once it has attained it, it occupies him with managing its disposal, guarding against its harm, and suffering from its heaviness. It strengthens the sources of desire and widens the channels through which Satan runs. For indeed, it flows through the son of Adam as blood flows. Fasting narrows its channels and blocks its paths, while satiety opens them and widens them. Whoever eats much drinks much, sleeps much, and loses much.

In the well-known hadith: "No human fills a vessel worse than his belly. It is enough for the son of Adam to have a few morsels to keep his back upright. If he must do otherwise, then a third for his food, a third for his drink, and a third for his breath."

It is related that Iblis, may Allah curse him, appeared to Yahya ibn Zakariyya, peace be upon them both. Yahya said to him: Have you ever gained anything from me? He said: No, except that food was once set before you at night, and I made it appealing to you until you were full of it, and you slept through your wird. Yahya said: For Allah's sake, I vow never to be full of food ever again. Iblis said: And I, for Allah's sake, vow never to advise a human ever again.

[Section: Adab is the whole of religion]

Covering the private parts is part of adab. Wudu' and ghusl from janabah are part of adab. Purifying oneself from impurity is part of adab, so that one stands before Allah in a state of purity. For this reason, they used to recommend that a man beautify himself for his prayer, for standing before his Lord.

I heard Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, say: Allah commanded a measure beyond covering the private parts in prayer, which is taking adornment. He said, exalted is He: ﴿take your adornment at every place of prayer﴾ [al-A'raf: 31]. He linked the command to taking adornment, not to covering the private parts, indicating that the servant should wear his finest and most beautiful clothing in prayer.

One of the pious predecessors had a robe worth a great sum of money, and he would wear it at the time of prayer, saying: My Lord is more deserving that I beautify myself for Him in my prayer.

It is well known that Allah, glorified and exalted, loves to see the effect of His blessing upon His servant, especially when he stands before Him. The best way to stand before Him is with the clothing and blessings with which He has clothed him, outwardly and inwardly.

And from adab: the Prophet ﷺ forbade the one praying "to raise his gaze to the sky."

I heard Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah sanctify his soul, say: This is from the perfection of the adab of prayer: that the servant stands before his Lord with his head bowed, lowering his gaze to the ground, and not raising his eyes upward.

He said: The Jahmiyyah, since they did not understand this adab nor recognised it, thought that this was evidence that Allah is not above His heavens upon His Throne, as He has told us of Himself, and as His messengers and all the People of the Sunnah agreed.

He said: This is from their ignorance. Rather, this is evidence, for whoever understands from the Messenger ﷺ, against their claim; for among the adab with kings is that one who stands before them lowers his gaze to the ground and does not raise his eyes to them. So what then of the King of kings, glorified is He?

I also heard him say, regarding the Prophet's ﷺ prohibition of reciting the Qur'an in bowing and prostration: The Qur'an is the most noble speech, and it is the speech of Allah. Bowing and prostration are states of humility and lowliness on the part of the servant. So it is from adab toward the speech of Allah that it not be recited in these two states, and that the state of standing and upright posture be more fitting for it.

And from adab toward Allah: one should not face His House nor turn his back to it when relieving oneself, as was established from the Prophet ﷺ in the hadith of Abu Ayyub, Salman, Abu Hurayrah, and others, may Allah be pleased with them. The correct view is that this adab applies to open country and to buildings, as we have mentioned in another place.

And from adab toward Allah in standing before Him in prayer: placing the right hand upon the left during the recitation. In the Muwatta' of Malik, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, it is related that it is from the Sunnah, and people used to be commanded to do so. There is no doubt that it is from the adab of standing before kings and great personages; the Greatest of the great is more deserving of it.

And among them: stillness in prayer, which is the constancy that Allah, the Most High, mentioned when He said: ﴿Those who are constant in their prayer﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 23]. Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak related from Ibn Lahi'ah: Yazid ibn Abi Habib told me that Abu al-Khayr informed him, saying: We asked Uqbah ibn Amir about the words of the Most High: ﴿Those who are constant in their prayer﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 23]. Are they those who pray continually? He said: No, but when one prays, he does not turn to his right nor to his left, nor behind him.

I say: These are two matters: constancy in it (al-dawam 'alayha), and perseverance in it (al-mudawamah 'alayha). The former is constancy (al-dawam); the latter is perseverance (al-mudawamah), as in the words of the Most High: ﴿And those who guard their prayers﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 34]. Constancy has been interpreted as stillness of the limbs and tranquillity.

And from its adab in listening to the recitation: that one listens attentively while present.

And its adab in bowing: that one stands straight, and magnifies Allah, the Most High, until nothing in his heart is greater than Him, and he becomes humble and small in himself, until he is less than dust.

The point is: adab with Allah, blessed and exalted is He, is to uphold His religion and to be disciplined by His manners, outwardly and inwardly.

Adab with Allah is never fully realised for anyone except through three things: knowledge of His names and attributes; knowledge of His religion and law, and of what He loves and what He dislikes; and a soul that is prepared, receptive, soft, and ready to accept the truth in knowledge, action, and state. And Allah is the One sought for help.

[Section: His ﷺ guidance in preserving health]

Since the balance, health, and continuance of the body depend on the moisture that counters heat, moisture is its substance, and heat ripens it, expels its wastes, refines and softens it; were it not so, it would corrupt the body and its existence would be impossible. Likewise, moisture is the nourishment of heat; were it not for moisture, heat would burn the body, dry it out, and corrupt it. Thus the subsistence of each of them depends on the other, and the subsistence of the body depends on both together, and each is the substance of the other.

Heat is the substance of moisture: it preserves it and protects it from corruption and transformation. Moisture is the substance of heat: it feeds it and carries it. Whenever one of them inclines to excess over the other, the temperament of the body becomes deviated accordingly. Heat constantly dissolves moisture, so the body needs what replaces what heat has dissolved, for the sake of its survival, and that is food and drink. If intake exceeds the amount of dissolution, heat becomes too weak to dissolve its wastes, which then turn into bad substances that spread through the body and corrupt it, so various diseases arise according to the variety of these substances and the readiness and receptivity of the organs. All of this is derived from the words of the Most High: ﴿And eat and drink, but do not be excessive﴾ [al-A'raf: 31]. He guided His servants to introduce, in place of what has dissolved, the food and drink that sustains the body, in the quantity and quality that the body benefits from. Whenever this is exceeded, it becomes excess, and both deficiency and excess prevent health and bring on illness: I mean, not eating and drinking, or excess in them.

Thus the entire preservation of health lies in these two divine words. There is no doubt that the body is constantly in dissolution and replacement, and the more dissolution there is, the weaker heat becomes, because its substance is being exhausted, for excessive dissolution destroys moisture, which is the substance of heat. When heat weakens, digestion weakens, and this continues until moisture is exhausted and heat is wholly extinguished, and the servant reaches the term that Allah has decreed for him.

Therefore, the ultimate aim of a person's treatment of himself and others is to guard the body until it reaches this state, not that it requires the continuance of the heat and moisture by which youth, health, and strength endure. This has never been attained by any human in this world. The physician's goal is only to protect moisture from what corrupts it, such as putrefaction and other things, to protect heat from what weakens it, and to balance the two with justice in the regimen by which the human body subsists, just as the heavens and the earth and all creation subsist by justice.

Whoever reflects upon the guidance of the Prophet ﷺ will find it the finest guidance by which health can be preserved, for its preservation depends on the good management of food and drink, clothing and dwelling, air and sleep, wakefulness, movement and rest, sexual relations, and evacuation and retention. When these are in the balanced manner that suits the body, the land, the age, and the habit, health is more likely to endure or to prevail until the term ends.

Since health and well-being are among the greatest blessings of Allah upon His servant, the most abundant of His gifts and most generous of His favours, indeed unconditional well-being is the greatest of blessings in the absolute sense, it is fitting for one who has been granted a share of success to observe, preserve, and protect it from what opposes it. Al-Bukhari related in his Sahih, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Two blessings are neglected by many people: health and free time."

In al-Tirmidhi and others, from the hadith of Ubaydullah ibn Mihsan al-Ansari, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever wakes up healthy in his body, secure in his dwelling, with his food for the day, it is as if the world has been gathered for him."

Also in al-Tirmidhi, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "The first thing a servant will be asked about on the Day of Resurrection concerning blessings is that it will be said to him: Did We not make your body healthy and give you cool water to drink?"

From here, some of the predecessors said, regarding the words of the Most High: ﴿Then on that Day you will surely be questioned about the blessings﴾ [al-Takathur: 8]: "The blessings are health."

In the Musnad of Imam Ahmad: the Prophet ﷺ said to al-Abbas: "O Abbas, O uncle of the Messenger of Allah! Ask Allah for well-being in this world and the Hereafter."

Also in it, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Ask Allah for certainty and well-being, for no one is given anything better after certainty than well-being." Thus he combined the well-being of religion and of the world. The servant's righteousness in both abodes is not complete except through certainty and well-being: certainty repels from him the punishments of the Hereafter, and well-being repels from him the diseases of this world, in his heart and in his body.

In the *Sunan al-Nasa'i*, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Ask Allah for pardon (al-'afw), well-being (al-'afiyah), and continued well-being (al-mu'afah), for no one is given anything better after certainty than continued well-being."

These three requests encompass the removal of past harms through pardon, present harms through well-being, and future harms through continued well-being, for they include persistence and continuance in well-being.

In the *Tirmidhi*, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Nothing has been asked of Allah that is more beloved to Him than well-being."

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla said, from Abu al-Darda': I said, "O Messenger of Allah! That I be given well-being and give thanks is more beloved to me than that I be tried and show patience." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Messenger of Allah loves well-being for you as well."

It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that a Bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said to him: "What should I ask of Allah after the five prayers?" He said: "Ask Allah for well-being." He repeated it to him, and then he said to him the third time: "Ask Allah for well-being in this world and the Hereafter."

This is evidence that these are abominations in themselves, which sound reason does not find good. Thus the prohibition is attached to them because of their foulness. For the establishing of a ruling upon a fitting, derived attribute (al-wasf al-munasib al-mushtaqq) indicates that it is the operative cause (al-'illa al-muqtadiya) for that ruling. This is evidence across all the verses we have mentioned, showing that He prohibited them because they are abominations (fawahish), and prohibited the corrupt thing because it is corrupt, and enjoined the good because it is good. The cause (al-'illa) must be distinct from the effect (al-ma'lul). If the fact that it is an abomination were the very meaning of its being forbidden, and its being corrupt were the very meaning of its being prohibited, then the cause would be identical with the effect, and this is impossible. So reflect upon this. Likewise, the prohibition of sin (al-ithm) and transgression (al-baghy) is evidence that this attribute is established in them prior to the prohibition.

From this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not approach adultery; indeed, it is an abomination and an evil way.﴾ He has given the prohibition in both places the cause of the forbidden thing being an abomination. If the aspect of its being an abomination were the prohibition itself, it would be giving a cause for a thing by itself, and it would be as if one said: "Do not approach adultery, for it tells you not to approach it," or "for it is forbidden." And this is impossible for two reasons.

The first: it entails emptying the speech of benefit.

The second: it is giving the prohibition as a cause for the prohibition!

(Benefit)

The saying "The world is a prison for the believer" has two sound interpretations:

The first: his faith restrains him from what is forbidden, whereas the disbeliever has unrestricted freedom of action.

The second: this is with regard to the outcomes. The believer, even if he is the most blessed of people, is in comparison with his final destiny in Paradise like one in prison. The disbelievers are the opposite: even if they are the most wretched of people, that is in comparison with the Fire, which is their paradise.

[Section: The prohibited things in four degrees]

Allah, glorified is He, has forbidden saying about Him without knowledge in fatwa and judgment, and made it among the greatest of prohibited things; indeed, He placed it at the highest rank among them. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: My Lord has only forbidden the indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is concealed, and sin, and oppression without right, and that you associate with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority, and that you say about Allah what you do not know.﴾ [al-A'raf: 33]

He arranged the prohibited things in four degrees, beginning with the least of them, which are the indecencies (al-fawahish). Then He followed with what is more severely forbidden than that, namely sin (al-ithm) and wrongdoing (al-zulm). Then He made a third with what is greater in prohibition than these two, namely associating partners with Him, glorified is He. Then He made the fourth with what is more severely forbidden than all of that, namely saying about Him without knowledge. This encompasses saying about Him, glorified is He, without knowledge concerning His names, His attributes, His acts, and concerning His religion and His law. The Exalted also said: ﴿And do not say, concerning what your tongues describe falsely, "This is lawful and this is unlawful," to fabricate against Allah falsehood. Indeed, those who fabricate against Allah falsehood will not succeed. [It is] a brief enjoyment, and for them is a painful punishment.﴾ [al-Nahl: 116–117]. So He gave advance warning of the threat for lying about Him in His rulings, and for their saying of what He has not made unlawful, "This is unlawful," and of what He has not made lawful, "This is lawful." This is a clarification from Him, glorified is He, that it is not permissible for the servant to say, "This is lawful and this is unlawful," except with what he knows Allah has made lawful and unlawful.

Some of the early generation (al-salaf) said: Let each of you beware of saying, "Allah has made lawful such-and-such, and has made unlawful such-and-such," for Allah will say to him: "You have lied; I did not make such-and-such lawful, and I did not make such-and-such unlawful." So it is not fitting for one to say, concerning what he does not know of the clear revelation's descent with its permitting or forbidding, that Allah has made it lawful or has mercifully permitted it, merely by imitation (taqlid) or by interpretation (ta'wil).

(Benefit)

Included in His saying: ﴿Say: My Lord has only forbidden the indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is concealed, and sin, and oppression without right, and that you associate with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority, and that you say about Allah what you do not know.﴾

is the prohibition of every indecency, apparent and concealed; and every oppression and transgression against property, life, or honour; and every association with Allah, however subtle, in speech, action, or intention, by making a rival to Allah with another in utterance, purpose, or belief; and every saying about Allah that is not supported by a text from Him or from His Messenger concerning prohibition, permission, obligation, removal, or a report about Him by a name or attribute, whether negation or affirmation, or a report about His act. Thus saying about Him without knowledge is forbidden regarding His acts, His attributes, and His religion.

[Section: Saying about Allah without knowledge]

As for saying about Allah without knowledge, it is the most severely prohibited of these prohibitions and the greatest of them in sin. For this reason it was mentioned in the fourth degree of prohibited things, which all the religions and laws agree upon, and which are never permitted in any circumstance; rather, they are only ever forbidden. They are not like carrion, blood, and the flesh of swine, which are permitted in some circumstances and not others.

Prohibited things are of two kinds: that which is forbidden in its own essence and is never permitted in any circumstance, and that which is forbidden by an incidental prohibition at one time and not another. Allah, the Exalted, said regarding what is forbidden in its essence: ﴿Say: My Lord has only forbidden the indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is concealed﴾ [al-A'raf: 33]. Then He moved from it to what is greater than it, saying: ﴿and sin, and oppression without right﴾ [al-A'raf: 33]. Then He moved from it to what is greater still, saying: ﴿and that you associate with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority﴾ [al-A'raf: 33]. Then He moved from it to what is greater still, saying: ﴿and that you say about Allah what you do not know﴾ [al-A'raf: 33]. This is the greatest of the prohibited things with Allah and the most sinful of them, for it includes lying about Allah, attributing to Him what is unfitting for Him, altering and changing His religion, negating what He has affirmed and affirming what He has negated, establishing what He has invalidated and invalidating what He has established, taking as enemies those He has befriended and befriending those He has opposed, loving what He has hated and hating what He has loved, and describing Him with what is unfitting for Him in His essence, His attributes, His sayings, and His acts.

There is nothing among the categories of prohibited things greater than it with Allah, nor more sinful. It is the root of shirk and disbelief, and upon it heresies (bid'ah) and misguidances are founded. Every misguiding innovation in the religion has as its foundation saying about Allah without knowledge.

For this reason the early generation and the imams fiercely denounced it, cried out against its people from every corner of the earth, warned most strongly against its trial, and exaggerated in this far more than they exaggerated in denouncing indecencies, oppression, and transgression, since the harm of innovations and their demolition of the religion and their contradiction of it is greater. Allah, the Exalted, denounced those who attributed to His religion the lawfulness or unlawfulness of something from themselves, without proof from Allah, saying: ﴿And do not say, concerning what your tongues describe falsely, "This is lawful and this is unlawful," to fabricate against Allah falsehood﴾ [al-Nahl: 116], and so on.
