So how about one who attributes to Allah's attributes, glorified is He and exalted, what He has not described Himself with, or negates from Him what He has described Himself with?

One of the early generation said: Let each of you beware of saying, "Allah has made lawful such-and-such, and Allah has made unlawful such-and-such," for Allah will say: "You have lied; I did not make this lawful, and I did not make this unlawful."

He means the making lawful and unlawful by mere opinion, without proof from Allah and His Messenger.

The root of shirk and disbelief is saying about Allah without knowledge, for the polytheist claims that whoever he takes as an object of worship besides Allah will bring him closer to Allah, intercede for him with Him, and fulfil his need through his mediation, just as intermediaries are with kings. So every polytheist is one who speaks about Allah without knowledge, but not vice versa, since saying about Allah without knowledge may include negation (ta'til) and innovation in the religion of Allah. Thus it is more general than shirk, and shirk is one instance of it.

For this reason, lying about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entails entry into the Fire and taking for oneself a dwelling place in it (mubawwa'), which is the fixed abode that its occupant never leaves, because it includes saying about Allah without knowledge, just like outright lying about Him. For what is attributed to the Messenger is attributed to the One who sent him, and saying about Allah without knowledge is plain fabrication of lies against Him. ﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates against Allah a lie?﴾ [al-An'am: 21].

Thus, the sins of the people of innovation all fall under this category, and repentance from it is not realized except by repenting from innovations.

And how can one repent from them when he does not know that they are innovations, or thinks them to be a sunnah, so he calls to them and urges others toward them? The sins that obligate repentance are not disclosed to such a person except through his deep grounding in the Sunnah, abundant acquaintance with it, constant searching and inquiry into it. You will never see an innovator like that.

Indeed the Sunnah in its very essence erases innovation and cannot stand before it. When the sun of the Sunnah rises in the heart of a servant, it cuts away from his heart the haze of every innovation and removes the darkness of every error, for there is no authority for darkness in the presence of the sun's authority. The servant does not perceive the difference between the Sunnah and innovation, and what helps him to leave its darkness for the light of the Sunnah is nothing but following, and migrating with his heart at all times to Allah, through seeking help, sincerity, true turning to Allah, and migrating to His Messenger, by eagerness to reach his sayings, acts, guidance, and Sunnah. "Whoever's migration was to Allah and His Messenger, his migration is to Allah and His Messenger." Whoever migrates to other than that, it is his portion and share in this world and the Hereafter. And Allah is the One sought for help.

[Section: One does not issue fatwa or judge except with what he knows to be the truth in it]

When a case befalls the judge or the mufti, either he knows the truth in it or it is predominant in his assessment, to the point that he has exhausted his capacity in seeking and knowing it; or not. If he does not know the truth in it and it is not predominant in his assessment, it is not lawful for him to issue fatwa or to judge with what he does not know. Whenever he proceeds to do so, he has exposed himself to Allah's punishment and has entered under His saying: ﴿Say: My Lord has only forbidden the indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is concealed, and sin, and oppression without right, and that you associate with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority, and that you say about Allah what you do not know.﴾ [al-A'raf: 33]. So He made saying about Him without knowledge the greatest of the four prohibited things that are never permitted in any circumstance; for this reason He confined the prohibition to them with the form of restriction.

He also entered under His saying: ﴿And do not follow the steps of Satan. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 168] ﴿He only commands you to evil and immorality and that you say about Allah what you do not know.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 169], and under the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever issues a fatwa without knowledge, its sin is upon the one who gave him the fatwa." And he is one of the three kinds of judges, two-thirds of whom are in the Fire. Even if he knows the truth of the matter with knowledge or a predominant assessment, it is not lawful for him to issue fatwa or to judge other than by it, by the consensus known necessarily from the religion of Islam. He is one of the three judges, the three muftis, and the three witnesses. And if one who issues fatwa, judges, or testifies without knowledge is committing one of the greatest major sins, how about one who issues fatwa, judges, or testifies with what he knows to be contrary to it?

The judge, the mufti, and the witness each reports on the ruling of Allah. The judge reports and executes; the mufti reports without executing; the witness reports on the existential, decreed ruling that corresponds to the legislative, commanded ruling of religion. So whoever among them reports what he knows to be contrary to it is deliberately lying about Allah: ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about Allah with their faces blackened﴾ [al-Zumar: 60]. There is no one more unjust than one who lies about Allah and His religion. And if they report what they do not know, they have lied about Allah in ignorance, even if they happen to be correct inwardly, and they report what Allah did not permit them to report.

They are in a worse state than the slanderer who sees an act of indecency alone and reports it: he is a liar before Allah, even if he reports the reality, for Allah did not permit him to report it except when he is the fourth of four. So if he is a liar before Allah in a report that corresponds to what it reports, when Allah did not permit him to report it, how about one who reports on His ruling with what he does not know Allah has ruled, and whom He has not permitted to report it? Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And do not say, concerning what your tongues describe falsely, "This is lawful and this is unlawful," to fabricate against Allah falsehood. Indeed, those who fabricate against Allah falsehood will not succeed.﴾ [al-Nahl: 116] ﴿[It is] a brief enjoyment, and for them is a painful punishment.﴾ [al-Nahl: 117]. And He said: ﴿So who is more unjust than one who lies about Allah and denies the truth when it has come to him?﴾ [al-Zumar: 32]. Lying about Allah necessitates denying the truth and the sincere. And He said: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates against Allah a lie? Those will be presented before their Lord, and the witnesses will say, "These are the ones who lied about their Lord. Unquestionably, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers."﴾ [Hud: 18].

And these verses, although they concern the polytheists and disbelievers, encompass whoever lies about Allah regarding His monotheism, His religion, His names, His attributes, and His acts. They do not include the mistaken one who is rewarded when he exerts his effort and exhausts his capacity in reaching the ruling and law of Allah, for this is what Allah has obligated upon him. So it does not include one who obeys Allah even if he errs. And success is from Allah.

[Section: The station of jealousy (al-ghayrah)]

Among the stations of "You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help" is the station of jealousy (ghayrah).

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: My Lord has only forbidden the indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is concealed﴾ [al-A'raf: 33].

In the Sahih, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No one is more jealous than Allah, and from His jealousy He has forbidden indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is concealed. No one loves praise more than Allah, and for that reason He praised Himself. No one loves excuse more than Allah, and for that reason He sent the Messengers as bearers of good news and warners."

And in the Sahih also, from the narration of Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah is jealous (yaghar), and the believer is jealous. The jealousy of Allah is that a servant commits what He has forbidden to him."

And in the Sahih also, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do you wonder at the jealousy of Sa'd? I am more jealous than him, and Allah is more jealous than me."

Among the things that fall within jealousy (al-ghayrah) is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And when you recite the Qur'an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a hidden barrier﴾ [al-Isra': 45].

Al-Sarri said to his companions: "Do you know what this barrier is? It is the barrier of jealousy. And no one is more jealous than Allah. Allah the Exalted did not make the disbelievers fit to understand His speech, nor fit to know Him, to affirm His oneness, or to love Him. So He placed between them and His Messenger, His speech and His oneness, a barrier concealed from the eyes, out of jealousy over it, lest it be attained by one who is not worthy of it."

Jealousy is a very noble and great station, of exalted rank. But the later Sufis among them have turned its meaning upside down and taken it in a false direction. They named it "jealousy" and placed it in other than its proper place, and they were deceived in the greatest deception, as you will see.

Jealousy is of two kinds: jealousy of a thing (ghayrah min al-shay') and jealousy for a thing (ghayrah 'ala al-shay').

Jealousy of a thing is the aversion to its competing with you and sharing with you in what you love.

Jealousy for a thing is the intensity of your eagerness for the beloved that another should attain it instead of you, or should share with you in attaining it.

Jealousy is also of two kinds: the servant's jealousy for himself over himself, such as his jealousy from his own self over his heart, over his divided state over his gathered state, over his turning away over his turning toward, and over his blameworthy attributes over his praiseworthy attributes.

This jealousy is the distinguishing quality of the noble, pure, elevated soul. The lowly, contemptible soul has no share in it. The degree of this jealousy is in proportion to the nobility of the soul and the loftiness of its aspiration.

Then jealousy is also of two kinds: the jealousy of the Real (the Exalted) over His servant, and the servant's jealousy for his Lord, not over Him. As for the Lord's jealousy over His servant, it is that He does not make him a servant to creation, but takes him for Himself as a servant. So He does not allow him partners who quarrel (cf. al-Zumar: 29), but singles him out for Himself and withholds him from others. This is the highest of the two jealousies.

The servant's jealousy for his Lord is also of two kinds: jealousy from his own self, and jealousy from others. That from his own self is that he does not assign any of his deeds, words, states, times, or breaths to other than his Lord. That from others is that he becomes angry for His sacred prohibitions when the violators violate them, and for His rights when the negligent neglect them.

As for jealousy "for Allah" (i.e., on behalf of Allah as if He needed defending): it is the greatest ignorance and the most false of falsehoods. Its bearer is among the most ignorant of people, and it may lead its bearer to opposing Him while he is unaware, and to his stepping out of the root of the religion and Islam.

Its bearer may be more harmful to those travelling to Allah than highwaymen. Indeed he is, in reality, a highwayman on the path of the travellers, and he has brought highway robbery in the mould of jealousy. Where is this from jealousy for Allah, which necessitates honouring His rights and purifying one's deeds and states for Allah? The one who knows (al-'arif) is jealous for Allah; the ignorant is jealous "on" Allah. So one should not say, "I am jealous on Allah," but rather, "I am jealous for Allah."

The servant's jealousy from his own self is more important than his jealousy from others. For when you are jealous from your own self, your jealousy for Allah from others is sound. But if you are jealous for Him from others and are not jealous from your own self, then the jealousy is corrupted and flawed, without doubt. So reflect on it and examine it carefully.

Let the discerning traveller ponder these words in this station, where the feet of many travellers have slipped. And Allah is the Guide, the Granter of success, the Steadfast.

As is related from one of the famous Sufis, that he said: "I will not rest until I see no one remembering Allah." He meant jealousy for Him against the people of heedlessness and their remembrance (of other than Him).

And what is strange is that this is counted among his virtues and fine qualities.

The best that can be said of this is that he is excused, because he was overcome in his intellect. Yet it is among the most ugly of the ecstatic utterances (shathahat). The remembrance of Allah while heedless, and in every state, is better than forgetting Him altogether. And the tongues, when they abandon the remembrance of Allah, which is their Beloved, occupy themselves with mentioning what He hates and detests. So what rest is there for the knower in this? Is it not rather harder for him and more hateful to him?

Another saying: "I do not love to see Allah, nor to look at Him." It was said to him: "How so?" He said: "Out of jealousy for Him, from the gaze of one like me."

Look at this ugly jealousy, which indicates the ignorance of its bearer, even though he is under the protection of his own humility, submission, brokenness, and contempt for himself.

[Section: The Act's Indication of Its Own Goodness or Ugliness]

As for the second principle, namely that the Law indicates that the act in itself is good or bad, this is very frequent, such as the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And when they commit an immorality, they say, "We found our fathers doing it, and Allah has commanded us with it." Say, "Indeed, Allah does not command immorality. Do you say about Allah what you do not know?" Say, "My Lord has commanded justice. And set your faces [toward Him] at every place of prostration and invoke Him, sincere to Him in religion. Just as He originated you, you will return." A group He has guided, and a group upon whom error is due. Indeed, they have taken the devils as allies instead of Allah and think that they are guided. O children of Adam, take your adornment at every mosque and eat and drink but do not be excessive. Indeed, He does not like the excessive. Say, "Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He has brought forth for His servants and the good things of provision?" Say, "They are for those who believed in the worldly life, purely [for them] on the Day of Resurrection. Thus do We detail the verses for a people who know." Say, "My Lord has only forbidden immoralities, what is apparent of them and what is concealed, and sin, and oppression without right, and that you associate with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority, and that you say about Allah what you do not know.﴾ [al-A'raf: 28–33]

So He, glory be to Him, informed that their act was an immorality before His prohibition of it, and He commanded its avoidance by taking adornment. The immorality here is their circumambulating the House naked, men and women, other than the Quraysh. Then He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not command immorality﴾ [al-A'raf: 28], meaning He does not command what is an immorality in the intellects and natural dispositions (fitar). Had it been that its being an immorality were known only through the prohibition, and that there is no meaning to its being an immorality except the prohibition's attaching to it, the meaning of the statement would become: "Allah does not command what He forbids," and this is something that even individual intelligent people are protected from speaking, let alone the speech of the Mighty, the Wise. And what benefit is there in saying: "Allah does not command what He forbids"? For in their view the meaning of its being an immorality is only that it is forbidden, not that intellects find it abhorrent.

Then the Exalted said: ﴿Say, "My Lord has commanded justice"﴾ [al-A'raf: 29]. Justice, in their view, is what is commanded, not that it is just in itself. So the true meaning of the statement is: "Say, My Lord has commanded what He has commanded."

Then He said: ﴿Say, "Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He has brought forth for His servants and the good things of provision?"﴾ [al-A'raf: 32]. This indicates that it was good before the prohibition, and that the quality of goodness in it prevents its prohibition, which would contradict wisdom.

Then He said: ﴿Say, "My Lord has only forbidden immoralities, what is apparent of them and what is concealed"﴾ [al-A'raf: 33]. Had their being immoralities been only because the prohibition attached to them, and they were not immoralities before that, the sum of the speech would be: "Say, My Lord has forbidden only what He has forbidden." Likewise the forbidding of sin and oppression. So their being immorality, sin, and oppression is like the being of polytheism as polytheism: it is polytheism in itself, before the prohibition and after it.

Whoever says that immoralities, abominations, and sins became so only after the prohibition is like one who says: polytheism only became polytheism after the prohibition, and it was not polytheism before that.

It is known that this and that are clear obstinacy against intellect and natural disposition. Injustice is injustice in itself, before the prohibition and after it. The ugly is ugly in itself, before the prohibition and after it. Immorality is likewise, and so is polytheism. It is not that these realities became so by the Law.

Yes, the Lawgiver clothed them, by His prohibition of them, with ugliness added to their ugliness. So their ugliness is from their essence, and they increased in ugliness in the intellect through the Lord's prohibition of them, His condemnation of them, and His informing that He hates them and the one who does them. Just as justice, truthfulness, and monotheism, and responding to the blessings of the Benefactor with praise and thanks, are good in themselves, and they increased in goodness above their goodness through the Lord's command to them, His praise of their doer, and His informing that He loves that and the doer of it.

Indeed, among the signs of the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ) is that he commands them with what is good (al-ma'ruf) and forbids them from what is reprehensible (al-munkar), makes lawful for them the good things, and makes unlawful for them the vile things.

So if their being good (ma'ruf), reprehensible (munkar), vile (khabith), and good (tayyib) were only because the command, prohibition, permission, and forbidding attached to them, it would be like saying: he commands them with what he commands them, forbids them from what he forbids them, permits for them what he permits for them, and forbids for them what he forbids for them! And what benefit is in this? And what knowledge of his prophethood would remain in it? The speech of Allah is protected from that, and from it being thought of Him. The praise, commendation, and knowledge indicating his prophethood are rather that what he commands is witnessed by sound intellects as good and as ma'ruf, what he forbids is witnessed as ugly and as munkar, what he makes lawful is witnessed as tayyib, and what he forbids is witnessed as khabith. This is the call of all the Messengers, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them. It is contrary to the call of the tyrannical usurpers, the liars, and the sorcerers, who call to what suits their desires and aims, of every ugliness, reprehensible act, transgression, sin, and injustice.

For this reason it was said to one of the Bedouins who had embraced Islam, when he had come to know his call (ﷺ): "For what did you embrace Islam, and what did you see from him that showed you he was the Messenger of Allah?" He said: "He did not command anything, so intellect said: 'Would that he had forbidden it!' Nor did he forbid anything, so intellect said: 'Would that he had commanded it!' Nor did he make lawful anything, so intellect said: 'Would that he had forbidden it!' Nor did he forbid anything, so intellect said: 'Would that he had permitted it!'" Look at this Bedouin, and the soundness of his intellect and natural disposition, the strength of his faith, and his reasoning for the soundness of the call by the conformity of his command to everything good in intellect. Likewise the conformity of his permission and prohibition. Had the aspect of goodness, ugliness, goodness, and vileness been merely the attachment of command, prohibition, permission, and forbidding to them, this answer would not have been fine from him, and it would have been like saying: "I found him commanding and forbidding, permitting and forbidding." And what proof is there in this?

Likewise is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice and good conduct and giving to relatives, and forbids immorality and bad conduct and oppression﴾ [al-Nahl: 90].

These people claim that injustice toward His servants is what is forbidden and prohibited, and that there is not, in the reality of the matter, an injustice He has forbidden. Likewise, the injustice from which He has exonerated Himself is what is impossible and inconceivable, not that there is a possible, attainable matter which, if He did it, would be injustice. So in the reality of the matter, in their view, there is no injustice that is forbidden or exonerated. Rather it is what is forbidden regarding Him, and what is impossible regarding Him. So the injustice from which He is exonerated, in their view, is the joining of two contradictories, and making one body to be in two places at one time, and the like.

The Qur'an is also explicit in refuting this doctrine. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿His companion said, "Our Lord, I did not make him transgress, but he was in far error." He said, "Do not dispute before Me, and I had already presented to you the warning. The word is not changed before Me, and I am not ever unjust to the servants."﴾ [Qaf: 27–29]. That is, I do not hold a servant accountable without a sin, nor do I withhold from him the reward of the righteous deed he did. For this reason He said before it: ﴿And I had already presented to you the warning﴾ [Qaf: 28], which includes the establishment of proof, the arrival of command and prohibition. And when I take you to account after the presentation, I am not unjust. This is unlike one who holds the servant accountable before presenting to him His command and prohibition. That is the injustice from which Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, is exonerated.

Ibn al-Qayyim, Tafsir al-Qayyim, on Surah 7, verse 33 (part 3 of 3)

And Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer, will not fear injustice or diminution﴾ [Ta-Ha: 112]. That is, nothing will be laid upon him of the sins of what he did not do, nor will anything be diminished from the good deeds of what he did. And if injustice were the impossible thing that cannot exist, there would be no meaning in not fearing it, nor any benefit in being secure from its occurrence.

And Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own self; and whoever does evil, it is against it; and your Lord is not ever unjust to the servants﴾ [Fussilat: 46]. That is, the evildoer does not bear the punishment for what he did not do, and the doer of good is not denied the reward of his deed.

And Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And your Lord would never destroy the towns unjustly while their people are reformers﴾ [Hud: 117]. This indicates that if He destroyed them while they were reformers, He would be unjust. Yet according to those (the Ash'arites), that is permissible, and it would not be injustice were He to do it. They interpret the verse to mean that He, glorified is He, informed that He would not destroy them while they are reformers, and it is known that He does not do that; and the opposite of His report and His knowledge is impossible, and that is the reality of injustice. It is known with certainty that the verse was not intended to mean this, nor was this meant by it, and it cannot bear this in any way, since its meaning would then amount to: "He would not destroy the towns unjustly due to the joining of two contradictories while they are reformers," and the speech of Allah the Exalted is far above and exalted beyond this.

Likewise, according to these same people, futility (ʿabath), purposelessness (sudā), and falsehood (bāṭil) are all impossibilities that cannot fall under what is within power, whereas Allah, glorified is He, has declared Himself free from them, since His enemies, who deny His promise and threat and reject His command and prohibition, attributed them to Him. So He informed that this would entail that creation is futile and false, while His wisdom and might reject that. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Did you then suppose that We created you in vain, and that you would not be returned to Us?﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 115], that is, for no purpose: you are not commanded, nor forbidden, nor rewarded, nor punished. Futility is ugly, and this indicates that the ugliness of this is firmly established in natural disposition (fiṭar) and intellects. For this reason He rebuked them with it, as one who alerts them to return to their intellects and dispositions, and that if they had reflected and seen clearly, they would have known that it is not befitting for Him, nor good from Him, that He create His creation in vain, neither for a command nor a prohibition, nor for reward nor punishment. This shows that the goodness of command, prohibition and recompense is firmly established in intellects and dispositions, and that whoever permits upon Allah the neglect of these has attributed to Him what is not befitting for Him, and what His most beautiful names and highest attributes repudiate.

Likewise, His saying the Exalted: ﴿Does man think he will be left neglected?﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 36]. Al-Shafi'i said: "Left unattended, not commanded and not forbidden." Others said: "Not rewarded and not punished." These two are mutually implicative. He rebuked those who supposed that, which indicates that it is ugly, one that His wisdom and might reject, and that it is not befitting for Him. For this reason He argued that He does not leave him neglected with His saying: ﴿Was he not a sperm-drop emitted [into a womb]? Then he became a clinging clot, and He created [him] and proportioned [him]﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 37], to the end of the surah. And if the ugliness of this were known only through revelation, He would have argued against it by saying that it contradicts revelation and contradicts what He has informed us of and told us; and His denial of it would not be because it is ugly in itself, but because it contradicts what He reported. And it is known that this is not the intended sense of the speech.

Likewise, His glorified denial of the ugliness of associating partners with Him in His divinity, and of worshipping others besides Him, by the parables He has struck for them and the rational proofs He has established against its falsehood. Had its ugliness been known only through the Law, those proofs and parables would have had no meaning.

Yet according to those who deny good and evil by reason (nufāt al-taḥsīn wal-taqbīḥ), it is permissible in the intellect that He command association with Himself and the worship of others! And its ugliness is known only by the mere prohibition against it!

How strange! What benefit remains in those parables, arguments and proofs that indicate its ugliness in the clear intellects and dispositions? And that it is the worst of ugliness and the greatest of injustice? And what could be sound in intellect if it contains no knowledge of the inherent ugliness of shirk, while the knowledge of its ugliness is self-evident and known by the necessity of reason? And that the Messengers alerted the nations to what is in their intellects and dispositions of its ugliness? And that its adherents have no intellects, no understanding, and no hearts? Rather He negated from them hearing and sight, meaning the hearing and sight of the heart; so He informed that they are deaf, dumb and blind, and this describes their hearts as not hearing, not seeing, and not speaking. He likened them to cattle that have no intellects by which to distinguish between good and ugly, and truth and falsehood. For this reason they will acknowledge in the Fire that they were not among the people of hearing and intellect, and that had they returned to their hearing and intellects they would have known the goodness of what the Messengers brought and the ugliness of opposing them.

Allah the Exalted says, relating about them: ﴿And they will say, "Had we been listening or reasoning, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze"﴾ [al-Mulk: 10]. And how often does He say to them in His Book: "Will you not reason?" and "Perhaps you will reason."

Thus He alerts them to what is in their intellects and dispositions of good and ugly, argues against them by it, and informs that He gave them these so that they might benefit by them and distinguish by them between good and ugly, and truth and falsehood.

How much in the Qur'an is there of rational and sensory parables by which He alerts the intellects to the goodness of what He commanded and the ugliness of what He forbade. Had it not been so in itself, there would be no meaning in striking parables for the intellects, and proving it by mere command and prohibition without striking parables and clarifying the aspect of ugliness, which is witnessed by good and intellect.

The Qur'an is full of this for whoever reflects upon it.

(A Subtle Point)

Ibn 'Awn bade farewell to a man and said: "Upon you is the fear of Allah, for the one who is mindful of Allah (al-muttaqi) does not feel loneliness."

Zayd ibn Aslam said: "It used to be said: whoever fears Allah, people will love him, even if they dislike him."

Al-Thawri said to Ibn Abi Dhi'b: "If you fear Allah, people will suffice you; and if you fear people, they will not avail you anything against Allah."

Sulayman ibn Dawud said: "We were given what people were given and what they were not given, and we were taught what people were taught and what they were not taught. Yet we found nothing better than the fear of Allah, in secret and in public, justice in anger and in contentment, and moderation in poverty and in wealth."

In al-Zuhd of Imam Ahmad there is a divine report (athar ilahi):

"No created being who seeks refuge in a created being other than Me will have its means to the heavens and the earth cut off from it. If it asks Me, I will not give to it; if it calls upon Me, I will not respond to it; and if it seeks forgiveness from Me, I will not forgive it. But no created being who seeks refuge in Me, apart from My creation, will have the heavens and the earth guarantee its provision. If it asks Me, I will give it; if it calls upon Me, I will respond to it; and if it seeks forgiveness from Me, I will forgive it."

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 7, verse 37:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Who does greater wrong than one who invents a lie against Allah or denies His signs? Those will receive their portion of the Decree (al-Kitab)⦆

Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid and Ata' said: "That is, what has preceded for them in the Book of wretchedness and happiness." Then Ata' recited: ﴿A group He guided, and a group upon whom misguidance was deserved﴾.

The meaning is that these people are overtaken by what was written for them of wretchedness. This is the saying of Ibn Abbas, in the narration of Ata'. He said: "He means what has preceded concerning them in My knowledge, in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz)."

According to this view, "the Book" is the first Book, and "their portion" is what was written for them of wretchedness and its causes.

Ibn Zayd, al-Qurtubi and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: "What is written for them of provisions and deeds reaches them. When their portion is exhausted and they have completed it, Our messengers come to them to take them in death."

Some scholars preferred this view because of the particle "hatta" (until), which denotes a limit: that is, they enjoy their provisions and their lifespans until death.

Those who support the first view may say that "hatta" in this place is the one that introduces sentences, and the speech turns to a new beginning, as in the line of poetry:

"Wonder of wonders, even Kulayb insults me..."

The correct view is that their portion of the Book encompasses both matters: it is their portion of wretchedness, their portion of the deeds that are its causes, their portion of the lifespans that are the period for earning, and their portion of the provisions by which they were aided in that.

So the verse encompasses this whole portion. Some have mentioned part of it and others have mentioned another part. This is according to the correct view, that what is intended is what has preceded for them in the Mother of the Book.

A group said the Book here means the Qur'an. Al-Zajjaj said: "The meaning of their portion of the Book is what Allah has informed of their recompense, such as His saying: ﴿So I have warned you of a Fire that blazes﴾ and His saying: ﴿He will make him enter a severe punishment﴾."

The proponents of this view said: "This is the apparent meaning, because He mentioned their punishment in the Qur'an in several places, then informed that their portion of it reaches them."

The correct view is the first, namely that their portion is what was written for them to attain before they were created. This view has a good aspect: the portion of the believers from it is mercy and happiness, and the portion of these people from it is punishment and wretchedness. So the portion of each group from it is what they chose for themselves and preferred over other things, just as the share of the believers from it was guidance and mercy, so the share of these people from it is misguidance and loss. Thus their share of this blessing became a curse and a regret for them. Close to this is His saying: ﴿And you make your provision that you deny it﴾, meaning you make your share of this provision by which you live denial of it.

Al-Hasan said: "You make your share and portion of the Qur'an the denial of it." He said: "A servant whose share of the Book of Allah is only denial of it is a loser."

(Section)

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Who does greater wrong than one who invents a lie against Allah or denies His signs﴾ mentions the two types of falsifiers.

The first: the one who originates falsehood and fabrication, sets it up, and calls people to it.

The second: the one who denies the truth.

The first's disbelief is in fabricating and originating falsehood; the second's disbelief is in rejecting the truth.

These two types apply to every falsifier. If to this is added calling others to his falsehood and turning people away from the truth, he deserves multiplied punishment for his disbelief and evil.

For this reason He, exalted, said: ﴿Those who disbelieve and bar from the way of Allah, We will increase their punishment upon punishment because of what they used to corrupt﴾.

So when they disbelieved and barred His servants from His way, He punished them with two punishments: a punishment for their disbelief and a punishment for their barring others from His way. Wherever mere disbelief is mentioned, the punishment is not multiplied, as in His saying: ﴿And the disbelievers, for them is a painful punishment﴾. His saying: ﴿Those will receive their portion of the Book﴾ means that they will receive what was written for them in this world of life, provision and other things. ﴿Until, when Our messengers come to them to take them, they say: Where is that which you used to invoke besides Allah? They say: They have strayed from us﴾, meaning they have departed and vanished, and that invocation has become void. ﴿And they will testify against themselves that they were disbelievers. He will say: Enter among nations that have passed away before you of jinn and men into the Fire﴾, meaning enter into the collective of these nations. Whenever a nation enters, it curses its sister, until when they have all overtaken one another therein, the last of them will say of the first: each later nation speaks of its predecessors: ﴿Our Lord, these misled us, so give them a double punishment of the Fire﴾, doubling it upon them because they misled us and turned us away from obedience to Your messengers. Allah, exalted, says: ﴿For each is double﴾ of followers and leaders according to their misguidance and disbelief. ﴿But you do not know﴾, meaning each group does not know what doubled punishment its sister has. ﴿And the first of them will say to the last: You had no advantage over us, so taste the punishment for what you used to earn﴾, because you came after us, messengers were sent to you, they explained the truth to you, warned you against our misguidance, and forbade you from following and imitating us, yet you refused except to follow and imitate us and abandon the truth that the messengers brought you. What advantage did you have over us, when you went astray as we went astray and abandoned the truth as we abandoned it? You were led astray by us as we were led astray by other peoples. So what advantage did you have over us? ﴿Taste the punishment for what you used to earn﴾.

How glorious is the admonition, and how far-reaching the counsel, if it finds life in hearts! For this verse and its like remind the hearts of those traveling to Allah, whereas the idle have no knowledge of such things.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 7, verse 43:

As for the words of the people of Paradise, ﴿Praise be to God, who guided us to this. We would not have been guided had God not guided us﴾, it is possible that they meant guidance to the path of Paradise, and it is possible that they meant the guidance in this world that led them to the abode of bliss.

If it were said that both meanings are intended, and that they praised God for His guidance to them in this world and for their guidance to the path of Paradise, that would be better and more eloquent.

(Benefit)

The people of Paradise said: ﴿Praise be to God, who guided us to this. We would not have been guided had God not guided us.﴾ They did not mean that some of the guidance comes from Him and some from them. Rather, all guidance is from Him, and had He not guided them, they would not have been guided.

(Section)

Here is a matter that must be pointed out: Paradise is entered only through the mercy of God, Exalted is He, and the servant's deed does not by itself suffice for entry, although it is a cause. For this reason God affirmed entry into it through deeds in His saying: ﴿because of what you used to do﴾, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) negated entry through deeds in his saying:

"None of you will enter Paradise by his deeds."

There is no contradiction between the two matters, for two reasons:

The first: what Sufyan and others reported, that they used to say: "Salvation from the Fire is by the pardon of God, entry into Paradise is by His mercy, and the division of the ranks and degrees is according to deeds." This is supported by the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, which will come, God willing, that when the people of Paradise enter it, they will be settled there according to the excellence of their deeds. Related by al-Tirmidhi.

The second: the "bi" that negates entry is the "bi" of exchange, in which one of the two counterparts corresponds to the other. The "bi" that affirms entry is the "bi" of causation, which indicates that what it governs is a cause for something else, even if it is not independently sufficient to produce it. The Prophet (ﷺ) combined both matters in his saying:

"Be steadfast, strive to be close to the mark, and rejoice, and know that none of you will be saved by his deeds."

They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of God?"

He said: "Not even me, unless God covers me with His mercy."

Whoever knows God and witnesses the station of His right over him, and the station of his own shortcoming and sins, and perceives these two stations with his heart, will know this and be certain of it. And God, Glorified and Exalted, is the One whose help is sought.

[Section: The Qadariyya Negators]

The second category: the Qadariyya negators (Qadariyya, those who deny divine decree), who affirm a kind of wisdom and causation, but do not attribute it to the Lord and do not return it to Him. Rather, they return it merely to the benefit and advantage of the created being.

According to them, acts of worship were prescribed as prices for the reward and bliss that the servants receive, and they are like the payment of a hired worker's wage.

They said: For this reason God calls them a recompense, as in His saying: ﴿And they will be called out: "This is the Paradise you have been made to inherit because of what you used to do."﴾ [al-A'raf: 43] and His saying: ﴿Enter the Garden because of what you used to do﴾ [al-Nahl: 32] and His saying: ﴿Are you recompensed except for what you used to do?﴾ [al-Naml: 90] and the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) related from his Lord, Mighty and Majestic: "O My servants, these are only your deeds, which I count for you, and then I repay you for them." And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Only the patient will be given their reward without reckoning﴾ [al-Zumar: 10].

They said: God, Glorified is He, has named it a recompense, a wage, and a reward, because it returns (yathubu) to the doer from his deed, that is, it comes back to him from it.

They said: Had it not been for its connection to the deed, the naming of it as a recompense, a wage, and a reward would have no meaning.

They said: The weighing also indicates this. Had it not been for the attachment of reward and punishment to deeds, and their being demanded by them, and their being like prices for them, the weighing would have no meaning. God, Exalted is He, has said: ﴿The weighing on that Day is the truth. Those whose scales are heavy, they are the successful. And those whose scales are light, they are the ones who have lost their souls because they wronged Our signs﴾ [al-A'raf: 8-9].

These two groups are opposed to each other in the strongest opposition, and between them lies the greatest divergence.

The Jabriyya (determinists) did not make any connection between deeds and recompense at all. They permitted that God might punish one who spent his life in obedience to Him, and bless one who spent his life in disobedience, and both are equal in relation to Him. They also permitted that He might raise the one of little deed above one who has greater deeds and more and higher degrees. All of this, according to them, returns to pure will, without any cause, reason, or wisdom that requires specifying this one for reward and that one for punishment.

The Qadariyya, on the other hand, made it obligatory upon God to do what is best (ri'ayat al-aslah), and they made all of that depend purely on deeds, as their price. They also held that the arrival of reward to the servant without his deed is a defect, because it involves the burden of a gift given to him without price.

May God fight them! How ignorant they are of God, and how deceived about Him! They made His bounty and kindness toward His servant equivalent to a servant's charity toward another servant, to the point that they said: His giving what He gives as a wage for work is more beloved to the servant and more pleasant to him than that He gives it as a favor without work.

The Jabriyya opposed them with the utmost opposition, and did not make deeds have any influence on recompense at all.

Both groups are unjust and deviate from the straight path upon which God originated His servants, which the messengers brought, and which the books revealed: that deeds are means that lead to reward and punishment, requiring them just as all causes require their effects, and that good deeds are from God's grace, His bounty, His favor, and His charity toward His servant, if He helps him to do them, grants him success in them, creates in him the will to do them and the power over them, makes them beloved to him, adorns them in his heart, and makes their opposites hateful to him. Yet despite this, they are not a price for His recompense and reward, nor are they commensurate with it. Rather, the most that a servant can achieve, when he exerts his sincere effort and striving in them and performs them in the most perfect manner, is that they become thanks to Him for some of the blessings He has bestowed upon him. Had He demanded from him his due, there would remain upon him some portion of thanks for that blessing that he did not fulfill. For this reason, if He punished the people of His heavens and the people of His earth, He would punish them while not being unjust to them. And if He showed them mercy, His mercy would be better for them than their deeds, as has been established from the Prophet (ﷺ). For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) negated entry into Paradise through deeds, as he said: "His deed will not admit any one of you into Paradise." In another wording: "None of you will enter Paradise by his deed." In another wording: "His deed will not save any one of you." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Not even me, unless God covers me with a mercy from Him and grace."

And He, Glorified is He, affirmed entry into Paradise through deeds, as in His saying: ﴿Enter the Garden because of what you used to do﴾ [al-Nahl: 32]. There is no contradiction between them, since the negation and the affirmation do not come on one and the same meaning. What is negated is that entry is merited by deeds alone, and that deeds are a price and exchange for it, a refutation of the Qadariyya.

The Majusiyya (Zoroastrian-like) doctrine, which claimed that bestowing reward as a beginning (ibtida') implies a repetition of the favor (taknir al-minnah), was also refuted.

This sect is among the most ignorant of creation regarding God, and the most veiled from Him. It is fitting that they should be the Magians of this community. It is sufficient to show their ignorance of God that they did not know that the people of His heavens and His earth are within His favor, and that part of the completeness of joy, happiness, delight, and pleasure is their rejoicing in the favor of their Master and true Lord. Their life is pleasant to them only through this favor, and the one most exalted in station with Him and the nearest to Him is the one who knows this favor best, acknowledges it most, mentions it, gives thanks for it, and loves Him for its sake. Does anyone ever move about except within His favor? ﴿They consider it a favor to you that they have embraced Islam. Say: "Do not consider your Islam a favor to me. Rather, God has bestowed a favor upon you that He guided you to faith, if you are truthful."﴾ [al-Hujurat: 17].

Bearing the favor of a created being is only a defect because he is like you. When he bestows a favor, he rises above you, and the one favored sees himself as inferior to him. Yet this is not present in every creature. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) had favor over his community, and his companions used to say: "God and His Messenger are more bountiful." There is no defect in a father's favor toward his child, nor any shame for the child in bearing it. Likewise a master toward his slave. How then about the Lord of the worlds, in whose ocean of favor creation moves, through His pure charity toward them, without any return from them whatsoever? And even if their deeds are causes for what they receive of His generosity and bounty, He is the One who bestows favor upon them, by granting them success in those causes, guiding them to them, helping them to perform them, perfecting them for them, and accepting them from them with their shortcomings. And this is the meaning by which He affirmed entry into Paradise in His saying: ﴿because of what you used to do﴾ [al-A'raf: 43].

So this is the "bi" of causation, a refutation of the Qadariyya and the Jabriyya, who say that there is no connection between deeds and recompense, and that deeds are not causes for it, and that their most that can be said is that they are signs.

They also said: Nor is it consistently regular, because recompense does not follow them in good and evil. So nothing remains but pure divine command and will.

The texts invalidate the view of these people, just as they invalidate the view of those others. Rational and innate arguments also invalidate the view of both parties, and they clarify, for whoever has a heart and intellect, the value of the view of Ahl al-Sunna (the People of the Sunnah), who are the middle sect, affirming the universality of God's will and power, His creation of servants and their deeds, His perfect wisdom which includes linking causes to their effects, and their connection with them legally and by decree, and their ordering upon them in this world and in the next.

Each of the two deviant groups abandoned a kind of truth and committed for its sake a kind of falsehood, indeed many kinds. God guided Ahl al-Sunna to the truth regarding which they differed, by His permission: ﴿God guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾ [al-Baqarah: 213] and ﴿That is the bounty of God, which He gives to whom He wills, and God is the possessor of great bounty﴾ [al-Hadid: 21].

(Tabaqah 12)

A people whose good deeds and bad deeds were equal: their effects cancel each other out, so their equal good deeds prevent them from entering the Fire, and their equal bad deeds prevent them from entering Paradise.

These are the People of al-A'raf (al-A'raf), for none of them has a good deed that earns him his Lord's mercy, nor a bad deed that earns him punishment.

Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has described the people of this category in Surat al-A'raf, after mentioning the entry of the people of the Fire, their cursing one another therein, the address of the followers to their leaders and their replies, and then the calling of the people of Paradise to the people of the Fire. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And between them is a barrier, and upon the A'raf are men who recognize each by his mark. And they call out to the companions of Paradise, "Peace be upon you." They have not entered it, though they aspire [to]. And when their eyes are turned toward the companions of the Fire, they say, "Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people."﴾ [al-A'raf: 46-47]. So His saying ﴿And between them is a barrier﴾ [al-A'raf: 46] means that between the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire there is a barrier. It has been said: it is the wall that is set up between them, having a gate whose inner side contains mercy and whose outer side, facing those beyond it, contains punishment: its inner side, which faces the believers, contains mercy, and its outer side, which faces the disbelievers, contains punishment.

Al-A'raf is the plural of 'urf, which means an elevated place, and it is a high wall between Paradise and the Fire.

It has been said: it is this wall that is set up between them.

It has also been said: it is a mountain between Paradise and the Fire, upon which are the people of al-A'raf.

Hudhayfah and Abdullah ibn 'Abbas said: they are a people whose good deeds and bad deeds were equal; their bad deeds kept them from Paradise, and their good deeds kept them from the Fire, so they stopped there until Allah decides concerning them what He wills, then He admits them to Paradise by the bounty of His mercy.

Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said: Abu Bakr al-Hudhali informed us, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr used to narrate from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: Allah will call people to account on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever's good deeds outweigh his bad deeds by one [deed] enters Paradise, and whoever's bad deeds outweigh his good deeds by one [deed] enters the Fire. Then he recited His saying: ﴿Then as for he whose scales are heavy, those are the successful. And as for he whose scales are light, those are the ones who have lost themselves﴾ [al-A'raf: 8-9]. Then he said: the scale tips with the weight of a mustard seed, either up or down.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And when their eyes are turned toward the companions of the Fire, they say, "Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people."﴾ This is evidence that they are in an elevated place between Paradise and the Fire: when they overlook the people of Paradise, they greet them with peace and hope to enter it, and when they overlook the people of the Fire, they ask Allah not to place them with them. Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And the companions of al-A'raf call out to men whom they recognize by their marks﴾, meaning from among the disbelievers who are in the Fire, and they say to them: ﴿What did your multitude avail you, nor what you used to be arrogant about?﴾ [al-A'raf: 48], meaning: your numbers, your tribe, and your audacity against the people of truth, and your arrogance, did not benefit you. This is either a negation or a rebuking question, and it is more eloquent and more impressive.

Then they look toward Paradise and see the weak ones whom the disbelievers used to despise in the world and whom they claimed Allah would not single out with His favour over them, as He did not single them out in the world. So the people of al-A'raf say to them: ﴿Are these the ones of whom you swore﴾, O polytheists, that Allah would not reach them with mercy? Behold, they are in Paradise, enjoying and delighting, and in its gardens they are made joyful. Then it is said to the people of al-A'raf: ﴿Enter Paradise; no fear shall be upon you, nor shall you grieve﴾ [al-A'raf: 49].

It has also been said: when the people of al-A'raf rebuke the disbelievers and inform them that their multitudes and arrogance did not avail them, the disbelievers rebuke them for their staying behind from Paradise, and swear that Allah will not reach them with mercy, seeing that they are held back from Paradise and that they are heading to the Fire. Then the angels will say to them at that time: ﴿Are these the ones of whom you swore that Allah will not reach them with mercy? Enter Paradise; no fear shall be upon you, nor shall you grieve﴾ [al-A'raf: 49]. Both views are strong and admissible, and Allah knows best.

These classes are the people of Paradise whom the Fire has not touched.

((End of Part Six))

(Section)

The Jahmiyya rejected the clear (muhkam) statements of Him: ﴿Indeed, His is the creation and the command﴾ and His saying ﴿But the word from Me has come into effect﴾ [As-Sajda: 13], and His saying ﴿Say: The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord in truth﴾ [An-Nahl: 102], and His saying: ﴿And Allah spoke to Moses with direct speech﴾ [An-Nisa: 164], and His saying ﴿I have chosen you over the people by My messages and by My speech﴾ [Al-A'raf: 144], and other texts that are clear (muhkam), by means of the ambiguous (mutashabih) of His saying: ﴿Creator of all things﴾ [Al-An'am: 102], and His saying ﴿Indeed, it is the word of a noble messenger﴾ [Al-Haqqa: 40]. These two verses are a proof against them. For the attributes of Allah, majestic is His majesty, are included in the meaning of His name. "Allah" is not a name for an essence that has no hearing, no sight, no life, no speech, and no knowledge; and this is not the Lord of the worlds. His speech, His knowledge, His life, His power, His will, and His mercy are included in the meaning of His name. So He, glorified is He, by His attributes and His speech is the Creator, and everything other than Him is created. As for the attribution of the Qur'an to the Messenger, it is an attribution of mere conveying, not of origination.

Risala (messengership) necessarily entails conveying the speech of the one who sent the messenger. If the sender had no speech for the messenger to convey, the messenger would not be a messenger. This is why more than one of the early scholars (salaf) said: whoever denies that Allah speaks has denied the messengership of His messengers, for the reality of their messengership is conveying the speech of the One who sent them. The Jahmiyya and their brethren rejected those clear texts by means of the ambiguous ones, then made everything ambiguous, then rejected everything. They did not affirm for Allah an act subsisting in Him by which He is an agent, just as they did not affirm for Him a speech subsisting in Him by which He is a speaker. So, according to them, He has no speech and no acts; rather, His speech and His act are, in their view, created and separate from Him, and that cannot be an attribute of Him, because He, glorified is He, is described only by what subsists in Him, not by what does not subsist in Him.

(Benefit)

In the existing world there is no single cause that independently produces an effect. Rather, no cause at all produces an effect except by the joining of another cause to it and the absence of an impediment preventing its influence. This holds for observable causes, and for hidden and abstract causes, such as the influence of the sun on animals and plants, which depends on other causes: the presence of a receptive substrate and other causes that join that cause. Likewise, the existence of a child depends on a number of causes besides the mating of the male. And so with all causes together with their effects. Therefore, every created thing that is feared or hoped for has, at its highest, the status of a partial cause that is not independent in influence, and does not operate independently of its influence depending on something else, except Allah, the One, the Subduer. So it should not be hoped in, nor feared, other than Him. This is a decisive proof that attaching hope and fear to other than Him is invalid. For if it were supposed that such a thing is an independent cause on its own, its causality would be from another and not from itself, since it has no power of its own by which it acts; for there is no power and no strength except through Allah. He is the One in whose hand is all power and all strength. So the power and strength for which a created being is hoped in and feared are in truth only Allah's, and in His hand. How then can one fear or hope in one who has no power and no strength? Rather, fear and hope directed at a created being are among the causes of deprivation and of the descent of what is disliked upon the one who hopes in and fears them. For in proportion to your fear of other than Allah, He will set that over you, and in proportion to your hope in another, deprivation will come. This is the condition of all creation, even if most of them have forgotten it in knowledge and in state. What Allah wills happens, necessarily, and what He does not will does not happen, even if all creation agreed upon it.

(Section)

Reflect on the variation in the movements of the stars and the wonders within it. You will find that some of them move only together with their companions, never separating from them in their course, rather they only move all together; and some move with an absolute motion, not restricted by any companion or associate, but when it happens to be in the same station with another for a night, it agrees with it there, and parts from it the next night. While you see it and its companion and partner, suddenly you see them separated and far apart, as if they had never been companions at all. This wandering body has two very different motions in its course: a general motion by which its orbit carries it, and a particular motion by which it moves in its own orbit. They have likened this to an ant crawling on a millstone turning to the left while the millstone turns to the right. So the ant has two different motions toward two opposite directions: one by its own self, and the other compelled upon it, following the millstone, pulling it in a direction other than its intended direction. By this, every station is made to move toward the east, then its orbit and its station carry it toward the west. So ask the heretics and the deniers of attributes: what nature required this, and what orbit made it necessary? Why were they not all fixed, or all moving, or all of one measure, one shape, one motion, one course? Is this not the work of One whose wisdom dazzles the intellects, and whose created and originated works bear witness that He is the Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner, to whom nothing is like, who made beautiful everything He created and perfected everything He made, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise, who created and proportioned, measured and guided; and that this is one of His signs indicating Him, and wonderful works of His creation that lead thoughts to Him when they travel through them; and that He is a created being that is subjected, ordered, and governed? ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself above the Throne. He covers the night with the day, which pursues it swiftly, and [He created] the sun, the moon, and the stars, subjected by His command. Unquestionably, His is the creation and the command. Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ (54).

If you say: what is the wisdom in some stars being fixed and others moving? It is said: if they were all fixed, the indication and the judgments that arise from their movement among their stations and their course through their zodiacal signs would be void; and if they were all moving, there would be no stations by which their motion is known, and no marks by which it is measured, for the motion of the moving ones is measured by the fixed ones, just as the motion of those walking on the earth is measured by the stations they pass. Had they all been in one state, their order would be confused, and the judgments, benefits, and indications in their variation would be lost; and the denier would cling to this and say: if its doer and originator were choosing, they would not be in one manner, one command, and one measure. Rather, this arrangement and order in which they are is among the strongest proofs of the existence of the Creator, His power, His will, His knowledge, His wisdom, and His oneness.

These two verses contain the etiquette of the two kinds of supplication: supplication of worship (duʿa al-ʿibada) and supplication of request (duʿa al-masʾala).

In the Qur'an, the word "du'a" (supplication) is sometimes used to mean one of these two, sometimes the other, and sometimes both together. The two are inseparable.

Supplication of request is asking for what benefits the one who calls, and asking for the removal or repelling of what harms him. Whoever holds power over harm and benefit is the one truly worthy of worship, and the one worshipped must necessarily possess power over benefit and harm. For this reason God rebukes those who worship besides Him things that possess neither harm nor benefit, and this is frequent in the Qur'an. Such as His saying: ﴿And they worship besides God that which neither harms them nor benefits them﴾, His saying: ﴿And do not call upon, besides God, that which neither benefits you nor harms you﴾, His saying: ﴿Say: Do you worship besides God that which possesses for you neither harm nor benefit, while God is the Hearing, the Knowing?﴾, His saying: ﴿He said: Do you then worship besides God that which can benefit you not at all, nor harm you? Uff to you and to what you worship besides God﴾, His saying: ﴿And recite to them the news of Abraham, when he said to his father and his people: What do you worship? They said: We worship idols and we remain devoted to them. He said: Do they hear you when you call, or do they benefit you or harm you?﴾, His saying: ﴿And they have taken, besides Him, gods that create nothing, while they are themselves created, and they possess for themselves no harm or benefit, and they possess no power over death or life or resurrection﴾, and His saying: ﴿And they worship besides God that which can neither benefit them nor harm them, and the disbeliever is ever a helper against his Lord﴾.

Thus God negated from these deities worshipped besides Him both benefit and harm, whether it be lesser or grave. They possess nothing for themselves nor for their worshippers. This is clearly and abundantly stated in the Qur'an: that the one worshipped must necessarily possess power over benefit and harm, and so he is called upon for the bringing of benefit and the repelling of harm.

There is supplication of request, which is called upon out of fear and hope, and there is supplication of worship. It is known, then, that the two kinds are inseparable: every supplication of worship necessarily implies supplication of request, and every supplication of request contains within it supplication of worship.

On this basis is God's saying: ﴿And when My servants ask you about Me, indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me﴾. It encompasses both kinds of supplication, and the verse has been interpreted in terms of each of them. It has been said: "I give to him when he asks Me." It has been said: "I reward him when he worships Me." The two statements are inseparable.

This is not the use of a term with its two meanings together (the homonym, mushtarak), nor the use of a term in its literal and figurative senses. Rather, it is the use of the term in its single reality which includes both matters together.

Reflect upon this, for it is a point of great benefit, and few perceive it.

Most Qur'anic words that signify two or more meanings belong to this category. An example is His saying: ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night﴾. "Dulūk" (decline) has been interpreted as the zenith (zawāl) and it has been interpreted as the setting (ghurūb), and the two opinions have been reported in the books of tafsir (exegesis). But they are not two opinions; rather the word encompasses both together, for dulūk is inclination. The sun's dulūk is its inclining, and this inclining has a beginning and an end: its beginning is the zenith, and its end is the setting. So the word encompasses both in this respect, not by the inclusion of a homonym for its two meanings, nor by the word's literal and figurative senses.

Similarly, the interpretation of "al-ghāsiq" (the darkness) as night and as the moon, and that this is not a contradiction, but the word encompasses both because they are inseparable, for the moon is the sign of the night. Its parallels are numerous.

Among this is His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿Say: My Lord would not care for you were it not for your supplication﴾.

It has been said: "Were it not for your calling upon Him." And it has been said: "His calling you to His worship," so that the verbal noun is then an annexation to the object. On the first reading it is an annexation to the subject, and this is the more preponderant of the two opinions. On this basis, the intended meaning of the two kinds of supplication and worship is more evident: that is, "My Lord would not care for you were it not that you worship Him," a worship that necessarily entails asking Him. Thus both kinds are included in it.

Among this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And your Lord said: Call upon Me, I will respond to you﴾. So the supplication includes both kinds, and it is more evident in the supplication of worship. For this reason He followed it with His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell, humiliated﴾. The supplication in the verse was interpreted in this sense and in that sense.

Sufyān related from Manṣūr, from Zirr, from Nusayʿ al-Kindī, from al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say upon the pulpit: "Indeed, supplication is worship." Then he recited: ﴿Call upon Me, I will respond to you. Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell, humiliated﴾. Narrated by al-Tirmidhi, who said: it is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ (sound and good) hadith.

As for His saying: ﴿O mankind, a parable has been presented, so listen to it. Indeed, those you call upon besides God will never create a fly, even if they gathered together for it﴾,

and His saying: ﴿They call upon besides Him only females﴾, and His saying: ﴿And lost from them is what they used to call upon before﴾. Every place in which the supplication of the polytheists to their idols and gods is mentioned, what is meant is the supplication of worship, which includes supplication of request. It is more evident in the supplication of worship for three reasons:

The first: they said: ﴿We only worship them so that they may bring us near to God in position﴾, thereby acknowledging that their calling upon them was their worship of them.

The second: God explained this supplication in another place as worship, such as His saying: ﴿And it will be said to them: Where are those you used to worship besides God? Can they help you, or can they help themselves?﴾, and His saying: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are the fuel of Hell﴾, and His saying: ﴿Say: O disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship﴾. This is abundant in the Qur'an. Thus their calling upon their deities is their worship of them.

The third: they used to worship them, seeking nearness to God through them. When needs, distresses, and hardships came upon them, they called upon God alone and abandoned the idols. Nevertheless, they would ask them for some of their needs and request from them, so their calling upon them was both a supplication of worship and a supplication of request.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So call upon God, making the religion sincerely His﴾ is the supplication of worship. The meaning is: worship Him alone and make your worship sincere to Him, do not worship with Him anything else.

As for the saying of Abraham the Friend of God (peace be upon him): ﴿Indeed, my Lord is the Hearer of supplication﴾, the hearing here is special hearing, which is the hearing of answering and acceptance, not general hearing, because He hears everything that is heard.

Since that is the case, the supplication here encompasses both the supplication of praise and the supplication of request. The Lord's hearing of it, blessed and exalted is He, means His rewarding of the praise and His answering of the request. So He hears this and that.

As for the saying of Zakariyya (peace be upon him): ﴿And I have never been unblessed in my supplication to You, my Lord﴾, it has been said: it is a supplication of request, and the meaning is: You have accustomed me to Your answering and Your granting, and You did not make me miserable by refusal and deprivation. So it is a means of seeking nearness to Him, exalted is He, through what preceded of His answering and His goodness, as is related of a man who asked another man and said: "I am the one whom you treated well at such and such a time." He said: "Welcome to one who seeks nearness to us through us," and he fulfilled his need. This is evident here.

It is indicated by the fact that he placed that before his request for a child, and made it a means to his Lord, so he asked Him to continue with him in the custom He had accustomed him to: the fulfilling of his needs and the answering of what he asked.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Call upon God, or call upon the Most Merciful; whichever you call upon, to Him belong the most beautiful names﴾, this is the well-known supplication, and that it is a supplication of request, and it is the occasion of revelation.

They said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) used to call upon his Lord, saying sometimes: O God, and sometimes: O Most Merciful. So the ignorant among the polytheists thought that he was calling upon two gods, so God revealed this verse."

Ibn ʿAbbās said: "The polytheists heard the Prophet (ﷺ) calling in his prostration: O Most Merciful, O Most Compassionate. They said: This one claims that he calls upon one, but he calls upon two, two by two. So God revealed this verse: Say: Call upon God or call upon the Most Merciful."

It has been said: the supplication here means naming, as in their saying: "I named my son Saʿīd," and "Name him ʿAbd Allāh" and similar. The meaning is: name your Lord God, or name Him the Most Merciful. So the supplication here means naming.

This is the saying of al-Zamakhsharī. What led him to this is His saying: ﴿whichever you call upon, to Him belong the most beautiful names﴾, for the meaning of "whichever" (ayyan) and its generality here is only the multiplicity of names. The meaning is: whatever name you name Him by from the names of God, whether God or the Most Merciful, to Him belong the most beautiful names, that is, to the named One, exalted is He, belong the most beautiful names. The pronoun in "to Him" refers to the one named. This is what made him take the supplication in this verse to mean naming.

What he said is one of the implications of the meaning intended by supplication in the verse, but it is not its exact intended meaning. Rather, what is intended by supplication is its familiar and consistent meaning in the Qur'an, namely the supplication of request and the supplication of praise. But it contains the meaning of naming, so the intended meaning is not mere naming devoid of worship and request, but naming occurring within supplication of praise and request.

On this meaning, it is correct that "tadʿū" (you call) carries the sense of "tusammū" (you name).

Reflect upon this. The meaning is: whatever you name Him in your praise, your supplication, and your request. And God knows best.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, we used to call upon Him before. Indeed, He is the Good, the Merciful﴾, this is supplication of worship which includes request, out of desire and out of dread.

The meaning is: indeed we used to devote worship sincerely to Him before. By this they deserved that He protect them from the punishment of the scorching wind, not by mere request, which is shared between the one who is saved and others, for God, glorified is He, is asked by whoever is in the heavens and on earth. Success and salvation come only through sincerity in worship, not through mere request and asking.

Likewise is the saying of the youths, the People of the Cave: ﴿Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth. We will never call upon any god besides Him﴾, meaning: we will never worship other than Him.

Likewise is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do you call upon Baʿl and leave the best of creators?﴾

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it will be said: Call upon your partners. Then they called upon them, but they did not respond to them, and they saw the punishment, [and wished] that they had been guided﴾, this is from the supplication of request. God, mighty and majestic, rebukes them and disgraces them on the Day of Resurrection by showing them that their partners do not respond to their call. It does not mean "worship them."

It is similar to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the Day He will say: Call upon My partners whom you claimed. Then they will call upon them, but they will not respond to them﴾.

This explanation is useful in the matter of the prayer (ṣalāh): whether it has been transferred from its meaning in the language, so that it became a transferred Islamic technical term (ḥaqīqa sharʿiyya manqūla), used for this act of worship figuratively because of the relation between it and its linguistic meaning, or whether it remains on its linguistic usage with the addition of pillars and rulings to it.

According to what we have established, there is no need for any of that. For the worshipper, from the beginning of his prayer to its end, is never free from supplication, either supplication of worship and praise, or supplication of request and asking, and in both states he is a caller. Thus the prayer has not departed from the reality of supplication. Reflect upon this once you understand it.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Call upon your Lord humbly and in secret﴾ encompasses both kinds of supplication, but it is more evident in the supplication of request, which includes the supplication of worship. For this reason He commanded that it be concealed and made secret.

al-Ḥasan (al-Baṣrī) said: "Between the supplication in secret and the supplication openly there is a difference of seventy times."

The Muslims used to strive in supplication, and no voice of theirs was heard, except a whisper between them and their Lord.

That is because God, exalted is He, says: ﴿Call upon your Lord humbly and in secret﴾, and because God mentioned a righteous servant and approved of his action, saying: ﴿When he called upon his Lord with a secret call﴾.

There are several benefits in concealing the supplication.

The first: it is greater in faith, because its doer knows that God hears his hidden supplication. This is unlike one who says: God hears if we raise our voices, but does not hear if we conceal them.

The second: it is greater in courtesy and reverence. For this reason, one does not address kings or make requests with raised voices; rather, voices are lowered before them, and speech is softened before them to the measure of what they hear. Whoever raises his voice before them is despised. And to God belongs the highest likeness.

So if our Lord hears hidden supplication, it is not proper in courtesy before Him except to lower the voice with it.

The third: it is more eloquent in humility and submission, which is the spirit, the core, and the purpose of supplication. The humble, submissive, and lowly one only asks as a poor, abased person asks when his heart is broken, his limbs are humbled, and his voice is subdued, to the extent that his lowliness, poverty, brokenness, and submission nearly reach the point that his tongue is broken and no longer obeys him in speech. His heart is asking, seeking, and pleading, while his tongue, from the intensity of his abasement, submission, and poverty, is silent. This state does not allow raising the voice in supplication at all.

The fourth: it is more eloquent in sincerity.

The fifth: it is more eloquent in gathering the heart upon God in supplication, for raising the voice scatters it and disperses it. The lower the voice, the more it is conducive to his praise and to concentrating his aim and intention upon the One called, glorified and exalted is He.

The sixth, which is among the wonderful secret subtleties, is that it indicates the nearness of its doer to God, and that because of his nearness to Him and the intensity of his presence, he asks Him a request as one asks the nearest thing to him. So he asks with the request of one intimately speaking to one who is near, not with the request of one calling out to one who is far away.

For this reason, God, exalted is He, praised His servant Zakariyya by saying: ﴿When he called upon his Lord with a secret call﴾.
