He sent for a man from the people of Oman called Shurahbil ibn Wada'a, who was from Hamadhan, and no one had been called upon for a matter of such difficulty before him. The Bishop gave Shurahbil the letter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he read it. The Bishop said: "What is your opinion, Abu Maryam?"

Shurahbil said: "You know what Allah promised Abraham concerning the offspring of Ishmael of prophethood. How can we be sure that this is that man? I have no opinion on prophethood. If it were a matter of this world, I would advise you with my opinion and exert myself for you."

The Bishop said: "Step aside and sit," and he stepped aside and sat in a corner. The Bishop then sent for a man from the people of Najran called Abd Allah ibn Shurahbil, who was a young man from Dhu Asbah of Himyar. He had the letter read to him and asked him for his opinion. He gave the same answer as Shurahbil. The Bishop said to him: "Step aside and sit," and he sat in a corner. The Bishop then sent for a man from the people of Najran called Jabbar ibn Fayd, from the Banu al-Harith ibn Ka'b. He had the letter read to him and asked him for his opinion concerning it. He gave the same answer as Shurahbil and Abd Allah, so the Bishop ordered him to step aside to a corner.

When the opinion of all of them had gathered upon that same statement, the Bishop ordered the naqus (a wooden or metal board struck to summon people to worship) to be struck, and the sackcloth garments were raised in the monasteries (sawami', singular sawma'a). This was what they used to do when they were alarmed during the day. If their alarm was at night, the naqus was struck and fires were raised in the monasteries. The people of the valley, both upper and lower, gathered together. Its length was a day's journey for a swift rider, and in it were seventy-three villages and one hundred and twenty thousand fighting men. He read to them the letter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and asked them for their opinion concerning it. The opinion of the men of opinion gathered that they should send Shurahbil ibn Wada'a al-Hamadhani, Abd Allah ibn Shurahbil, and Jabbar ibn Fayd, so that they might come back with news of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

The delegation set out until, when they reached Madina, they took off their travelling clothes and put on their fine garments of striped Yemeni cloth (hibara), trailing them, and wore gold rings. Then they went until they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and greeted him, but he did not return their greeting. They attempted to speak with him for a long time, but he did not speak to them, and they were still wearing those garments and gold rings. So they went off following Uthman ibn Affan and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, who were known to them, for they used to send caravans to Najran in the Jahiliyya, and they would buy from them some of its wheat and dates. They found them in a gathering of men from the Muhajirun and the Ansar, and they said: "O Uthman, and O Abd al-Rahman, your Prophet wrote a letter to us, so we came in response to it. We went to him and greeted him, but he did not return our greeting. We attempted to speak with him for a long time, but he was unable to speak with us. So what is your opinion: should we return to him or go back?"

They said to Ali ibn Abi Talib, who was among the people: "What do you think, O Abu al-Hasan, concerning these people?" Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said to Uthman and Abd al-Rahman, may Allah be pleased with them both: "I think they should take off these garments and rings and put on their travelling clothes, then return to him."

The delegation of Najran did that. They took off their garments and rings, then returned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and greeted him, and he returned their greeting. Then he said: "By the One who sent me with truth as a prophet, they came to me the first time, and Iblis was with them." Then he questioned them and they questioned him, and the discussion continued between him and them until they said to him: "What do you say about Isa? For we would like to know what you say about him." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of Jesus before Allah is like that of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him, "Be," and he was. The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters. Whoever argues with you concerning it after knowledge has come to you, say: "Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, and ourselves and yourselves. Then let us invoke earnestly and place the curse of Allah upon the liars."﴾

They refused to acknowledge this. When the morning came, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), after he had informed them of the matter, went out wrapped in a cloak with al-Hasan and al-Husayn, and Fatima was walking behind him to the mubahala (mutual cursing, the invocation of Allah's curse upon the liars). He had with him at that time a number of his wives. Shurahbil said to his two companions: "O Abd Allah ibn Shurahbil, and O Jabbar ibn Fayd, you know that when the valley, both upper and lower, has gathered, they do not come forward or retreat except by my opinion. By Allah, I see a matter approaching. By Allah, if this man is a true king sent by Allah, and we are the first of the Arabs to challenge him and reject his command, he will not leave from our chest or the chests of our people until he strikes us with a calamity. We are the closest of the Arabs to them in neighbourhood. And if this man is a prophet sent by Allah, and we invoke a curse upon him, not a single hair or nail will remain of us on the face of the earth without perishing."

His two companions said to him: "What is your opinion, O Abu Maryam? For affairs have placed you in a difficult position, so tell us your opinion." He said: "My opinion is that I should make him the arbiter, for I see that this man never judges unjustly at all." They said to him: "It is up to you."

Shurahbil met the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "I have seen something better than cursing you." He said: "And what is that?" Shurahbil said: "I make you the arbiter today until night, and tonight until morning. Whatever you judge concerning us is permissible." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Perhaps there is someone behind you who reproaches you?" Shurahbil said to him: "Ask my two companions." He asked them, and they said: "The valley does not come forward or retreat except by the opinion of Shurahbil."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned and did not curse them. When the next day came, they came to him, and he wrote for them a document of peace and truce. They received their document and went back to Najran.

The Bishop and the notables of Najran met them at a distance of one night's journey from Najran. With the Bishop was his maternal half-brother, who was also his paternal cousin, called Abu Alqama. The delegation handed the letter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to the Bishop. While he was reading it, Abu Alqama was with him, and they were both travelling, when Abu Alqama's she-camel stumbled and he fell, and he was cursed (ta'assa). However, he did not refer to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) by a kunya (a teknonymic). The Bishop then said to him: "By Allah, you have cursed a prophet sent by Allah." Abu Alqama said to him: "Indeed, by Allah, I will not untie its knot until I come to him." He struck the face of his she-camel towards Madina, and the Bishop turned his she-camel back towards him and said to him: "Understand me. I only said this so that it would reach the Arabs on my behalf, out of fear that they would think we had been seized by foolishness, or that we had been persuaded by this man in a way the Arabs have not been persuaded, though we are the most honoured of them and the most numerous in homes." Abu Alqama said to him: "By Allah, I will never accept you again after what has come out of your head." Then he struck his she-camel while saying:

Towards you she runs, restless in her saddle-girth,
Her unborn young thrown across her belly,
Opposing the religion of the Christians, her religion.

He came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and remained with him, and then he was martyred after that.

When this is understood, the knowledge that he (ﷺ) is mentioned in the holy books is known from several aspects:

The first: the report of one whose prophethood is certainly established that he is mentioned among them in their books. He has been informed of this by one for whose truthfulness there is decisive proof, so it is obligatory to affirm him in this, for in such a case to deny him is impossible in itself. This would be so even if it were known only from the bare report of him, so how much more so when the proofs agree on the soundness of what he reported.

The second: he made the report of him one of the greatest proofs of his truthfulness and the attribute of his prophethood. This is impossible to come from anyone except one who is fully confident of it and has certain conviction in it.

The third: those among the rabbis and monks who believers in him, who preferred truth over falsehood, confirmed him in this and bore witness to what he said.

The fourth: those who denied and rejected his prophethood could not deny the good tidings and the report that he is a prophet of great rank, whose description is such and such, whose attributes are such and such, and whose community, place of emergence, origin and affairs are such and such. But they denied that he was the one of whom the good tidings were given, and that there is another prophet besides him. They and the believers among their own people knew that they had mounted the back of obstinacy and bridled the withers of slander.

The fifth: many of them declared to their intimates and inner circle that he was indeed the same one, and that they were determined to oppose him as long as they lived, as has been mentioned previously.

The sixth: the Prophet's (ﷺ) report that he is mentioned in their books is one instance of his reports about what is in their books concerning the affairs of their prophets and their people, what happened to them, the stories of the earlier prophets and their nations, the matter of the origin and the return, and other things reported by the prophets. All of this they know to be true in what he said and in its agreement with what they have. Those reports are too numerous to be counted. They never once denied him in any of them, and they were most eager to catch him in a single lie, error or slip, so that they could proclaim it against him and find a way to turn people away from him. Yet no one among them ever said, at any time, that he reported such and such in our books and it was false in that. Rather, they used to confirm him in that, while they persisted in not following him. This is one of the greatest proofs of his truthfulness in what he reported, even if it were known only from the bare report of him.

The seventh: he reported this to his enemies among the polytheists, who have no book, and he reported it to his enemies among the People of the Book, and he reported it to his followers. If this were false and had no validity, it would have given the polytheists power to ask the People of the Book, who would then deny it, and it would have given the People of the Book power to deny it, and it would have given his followers power to turn back from him and disbelieve him after believing him. This would destroy the purpose intended by his report in every respect. It is like a man who reports something that witnesses to his lie, and makes his report a proof of his truthfulness, and makes his report a confirmation. This does not come from any sane person or any madman.

So by these aspects, the truthfulness of what he reported is known, even if its existence were not known from any source other than his report. How much more so when the existence of what he reported is known.

The eighth: even if it is assumed that they did not know the good tidings of the prophets concerning him, and their description of his attributes, it would not follow that they did not mention him, report about him and proclaim good tidings of his prophethood. For not everything the earlier prophets said reached the later ones, nor did they encompass it in knowledge. This is known by constant experience. How many statements were made by Moses and Jesus, peace be upon them both, of which the Jews and Christians have no knowledge. So when one whose truthfulness is established by decisive proof reports something, their ignorance of it does not require its rejection or denial.

The Ninth: It is possible that there were copies other than these copies that are in their hands, so some of it was removed from some of them, and these were abrogated by what was removed from them. Their claim that the copies of the Torah agree in the East and West of the earth is an obvious lie. This Torah that is in the hands of the Christians differs from the Torah that is in the hands of the Jews, and the one in the hands of the Samaritans differs from this and that. And these copies of the Gospel differ among themselves and contradict one another. So their claim that the copies of the Torah and the Gospel agree in East and West is of the falsehood and lying that they circulate upon the likes of cattle. Even this Torah that is in the hands of the Jews contains addition, distortion and omission that is not hidden from those firmly grounded in knowledge, and they know with certainty that this is not in the Torah that Allah sent down to Moses, peace be upon him. This is like their statements narrating the descent of the Tablets, how Moses, peace be upon him, threw them, and the story of the death of Moses.

The Tablets themselves were the Torah, and the death of Moses occurred only many years after the descent of the Torah.

Among them is the narration that Moses copied what was in the Tablets with his own hand, and it is not in the Gospel that was sent down to Jesus, peace be upon him.

How could there be in the Gospel that was sent down to the Messiah the story of his crucifixion, what happened to him, that he did such-and-such and was crucified on such-and-such a day, that he was crucified, buried, and rose from the grave after three days, and other things that are from the words of the elders of the Christians? At best it could be from the words of the Apostles, which they mixed into the Gospel and called the whole of it a Gospel. For this reason, they have four Gospels that differ from one another.

And from their deceit and lying is their saying that the Torah that is in their hands and in the hands of the Jews and the Samaritans is the same.

The Christians do not acknowledge that the Gospel was sent down from Allah to the Messiah and that it is the speech of Allah. Rather, all their sects agree that it consists of four "Gospels," histories composed by four well-known men at different times, and they know of no Gospel other than this.

A Gospel composed by Matthew, a disciple of the Messiah, seven years after the ascension of the Messiah, and written in Hebrew in the land of Judea in al-Sham.

A Gospel composed by Mark the Harunite, a disciple of Simon, twenty-three years after the ascension of the Messiah, and written in Greek in the city of Antioch in the lands of the Romans. They say that Simon mentioned above composed it, then his name was erased from its beginning and it was attributed to his disciple Mark.

A Gospel composed by Luke the Antiochene physician, a disciple of Simon, after the composition of Mark.

A Gospel composed by John, a disciple of the Messiah, (after his ascension) by some sixty years, written in Greek.

Each of these four they call the Gospel, and between them there is such difference, addition and omission as is known to whoever examines them, and between the Torah of the Samaritans, the Jews and the Christians there is of that what is known to whoever examines them.

So the claim of the lying seeker that the copies of the Torah and the Gospel agree in East and West, near and far, is among the greatest slander and lying. A number of the scholars of Islam have mentioned the differences among them of difference, addition, omission and contradiction, for whoever wishes to examine them. Were it not for prolixity and for the sake of what is more important, we would have mentioned a great deal of it.

Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has rebuked them and reproached them through the tongue of His Messenger for distortion, concealment and hiding. He, exalted, said: ﴿O People of the Scripture, why do you mix up the truth with falsehood and conceal the truth while you know?﴾

And He, exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, those who conceal what We sent down of clear proofs and guidance after We had made it clear for the people in the Scripture — those are cursed by Allah and cursed by the cursers.﴾

And He, exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, those who conceal what Allah has sent down of the Book and exchange it for a small price — they consume into their bellies nothing but fire, and Allah will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, and for them is a painful punishment.﴾ And He, exalted, said: ﴿O People of the Scripture, there has certainly come to you Our Messenger, making clear to you much of what you used to conceal of the Scripture and pardoning much. There has certainly come to you from Allah a light and a clear Book, by which Allah guides whoever follows His pleasure to the ways of peace, and brings them out of darkness into light by His permission, and guides them to a straight path.﴾

As for distortion, Allah, glorified and exalted, has informed of it in several places, and likewise the twisting of the tongue with the Book so that the listener supposes it to be from it when it is not. These are five matters:

The first: mixing truth with falsehood, which is blending it with it such that the truth cannot be distinguished from the falsehood.

The second: concealing the truth.

The third: hiding it, which is close to concealing it.

The fourth: altering words from their places, and this is of two kinds: altering their wording, and altering their meaning.

The fifth: twisting the tongue with it so that the revealed wording is confused for the listener with something else.

These matters they committed only for purposes that prompted them to that. When they opposed the Messenger, denied his prophethood, rejected him and fought him, then they are far more likely to deny his description and attributes, to conceal that, to remove it from its places, and to interpret it other than its true interpretation. And so they did. But because of the abundance and variety of the good tidings, they were overcome in concealing them and their dissemination, so they resorted to distorting the interpretation and removing its meaning from what it is fit for, and applying it to something non-existent which Allah has not created and which has no existence at all.

The Tenth: that he (the Prophet) cited the scholars of the People of the Scripture as evidence for the soundness of his prophethood, and their upright scholars testified for him. Therefore the denial of the lying, obstinate disbelievers does not harm this afterward. Allah, exalted, said: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "You are not a messenger." Say, "Sufficient is Allah as witness between me and you, and whoever has knowledge of the Scripture."﴾

And He, exalted, said: ﴿Say, "Have you considered: if it is from Allah and you disbelieve in it, and a witness from the Children of Israel testifies to its like and believes while you are arrogant? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people."﴾

And He, exalted, said: ﴿And indeed, among the People of the Scripture are those who believe in Allah and what has been revealed to you and what was revealed to them, humbly submissive to Allah, not exchanging the verses of Allah for a small price. Those will have their reward with their Lord. Indeed, Allah is swift in account.﴾

And He, exalted, said: ﴿That is because among them are priests and monks, and because they are not arrogant. And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears from what they have recognized of the truth. They say, "Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses."﴾

And He, exalted, said: ﴿Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it, they believe in it. And when it is recited to them, they say, "We have believed in it; indeed, it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed, we were Muslims before it." Those will be given their reward twice for what they patiently endured, and they repel evil with good, and from what We have provided them they spend.﴾

If one of these testifies, the entire earth of disbelievers will not be weighed against him, and his testimony is not opposed by the denial of the entire earth of disbelievers. How much more so when those who testify for him among the scholars of the People of the Scripture are many times over those among them who deny him?

Not everyone who speaks from among the likes of donkeys, the worshippers of the cross and the nation of wrath, and claims that he is one of their scholars, is so — meaning a scholar — as they claim. And if most of the common Muslims suppose that he is one of their scholars — meaning the People of the Scripture — is it not so that the supposition about others, meaning the scholars of the Muslims, is not the same?

The scholars of the People of the Scripture, if those who do not act on their knowledge are not included among them, then their scholars are none but those who believed in him and affirmed him. And if those who know but do not act, like evil scholars, are included among them, their denial of his prophethood does not harm the testimony of the scholars who speak by their knowledge.

The Eleventh: Suppose there were no mention of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by his description, attribute or sign in the books that are in the hands of the People of the Scripture today. It would not follow from that that he is not mentioned in the books that were in the hands of their predecessors at the time of his mission, and that those books did not reach these people in their original form. Rather, those people altered and substituted and concealed them, conspired together and wrote what they wished, and said, "This is from Allah." Then those books became well known, and their successors transmitted them from their predecessors, so the altered and substituted version became the famous one, while the authentic version became extremely obscure among them. There is no way to know the impossibility of that; rather it is in the highest degree of possibility.

So these Samaritans altered places in the Torah, then the altered copies became famous among all of them, so they know no other, and the authentic copy was entirely abandoned among them. Likewise is the Torah that is in the hands of the Christians.

Thus religions and books are changed. Had Allah, glorified and exalted, not taken upon Himself the preservation of the Qur'an by His own essence, and guaranteed to the community that it would not agree upon error, it would have suffered what befell the books before it. Allah, exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We will be its guardian.﴾

The Twelfth: It is impossible that the earlier books would be devoid of informing about this tremendous matter, a matter greater than which has never reached the world since its creation until the Hour is established, nor is there any greater affair or more significant matter than it. Indeed, knowledge of it has spread over the eastern and western regions of the earth, and it continued through successive generations until Allah inherits the earth and whoever is upon it. Such a great news must necessarily be agreed upon by the messengers in informing of it. And if the Dajjal — a lying man who emerges at the end of time, whose remaining on earth is forty days, and it was said six months — has been agreed upon by the messengers in informing of him, and every prophet warned his people of him from Noah to the Seal of the Prophets and the Seal of the Messengers, may Allah bless them all, how then would the divine books all agree from beginning to end on silence about this great news and this tremendous matter, which has never reached the world, nor will it ever reach it, a matter greater than it? This is something no intelligent person's reason would permit, and the wisdom of the Most Wise of judges rejects it. Rather, the matter is the opposite of that, and Allah, glorified and exalted, did not send any prophet except that He took from him the covenant to believe in Muhammad ﷺ and to affirm him, as He, exalted, said: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of the prophets: "Whatever I have given you of Scripture and wisdom, then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him." He said, "Do you affirm and accept My commitment upon that?" They said, "We affirm it." He said, "Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses."﴾

Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: Allah did not send any prophet except that He took from him the covenant: "If Muhammad ﷺ is sent while you are alive, you must believe in him and support him." And He commanded him to take the covenant from his community: "If Muhammad is sent while they are alive, they must believe in him and pledge allegiance to him."

(Section)

These aspects, on the assumption of the absence of knowledge of his description, attribute and report in the earlier books... and we mention some of what has come in them of good tidings about him, his description, attribute and the attribute of his community, and this appears to you from several aspects:

(1 - Good tidings of the Torah)

The First Aspect:

His saying in the Torah: "I will raise up for the Children of Israel a prophet from among their brothers like you; I will put My word in his mouth, and he will tell them what I command him. Whoever does not accept the word of that prophet who speaks in My name, I will take vengeance upon him and upon his tribe."

The interpretation of the People of the Scripture of this text: This text is one that none of them can deny or reject. However, for the People of the Scripture there are four ways regarding it:

The first: applying it to the Messiah, and this is the way of the Christians, which is an argument against their belief about the Messiah.

As for the Jews, they have three ways regarding it:

The first: by deleting the interrogative particle, the implied reading being, "Shall I raise up for the Children of Israel a prophet from among their brothers?" meaning, "I will not do this." So it is an interrogative of denial from which the interrogative particle has been deleted.

The second point: it is a report and a warning, but what is meant is Samuel the Prophet, for he was from the Children of Israel.
The glad tidings came through a prophet from among their brothers, and the brothers of a people are the sons of their father, and they are the Children of Israel.

The third point: he is a prophet whom God will send at the end of time, through whom He will establish the kingdom of the Jews and elevate their station. They are now awaiting him and call him "the Awaited One" (al-Muntazar).

The Muslims say: The glad tidings are explicit about the Arab, unlettered Prophet Muhammad ibn Abdullah (ﷺ), and cannot be applied to anyone else, because it came through a prophet from the brothers of the Children of Israel, not from the Children of Israel themselves. The Messiah is from the Children of Israel. Had the intended one been the Messiah, the verse would have said: "I will raise up for them a prophet from among themselves."

As God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed God conferred a favour upon the believers when He sent among them a messenger from themselves﴾ (Aal Imran 3:164). The brothers of the Children of Israel are the sons of Ishmael. In no language of any nation is it said that the Children of Israel are the brothers of the Children of Israel, just as the brothers of Zayd do not include Zayd himself.

Also, He said: "a prophet like you" (Deuteronomy 18:18). This indicates that he is a bearer of a universal law like Moses. This nullifies applying it to Samuel for these reasons too, and it nullifies applying it to Joshua for three reasons:
First: he is from the Children of Israel, not from their brothers.
Second: he was not like Moses. In the Torah in their hands: "There shall not arise in Israel a prophet like Moses."
Third: Joshua was a prophet in the time of Moses, namely Caleb, whereas this promise concerns a prophet whom God raises after Moses.

By these three points it is also nullified that it refers to Aaron, since Aaron died before Moses, and God made him a prophet alongside Moses during Moses' lifetime. It is also nullified by a fourth point: the glad tidings state that a book will be sent down to him which will appear to the people from his mouth. This was not granted to anyone after Moses except the Prophet (ﷺ), and this is among the signs of his prophethood that the earlier prophets foretold. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿And indeed it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. The trustworthy Spirit has brought it down upon your heart, that you may be one of the warners, in a clear Arabic tongue. And indeed it is in the Scriptures of the former peoples. Is it not a sign for them that the scholars of the Children of Israel know it?﴾ (ash-Shu'ara 26:192–197).

The Qur'an was sent down upon the heart of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and appeared to the community from his mouth. This glad tiding cannot be applied to the Messiah by the agreement of the Christians, because it came through one of the brothers of the Children of Israel, and the Children of Israel and their brothers are all servants of God, and among them there is no god. Yet the Messiah, in their view, is a worshipped god, and he is too exalted in their eyes to be one of the brothers of the servant Children of Israel. The glad tiding came through a created servant whom God raises up from among His servants and their brothers, and its ultimate reach is that he be a prophet, with no station beyond it. This is not the Messiah according to the Christians.

As for their claim that it is an elision of the interrogative alif, and the meaning is "Shall I raise up for the Children of Israel a prophet like you?", denying it: this is a well-known habit of theirs in distorting the words of God from their places and lying about God, and their saying about what they alter and distort: "This is from God."

Interpreting this statement as an interrogative denial is the utmost of distortion and alteration.

This distortion and alteration is among the miracles of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), which he foretold from God concerning their distortion and alteration. God thus manifested his truthfulness in all of this to every person of understanding and intellect, so that he increased in faith upon his faith, and the disbelievers increased in filth upon their filth.

In the Torah, in the Fifth Book, it says: "God came from Sinai, and shone forth from Seir, and appeared from the mountains of Paran, and with Him were ten thousands of the holy ones at His right hand." This contains the three prophethoods: the prophethood of Moses, the prophethood of Jesus, and the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ).

His coming from Sinai, which is the mountain upon which God spoke to Moses and informed him, is a report about his prophethood.
His shining forth from Seir is the manifestation of Jesus the Messiah from Jerusalem. Seir is a well-known village there to this day. This is a glad tiding of the prophethood of the Messiah.
Paran is Mecca. God, glorified and exalted, compared the prophethood of Moses to the coming and breaking of the dawn, the prophethood of the Messiah after it to its brightness and light, and the prophethood of the Seal of the Prophets after both of them (ﷺ) to the sun's rising and the appearance of its light across the horizons. The matter came to pass exactly as foretold: God split the darkness of disbelief with the prophethood of Moses and lit its dawn with his prophethood; the light and brightness increased with the prophethood of the Messiah; and the light was completed, manifested and covered the earth with the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ).

The mention of these three prophethoods contained in this glad tiding is like their mention at the beginning of Surah at-Tin: ﴿By the fig and the olive, and Mount Sinai, and this secure city﴾ (at-Tin 95:1–3).

So He mentions the places of these prophets and the lands from which they came. "The fig and the olive": what is meant is their place of growth and their land, which is the Holy Land, the manifestation of the Messiah. "Mount Sinai" is the mountain upon which God spoke to Moses, and it is the manifestation of his prophethood. "This secure city" is Mecca, the sanctuary and security of God, the manifestation of the prophethood of Muhammad, may the prayers and peace of God be upon him and upon them all.

These three are thus the exact counterpart of those three.

The Jews said: Paran is the land of al-Sham and not the land of the Hijaz. This is no novelty from their slander and distortion. In their Torah it is said that Ishmael, when he separated from his father, settled in the wilderness of Paran. Thus the Torah speaks, and its wording is: "And Ishmael dwelt in the wilderness of Paran, and his mother took for him a wife from the land of Egypt."

The scholars of the People of the Book do not doubt that Paran is the dwelling of the family of Ishmael. The Torah contains a prophethood that descends in the land of Paran, and contains a prophethood descending upon a great one of the offspring of Ishmael, and contains the spread of his community and followers until they fill the plain and the mountain, as we shall mention, God willing.

After this there remains no doubt at all that this is the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), which descended in Paran upon the most noble of the offspring of Ishmael, until he filled the earth with radiance and light, and his followers filled the plain and the mountain. It is not unlikely that the people whom the Torah describes as lacking judgment and understanding should divide into one ignorant of this, and one who denies it out of arrogance and obstinacy.

The wording of the Torah about them is: they are a people lacking judgment, and there is no understanding in them.

It may be said to these arrogant deniers: what prophethood came out of al-Sham and became manifest like the brightness of the sun, and appeared above the appearance of the two prophethoods before it? Is this not like the case of one who sees the sun rising from the east, yet argues and denies, saying: "No, it rose from the west"?

In the Torah, in the First Book, it says: "The angel appeared to Hagar, the mother of Ishmael, and said: O Hagar, where have you come from, and where are you going? When she explained her situation to him, he said: Return, for I will greatly multiply your descendants and your seed until they cannot be counted for multitude. Behold, you shall conceive and bear a son whose name is Ishmael, because God has heard your humility and submission. Your son will be a wild man; his hand will be over all, and the hand of all will be stretched out to him in submission."

This is a glad tiding containing that the hand of her son is above the hand of every creature, that his word is supreme, that the hand of her son is high, and that the hand of creation is beneath his hand. Who, then, is the one to whom this description applies other than Muhammad ibn Abdullah, may the prayers and peace of God be upon him?

His statement concerning the prophethood of Armiya (Jeremiah): "Before I formed you, I sanctified you. Before you came out of the womb, I made you holy, and I appointed you a prophet to all the nations." This is a glad tiding conveyed through Armiya for one who would come after him, and it refers either to the Messiah (al-Masih) or to Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them both. It cannot refer to anyone else. Muhammad is more fitting for it, because the Messiah was sent only to the Children of Israel, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿and a messenger to the Children of Israel﴾.

The Christians acknowledge this. The Messiah did not claim to be a messenger to all the peoples of the earth, since the prophets from the time of Musa (Moses) until the Messiah were sent only to their own people. Indeed, the Christians have in the Injil (Gospel) that the Messiah said to the two disciples (al-Hawariyyan): "Do not go on the path of the nations, but confine yourselves to the lost sheep of the house of Israel."

As for Muhammad ibn Abdullah, he is the one whom Allah sent to all the nations of the earth and to all the groups of the children of Adam.

This glad tiding corresponds to the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿O mankind, indeed I am the messenger of Allah to you all﴾.

It also corresponds to the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "I have been sent to the black and the red."

And his saying: "The prophet used to be sent to his own people, but I have been sent to all mankind."

The Christians have acknowledged this glad tiding and did not deny it. However, some of their leaders said that it is the glad tiding of Musa ibn Imran, Ilyas (Elijah) and al-Yasa (Elisha), and that they will come at the end of time. This is one of the greatest forms of slander, audacity against Allah the Exalted, and fabrication against Him, for one who has died will not return until the appointed day of the Resurrection.

**Section: The Harm That Sins Do to the Heart Is Like the Harm of Poisons to the Body**

Among what should be known is that sins and acts of disobedience do harm, and their harm to the heart is, without doubt, like the harm of poisons to the body, though they differ in degrees of harm. Is there any evil or disease in this world or the next whose cause is not sins and acts of disobedience? What expelled the two parents (Adam and Eve) from Paradise, the abode of delight, bliss, joy and happiness, to the abode of pains, sorrows and calamities?

And what expelled Iblis (Satan) from the kingdom of the heavens, and banished him and cursed him, and disfigured his outward and inward being, so that his form became the ugliest and most hideous of forms, and his inner being more ugly and hideous than his form? He was exchanged nearness for distance, mercy for curse, beauty for ugliness, Paradise for a blazing fire, faith for disbelief, and allegiance to the Praiseworthy Protector for the greatest enmity and hostility; and the chanting of glorification, sanctification and declaration of God's oneness was exchanged for the chanting of disbelief, polytheism, lying, falsehood and obscenity; and the garment of faith was exchanged for the garment of disbelief, wickedness and disobedience. So he became utterly despised before God, fell from His sight to the utmost degree of fall, and the wrath of the Lord, exalted is He, descended upon him, so that He cast him down, and His greatest hatred seized him so that He destroyed him. Thus he became a procurer for every sinner and criminal, content for himself to be a leader after that worship and lordship. So we seek refuge in You, O God, from opposing Your command and committing what You have forbidden.

And what drowned all the people of the earth, until the water rose above the tops of the mountains? And what sent the barren wind upon the people of ʿAd, until it cast them dead upon the face of the earth as though they were trunks of hollow palm trees, and destroyed whatever passed over them of their dwellings, their tilled lands, their crops and their livestock, until they became a lesson for the nations until the Day of Resurrection?

And what sent the Cry upon the people of Thamud, until it severed their hearts within their bodies and they all died to the last one?

And what raised up the towns of the people of Lot until the angels heard the barking of their dogs, then overturned them upon them, making their highest part their lowest, and destroyed them all? Then He followed them with stones from the sky which He rained down upon them, gathering upon them a punishment that He had not gathered upon any other nation. "And for their brethren there are similar things, and they are not far from the wrongdoers" (cf. Qur'an 11:83).

And what sent upon the people of Shuʿayb clouds of punishment like canopies, and when it came above their heads, it rained down upon them fire blazing fiercely?

And what drowned Pharaoh and his people in the sea, then their spirits were transferred to Hell? So the bodies were for drowning, and the spirits for burning.

And what caused Qarun to be swallowed up, with his house, his wealth and his family?

And what destroyed the generations after Noah with various kinds of punishments, and annihilated them with complete annihilation?

And what destroyed the people of the companion of Yaseen with the Cry, until they became silent, all of them to the last one?

And what sent against the Children of Israel a people of severe might, who roamed through the homes, killed the men, took captive the offspring and the women, burned the dwellings and plundered the wealth; then He sent them against them a second time, and they destroyed whatever they could and utterly ruined whatever they dominated?

And what subjected them to various kinds of punishments: at one time by killing, captivity and the ruin of lands; at another by the injustice of kings; and at another by being transformed into apes and swine? And at the last of that, the Lord, blessed and exalted, swore: "He will surely send against them until the Day of Resurrection those who will afflict them with a terrible punishment" (Qur'an 7:167).

Imam Ahmad said: Al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, from Safwan ibn ʿUmar, and ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr narrated to me, from his father, who said: When Cyprus was conquered, its people were separated, and some of them wept over others. I saw Abu al-Darda' sitting alone weeping, so I said: "O Abu al-Darda', what makes you weep on a day when God has honoured Islam and its people?" He said: "Woe to you, O Jubayr! How insignificant are creatures before God, the Mighty and Majestic, when they neglect His command! While they were a dominant nation, prevailing and possessing kingship, they abandoned the command of God, and so they came to what you see."

ʿAli ibn al-Jaʿd said: Shuʿbah informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, who said: I heard Abu al-Bakhtari say: "Someone who heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say informed me: 'The people will not perish until they make excuses for themselves.'"

In the Musnad of Ahmad, from the hadith of Umm Salamah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "When sins become apparent among my nation, God will envelop them all with a punishment from Him." I said: "O Messenger of God, will there not be among them on that day righteous people?" He said: "Yes." I said: "How will those be treated?" He said: "They will be afflicted with what afflicts the people, then they will proceed to forgiveness from God and good pleasure."

In the mursal narrations of al-Hasan, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "This nation will remain under the hand of God and in His protection so long as its reciters do not conspire with its rulers, and so long as its righteous do not praise its wicked, and so long as its best are not humiliated by its worst. When they do that, God will withdraw His hand from them, then their tyrants will be given power over them, who will subject them to a terrible punishment; then God will strike them with poverty and need."

In the Musnad, from the hadith of Thawban, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "A man is deprived of provision because of a sin that he commits."

Also in it, from him, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Soon the nations will summon one another against you from every horizon, as diners gather around their dish." We said: "O Messenger of God, will that be because of our small numbers on that day?" He said: "No, you will be many on that day, but you will be like scum, like the scum of a torrent. The awe of you will be removed from the hearts of your enemies, and weakness (wahn) will be placed in your hearts." They said: "What is wahn?" He said: "Love of this life and dislike of death."

In the Musnad, from the hadith of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "When I was taken up on the Night Journey, I passed by a people who had nails of copper with which they scratched their faces and chests. I said: 'Who are these, O Jibril?' He said: 'These are those who eat the flesh of people and slander their honour.'"

In the Jami' of al-Tirmidhi, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "At the end of time there will come a people who use religion to gain worldly things, and who wear for people the wool of sheep as a garment of gentleness. Their tongues are sweeter than sugar, but their hearts are the hearts of wolves. God, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Is it Me they are deceived by? Is it against Me that they are bold? By Myself I swear, I will surely send against them a trial that will leave the forbearing among them bewildered.'"

Ibn Abi al-Dunya mentioned, from the hadith of Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: ʿAli said: "There will come upon people a time when nothing of Islam will remain but its name, and nothing of the Qur'an but its outline. Their mosques on that day will be full, yet they will be ruins of guidance. Their scholars will be the worst of those beneath the dome of heaven; from them the trial emerges, and to them it returns."

He also mentioned, from the hadith of Simak ibn Harb, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, from his father, who said: When fornication and usury become apparent in a town, God, the Mighty and Majestic, permits its destruction.

In the mursal narrations of al-Hasan: "When people make knowledge apparent, but neglect action, love one another with their tongues, hate one another in their hearts, and sever the ties of kinship, God, the Mighty and Majestic, curses them at that time, and makes them deaf and blinds their sight."

In the Sunan of Ibn Majah, from the hadith of ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, who said: I was the tenth of ten men among the Emigrants (muhajirun) with the Messenger of God (ﷺ). The Messenger of God (ﷺ) turned his face to us and said: "O company of the Emigrants, there are five qualities I seek refuge in God from your encountering: No indecency has appeared among a people until they openly practise it, but they will be afflicted with plagues and diseases that were not present among their predecessors who passed away. No people has diminished measure and balance, but they will be afflicted with years of drought, severe hardship and the oppression of rulers. No people has withheld the zakat of their wealth, but they will be prevented from rain from the sky; were it not for the animals, they would not be rained upon. No people has broken a covenant, but God will give power over them to an enemy from outside them, who will seize some of what is in their hands. And when their leaders do not act by what God has revealed in His Book, God will make their violence to be among themselves."

In the Musnad and the Sunan, from the hadith of ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Salim ibn Abi al-Jaʿd, from Abu ʿUbaydah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, from his father, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Those who were before you, when a doer among them committed a sin, a forbidder would come to him as a warning. Then on the next day he would sit with him, eat with him and drink with him, as though he had not seen him in sin the day before. When God, the Mighty and Majestic, saw that from them, He struck the hearts of some of them against others, then cursed them upon the tongue of their prophets David and Jesus son of Mary. That was because they disobeyed and were transgressors. By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, you will surely enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and you will surely hold the foolish by the hand and compel him upon the truth with compulsion; or else God will strike the hearts of some of you against others, then He will curse you as He cursed them."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya mentioned, from Ibrahim ibn ʿAmr al-Sanʿani, who said: God revealed to Joshua son of Nun: "I am going to destroy forty thousand of your people, the best of them, and sixty thousand of their worst." He said: "O Lord, these are the wicked, so what of the righteous?" He said: "They did not become angry at My anger, and they used to eat and drink with them."

Abu ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Barr mentioned, from Abu ʿImran, who said: God, the Mighty and Majestic, sent two angels to a town, saying: "Destroy it with its inhabitants." They found a man standing praying in a mosque, so they said: "O Lord, in it is Your servant so-and-so, who is praying." God, the Mighty and Majestic, said: "Destroy it and destroy him along with them, for his face has never changed (in displeasure) on account of Me."

Al-Humaydi mentioned, from Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah, who said: Sufyan ibn Saʿid narrated to me, from Misʿar: "An angel was commanded to cause a town to sink. He said: 'O Lord, in it is so-and-so, the worshipper.' God revealed to him: 'Begin with him, for his face has never changed (in displeasure) for a single hour on account of Me.'"

Ibn Abi al-Dunya mentioned, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: When David committed the sin, he said: "O Lord, forgive me." He said: "I have forgiven you, but I have imposed its shame upon the Children of Israel." He said: "O Lord, how (can this be), when You are the Just Judge who wrongs no one? I commit the sin, and You impose its shame upon another!" So God revealed to him: "When you committed the sin, they did not hasten to denounce you."

(Section)

Know that the Jews are scattered across the east and west of the earth, and its south and north, as Almighty God said: ﴿And We divided them into tribes upon the earth﴾.

There is no group of them in any town except that a man from among the people of their religion arrives among them from a distant land, displaying harshness in his religion and excess in caution. If he is one of their jurists, he begins to denounce things to them, giving the impression of the weakness of their religion and their practice. Whenever he is strict with them, they say: "This is the scholar." The most knowledgeable of them is the one who is most severe toward them. You see him, as soon as he descends upon them, not eating from their food and their slaughtered animals, examining the butcher's knife, and beginning to denounce them over some aspect of it, saying: "I will eat only from an animal I have slaughtered myself."

You see them with him in torment, and they say: "This is a strange scholar who has come to us. He keeps denouncing the permitted to us, makes the burdens and shackles heavy upon us, and opens for us the doors of deceit and trickery." Whenever he does this, they say: "This is the divine scholar and the excellent rabbi." When their chief sees that his condition has spread and his words have circulated among them, he measures himself against him. When he sees that he has disparaged him and criticized him, he does not accept from him, for people in general tend toward the stranger, and his companions attribute him to ignorance and weakness of religion, and they do not believe him, because they see the newcomer as having been strict and constricting with them. Whatever man is greater in severity and constriction, he is considered more learned among them. So he turns away from this opinion and begins to praise him and thank him, saying: "God has magnified the reward of so-and-so, for he has strengthened the law of religion in the hearts of this community, has fortified its foundation, and perfected the enclosure of the Sharia." The newcomer hears his words and says: "What you have is more knowledgeable than him, and I know of no one more knowledgeable than him." And when he meets him, he says: "God has adorned our town through you and has raised this sect through you."

If the newcomer among them is one of their rabbis (ḥabr), then there you see the wondrous marvel of the code (nāmūs) he relies upon and the customs he introduces, and no one objects to him; rather, you see them submitting to him, while he draws their gold and draws their silver. If word reaches him of a Jew's criticism of him, he is patient with him until he sees him sitting on the side of the road on the Sabbath, or until he is informed that he bought milk or wine from a Muslim, or departed from some of the rulings of the Mishnah and the Talmud. He prohibits him in the assembly of the Jews, permits his honor to them, and attributes to him departure from Judaism. Then the town becomes too narrow for him in this state, and he has no choice but to reconcile what is between him and the rabbi by what the situation requires. He tells the Jews: "So-and-so has seen his right course, returned to the truth, and abandoned what he was in. He is now a Jew in the proper manner." Thereupon they return with honor and respect.

I will mention to you a question from among the questions of their altered or abrogated law, known as the matter of the *Yibbum* (levirate marriage) and the *Ḥalitzah* (the sandal ceremony), and it is this: they have in the Torah that if two brothers dwell in one place and one of them dies without leaving offspring, the widow does not go to an outside man; rather, her brother-in-law marries her, and the first son born to her is attributed to his deceased brother. If he refuses to marry her, she goes out complaining to the elders of his people, saying: "My brother-in-law has refused to preserve the name of his brother among the Children of Israel, and he did not want to marry me." He is summoned and required to stand and say: "I did not want to marry her." Then the woman takes his sandal, removes it from his foot, holds it in her hand, spits in his face, and calls out: "Thus shall be done to the one who does not build his brother's house." He is afterward called "the one whose sandal was removed," and his sons are given this nickname.

This is, in effect, a compulsion toward marrying her, for when he knows that it has been imposed upon the woman and upon him, he may feel shame and embarrassment at having his sandal removed from his foot, being spat upon in the face, and being branded with the hateful nickname that remains upon him and his children as a disgrace. He finds no alternative but to marry her. But if it stems from indifference toward her and dislike of her, to the point that he sees all of this as easier for him than being afflicted with her, and all of this is trivial to him in order to be free of her, he is not compelled to marry her.

This is their law in the Torah. From it there arose for them a derivative branch: that a man desires a woman and loves her, while she is in the utmost aversion to him. They devised, on the basis of this branch, a ruling of the utmost injustice and disgrace. When she comes to the judge, they bring him with her and coach her to say: "My brother-in-law does not preserve a name for his brother among the Children of Israel, and he did not want to marry me," while he is in love with her. They then force him to lie about himself, and that she wanted him and he refused. When she says this, the judge orders him to stand and say: "I did not want to marry her," though marrying her is the ultimate object of his desire and wish. So they command him to lie, and he removes his sandal from his foot, except that there is no sandal here, and he is spat upon in the face, and it is called out upon him: "This is the recompense of the one who does not build his brother's house." It was not enough for them that they lied about him, and they placed him in a position of disgrace, obligating him to lie, to be spat upon, and to be reproached for a sin another had drawn upon him, as it has been said:

"A crime drawn by the foolish of a people, and punishment alights upon one who did not commit it."

Is he not ashamed to disparage the Muslims, when this is his law and his religion?!

(Excellent benefit.)

Anyone among the people of knowledge who prefers this world and loves it will inevitably speak about God other than the truth in his fatwa, in his judgment, in his reports, and in what he imposes. This is because the rulings of the Lord, glory be to Him, very often come contrary to people's aims, especially the people of leadership and those who follow doubtful matters. Their aims are not fulfilled except by opposing the truth and repelling it, often. So if the scholar and the judge love leadership and follow desires, their aims are not achieved except by repelling what contradicts them of the truth. This is especially so when a doubt arises for him, so the doubt and the desire coincide, passion is stirred, the right is hidden, and the face of the truth is obliterated. Even if the truth is manifest, with no obscurity and no doubt about it, he proceeds to oppose it and says, "There is an escape through repentance." Concerning such people and their likes, God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Then there succeeded them a successor who neglected the prayer and followed their desires﴾. And God, the Exalted, also said about them: ﴿Then there succeeded them a successor who inherited the Book, taking the goods of this lower life and saying, "It will be forgiven us." And if there comes to them goods like it, they will take it. Was not the covenant of the Book taken from them, that they should not say about God except the truth, and they studied what is in it? And the Last Abode is better for those who fear God. Will you not then reason?﴾

He, glory be to Him, informed that they took the lower goods while knowing their prohibition, and they said, "It will be forgiven us," and if another such good came to them, they took it. So they persist in that. This is what drives them to say about God other than the truth: they say, "This is His judgment, His law, and His religion," while they know that His religion, law, and judgment are other than that, or they do not know that this is His religion, law, and judgment. Thus at times they say about God what they do not know, and at other times they say about Him what they know to be false.

As for those who fear God, they know that the Last Abode is better than this world, so love of leadership and desire do not lead them to prefer this world over the Hereafter. The way to this is that they hold fast to the Book and the Sunnah, seek help through patience and prayer, and reflect on the world and its passing and its baseness, and on the Hereafter and its coming and its permanence. These people must inevitably innovate in religion together with corruption in action, so both matters combine for them. For following desire blinds the eye of the heart, so it does not distinguish between the Sunnah and innovation, or it inverts it, so it sees innovation as Sunnah and Sunnah as innovation. This is the affliction of scholars when they prefer this world and follow leaderships and desires. And these verses concern them, up to His saying: ﴿And recite to them the story of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he detached himself from them, so Satan pursued him, and he became of the misguided. And had We willed, We would have raised him thereby, but he inclined toward the earth and followed his desire. So his example is like the example of the dog: if you chase it, it pants, or if you leave it, it pants﴾. This is the example of the evil scholar who acts contrary to his knowledge.

**[Section: The Disagreement over Whether the Bodies Were Created Before the Souls or the Reverse]**

As for the statement of Ishaq (Ibn Rahawayh), that the scholars reached *ijma'* (scholarly consensus) that the words of Allah the Exalted, ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾, refer to the souls before the bodies, Ishaq, may Allah have mercy on him, spoke according to what had reached him and what was known to him. This is not a consensus. People have disagreed over whether the bodies were created before the souls or together with them, on two views reported by our shaykh and others.

Also, does the meaning of the verse concern the taking of the descendants from one another and having them bear witness to what He instilled in them (fitrah), or the taking of them from the loins of Adam and questioning them? This is on two well-known views.

Those who said "the souls were created before the bodies" have no text from the Book of Allah or the Sunnah of His Messenger. The most they have is His saying, ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam﴾, and it is known that this verse does not indicate that.

As for the *ahadith* (sing. *hadith*, reports from the Prophet ﷺ) in which it is said that He brought them out "like the dhar" (tiny ants or motes), it is disputed whether this means their forms or their likenesses, and there is no explicit statement in them that these are their souls.

What the Qur'an, the Sunnah and sound reasoning indicate is that souls were created only together with the bodies, or after them. Allah the Exalted created the body of Adam before his soul. When He had shaped it and perfected its creation, He breathed into it of His soul, so the attachment of the soul to it came after the creation of his body.

Likewise is His practice, the Exalted, in creating his offspring, as shown by the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, which is agreed upon as authentic, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The creation of each one of you is gathered in his mother's belly for forty days as a drop (*nutfah*), then he becomes a clot (*'alaqah*) for a similar period, then a lump of flesh (*mudghah*) for a similar period, then the soul is breathed into him."

Some people erred in thinking that breathing the soul means sending the soul and dispatching it to him, and that it existed before that, and that breathing it means attaching it to him. This is not what the hadith means. Rather, when the embryo's creation is complete, Allah sends the angel to it, and he breathes a breath into it, and by that breath the soul comes into being. Thus the soul came into being for him through the breath.

It was likewise with the creation of the Messiah: Allah sent the angel to his mother, and he breathed a breath into her womb, and she conceived the Messiah, as He the Exalted said: ﴿So We sent to her Our Spirit, and it presented itself to her as a man in every respect. She said: "Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you should be fearing of Allah." He said: "I am only a messenger of your Lord, to give you a pure son."﴾ [Maryam: 17-19].

This is explicit in refuting the view of one who said: "This Spirit that addressed her is the Spirit of the Messiah," for the Spirit of the Messiah came into being from that breath which the Messenger of Allah breathed. How could the Messiah say to his mother, "I am a messenger of your Lord, to give you a pure son"? And how could the saying of Allah, ﴿So We breathed into her of Our Spirit﴾ [al-Anbiya': 91], mean "of the spirit of her son," so that the Spirit of the Messiah would be the one breathing into itself in its mother's belly?!

This is a view for which the proofs of its falsehood are many, and we have only pointed to it briefly.

He said in (*Kitab al-Ruh*, The Book of the Soul) the following text:

**The Eighteenth Issue [which is whether the souls were created before the bodies or created after them]**

On this issue people hold two well-known views, reported by Shaykh al-Islam and others. Among those who held that the souls were created before, were Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Marwazi and Abu Muhammad ibn Hazm, and Ibn Hazm reported it as a consensus. We will mention the arguments of both sides and which of them is nearer to the truth.

Those who held that the souls were created before the creation of the body said: Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We created you, then We fashioned you, then We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," and they prostrated﴾. They said: *thumma* (then) indicates sequence and delay, so the verse includes that the creation of the souls preceded Allah's command to the angels to prostrate to Adam.

And it is known with certainty that our bodies came into being after that, so it is established that it is the souls.

They said: It is also indicated by His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves, "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we have testified."﴾ They said: This questioning and making them testify was only for our souls, since the bodies did not exist at that time. In the *Muwatta'*:

Malik narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah, that Abd al-Hamid ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn al-Khattab informed him, from Muslim ibn Yasar al-Juhani, that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) asked about this verse: ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾, and he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) being asked about it, and he said: "Allah created Adam, then He wiped his back with His right hand and brought forth from it his descendants. He said: 'I created these for the Fire, and they will do the deeds of the people of the Fire.' Then He created these for Paradise, and they will do the deeds of the people of Paradise." A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, then what is the point of deeds?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, when Allah creates a person for Paradise, He causes him to act by the deeds of the people of Paradise until he dies upon one of the deeds of the people of Paradise, and He admits him to Paradise by it. And when He creates a servant for the Fire, He causes him to act by the deeds of the people of the Fire until he dies upon one of the deeds of the people of the Fire, and so he enters the Fire."

Al-Hakim said: This is a hadith meeting the conditions of Muslim. Al-Hakim also narrated through the route of Hisham ibn Sa'd, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet ﷺ): "When Allah created Adam, He wiped his back, and there fell from his back every soul that He would create until the Day of Resurrection, like the dhar. Then He placed between the eyes of each one of them a gleam of light. Then He presented them to Adam, and he said: 'Who are these, O Lord?' He said: 'These are your descendants.' He saw a man among them whose gleam between the eyes pleased him, and he said: 'O Lord, who is this?' He said: 'This is your son David, who will be at the end of the nations.' He said: 'How much life have You decreed for him?' He said: 'Sixty years.' He said: 'O Lord, add to his life forty years from mine.' So Allah the Exalted said: ﴿When it is decreed, it is written and sealed, and it cannot be changed.﴾ When the life of Adam came to an end, the Angel of Death came to him, and he said: 'Has there not remained forty years of my life?' He said: 'Have you not given them to your son David?' He said: 'He denied,' so his descendants deny; and he forgot, so his descendants forget; and he erred, so his descendants err." Al-Hakim said: This hadith meets the conditions of Muslim. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it and said: This is a hasan sahih (good and authentic) hadith.

Imam Ahmad narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the verse of debt was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first one to deny was Adam." Muhammad ibn Sa'd added: Then Allah completed for Adam a thousand years, and for David a hundred years.

Also in *Sahih al-Hakim*, from the hadith of Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, concerning the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾, the verse, he said: "He gathered them for Him that day all together, what would exist until the Day of Resurrection, and made them souls, then shaped them and made them speak, and they spoke. He took from them the covenant and the pact: ﴿And made them testify concerning themselves, 'Am I not your Lord?' They said, 'Yes, we have testified, lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were unaware of this."'﴾ He said: 'I call to witness against you the seven heavens and the seven earths, and I call to witness against you your father Adam, lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were unaware of this." So do not associate anything with Me, for I will send to you My messengers who will remind you of My covenant and My pact, and I will send down to you My books.' They said: 'We testify that You are our Lord and our God, there is no lord for us other than You.' Their father Adam was shown them, and he saw among them the rich and the poor, the beautiful in form and other than that, and he said: 'O Lord, if only You had made Your servants equal.' He said: 'I love to be thanked.' He saw among them the prophets like lamps, and they were singled out with another covenant concerning prophethood and messengership. That is His saying: ﴿And when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah﴾, and it is His saying: ﴿So set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth, the fitrah of Allah upon which He created mankind; there is no alteration to the creation of Allah﴾, and His saying: ﴿This is a warner of the warners of old﴾, and His saying: ﴿And We found most of them not upright in covenant, and indeed We found most of them defiantly disobedient﴾. And the spirit of Jesus was among those souls over which the covenant was taken, and He sent that spirit to Maryam when she withdrew from her family to an eastern place, and it entered through her opening." This chain is sahih (authentic).

Ishaq ibn Rahawayh said: Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid narrated to us, saying: al-Zubaydi Muhammad ibn al-Walid informed me, from Rashid ibn Sa'd, from al-Rahman ibn Abi Qatadah al-Basri, from his father, from Hisham ibn Hakim ibn Hizam, that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, do we begin deeds, or has the decree already passed?" He said: "When Allah brought out the descendants of Adam from his back, He made them testify concerning themselves, then He scattered them in His palms, and said: 'These are for Paradise, and these are for the Fire. The people of Paradise are made easy for the deeds of the people of Paradise, and the people of the Fire are made easy for the deeds of the people of the Fire.'"

Ishaq said: And al-Nadr informed us, narrating from Abu Ma'shar, from Sa'id al-Maqburi and Nafi' the client of al-Zubayr, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: When Allah wanted to create Adam, and he mentioned the creation of Adam, Adam said to Him: "Which of my hands do You love more that I should show You your descendants in it?" He said: "The right hand of my Lord, and both hands of my Lord are right." So He extended His right hand, and in it were all his descendants who would be created until the Day of Resurrection, the righteous in their form, the tested in their form, and the prophets in their forms. He said: "Would that You had spared them all!" He said: "I love to be thanked." And he mentioned the hadith.

Muhammad ibn Nasr said: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, al-Layth ibn Sa'd informed us, Ibn Ajlan narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Salam, who said: "Allah created Adam, then He took with His hands and closed them, and said: 'Choose, O Adam.' He said: 'I have chosen the right hand of my Lord, and both of His hands are right.' He opened it, and in it were his descendants. He said: 'Who are these, O Lord?' He said: 'Those whom I have decreed to create from your descendants, from the people of Paradise, until the Hour arrives.'"

He said: Ishaq narrated to us, Ja'far ibn Awn narrated to us, Hisham ibn Sa'd informed us, Zayd ibn Aslam, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "When Allah created Adam, He wiped his back, and there fell from his back every soul that He would create from his descendants until the Day of Resurrection."

Ishaq and Amr ibn Zurarah narrated to us, Isma'il informed us, from Kulthum ibn Jabr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, concerning the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾, the verse. He said: "Your Lord wiped the back of Adam, and every soul that He would create until the Day of Resurrection came out of it, and He took their covenant: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾ They said: 'Yes, we have testified.'"

Abu Jamrah al-Dab'i, Mujahid, Khubayb ibn Abi Thabit, Abu Salih and others narrated it from Ibn Abbas.

Ishaq said: Jarir informed us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Abdullah ibn Amr, concerning this verse, he said: "He took them as a comb is taken through the hair."

Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from al-Zubayr ibn Musa, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with both of them), who said: "Allah struck His right shoulder, and every soul created for Paradise came out, white and pure, and He said: 'These are the people of Paradise.' Then He struck His left shoulder, and every soul created for the Fire came out, black, and He said: 'These are the people of the Fire.' Then He took from all the children of Adam His covenant to believe in Him, to know Him, to know His command, and to affirm, and He made them testify concerning themselves, and they believed, affirmed, knew and acknowledged."

Muhammad ibn Nasr mentioned from the tafsir of al-Suddi, from Ibn Malik and Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, and from Murrah al-Hamdani, from Ibn Mas'ud, from some companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam﴾, the verse: "When Allah brought Adam out of Paradise before he descended from the heaven, He wiped the right side of Adam's back and brought forth from it a white progeny like pearls, and like the dhar. He said to them: 'Enter Paradise by My mercy.' And He wiped the left side of his back and brought forth from it a black progeny like the dhar, and He said: 'Enter the Fire, and I do not care.'" That is where He says: ﴿The companions of the right﴾, ﴿and the companions of the left﴾. Then He took the covenant from them, saying: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾ They said: ﴿Yes.﴾ So He gave to one group, obedient ones, and a group unwilling, under compulsion of taqiyyah (dissimulation). He and the angels said: ﴿We testify, lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were unaware of this," or say, "It was only that our fathers associated others with Allah before, and we were their descendants after them."﴾ So there is no child of Adam except that he knows that Allah is his Lord, and no polytheist except that he says: ﴿Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion﴾. That is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam﴾, and His saying: ﴿And to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and earth, willingly or unwillingly﴾, and His saying: ﴿So to Allah belongs the conclusive argument; and if He had willed, He would have guided you all﴾. He said: meaning the day when the covenant was taken from them.

Ishaq said: Rawh ibn Ubadah informed us, narrating from Musa ibn Ubaydah al-Rabadhi, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi say concerning this verse, ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam﴾, the verse: "They affirmed to Him faith and knowledge, the souls, before He created their bodies."

He said: Al-Fadl ibn Musa narrated to us, from Abd al-Malik, from Ata', concerning this verse, he said: "They were brought out of the loins of Adam when the covenant was taken from them, then they were returned to his loins."

Ishaq said: Ali ibn al-Aj'lah informed us, from al-Dahhak, who said: "Allah brought out of the back of Adam, on the day He created him, all that would exist until the Hour, and He brought them out like the dhar, and said: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾ They said: ﴿Yes.﴾ The angels said: ﴿We testify, lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were unaware of this."﴾ Then He grasped with His right hand and said: 'These are in Paradise,' and He grasped with the other and said: 'These are in the Fire.'"

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 7, verse 172 (part 2 of 7):

Ishaq said: Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi and Abu Nu'aym al-Mala'i informed us, saying: Hisham ibn Sa'd related to us from Yahya, not Ibn Sa'id, who said: I said to Ibn al-Musayyib: "What do you say about 'azl (coitus interruptus)?" He said: "If you wish, I will narrate to you a hadith that is true. Indeed Allah, glorified is He, when He created Adam, showed him a honour that none of Allah's creation had seen: He showed him every soul that He would create from his progeny until the Day of Resurrection. So whoever tells you that He adds to them anything or subtracts from them anything, he has lied. And even if I had seventy (children), I would not care."

In the tafsir of Ibn 'Uyayna, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, regarding His words ﴿And to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly﴾: he said, "On the day He took the covenant."

Ishaq said: They were then acknowledging, because Allah, mighty and majestic, informed that He said: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾ They said: ﴿Yes, we testify﴾. Allah, exalted is He, does not address except one who understands the address, and does not answer except one who has understood the question. Their answer to Him by their saying is evidence that they understood from Allah and comprehended His questioning them: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾. So they answered Him after comprehension on their part of the address and understanding of it, that ﴿they said, "Yes"﴾, and thus they acknowledged His lordship.

[Section: The evidence that souls were created after bodies]

They also argued with what Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Mandah narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Sabir al-Bukhari informed us, Muhammad ibn al-Mundhir ibn Sa'id al-Harawi related to us, Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Harun al-Mus'ici related to us, 'Utba ibn al-Sakan related to us, Artat ibn al-Mundhir related to us, 'Ata' ibn 'Ajlan related to us, from Yunus ibn Halbas, from 'Amr ibn 'Absa, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Indeed Allah created the spirits of the servants two thousand years before the servants. Those among them who recognised each other are united, and those among them who disagreed are at odds."

This is some of what those people argued with.

The others said: The discussion with you is in two stations. One: mentioning the evidence that souls were created after the creation of bodies. Two: the answer to what you have used as evidence.

As for the first station: Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿O mankind, indeed We created you from male and female﴾, and this is an address to the human being who is spirit and body, which shows that his whole being was created after the creation of the two parents. And more explicit than it is His saying: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul and created from it its mate and dispersed from both of them many men and women.
