And fear Allah...﴾ — the verse — and this is explicit that the creation of the whole human species was after the creation of its origin.

If it is said: This does not negate the precedence of the creation of spirits over their bodies, even if they were created after the creation of the father of mankind, as the earlier reports indicate.

It is said: We will show, Allah willing, that the mentioned reports do not indicate the precedence of spirits over bodies with a settled, established precedence. Their maximum, after their soundness and authentication, is to indicate that their Creator and Originator, glorified is He, fashioned the forms of the souls, determined their creation, their terms and their deeds, extracted those forms from their substance, then returned them to it, and decreed each individual of them in its determined time. They do not indicate that they were created in a settled creation and then continued existing, alive, knowing, speaking, all in one place, and then were sent from it to the bodies in groups after groups, as Abu Muhammad ibn Hazm said. Can the reports bear what they have no capacity for? Yes: the Lord, glorified is He, creates from them group after group in the manner in which the decree was first preceded, so the external creation comes in conformity with the prior decree, as is His way, exalted is He, with all His creatures. For He decreed for them measures, terms, attributes and states, then brought them into existence conforming to that decree which He decreed for them, neither adding to it nor subtracting from it.

So the mentioned reports only indicate the affirmation of the prior decree. Some of them indicate that He, glorified is He, extracted their likenesses and forms, and distinguished the people of felicity from the people of wretchedness. As for His addressing them, questioning them, their acknowledgement of His lordship and their testimony against themselves of servitude, whoever said this from among the early generations, he only built it on his understanding of the verse, and the verse does not indicate this; rather it indicates the opposite.

As for the hadith of Malik, Abu 'Umar said: it is a disconnected hadith (munqati'), Muslim ibn Yasar did not meet 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, and between them in this hadith is Nu'aym ibn Rabi'ah. Also, with this chain it cannot be a proof. And this Muslim ibn Yasar is unknown; it has been said that he is Madani and not Muslim ibn Yasar al-Basri. Ibn Abi Khaythama said: I read to Yahya ibn Ma'in the hadith of Malik this, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysa, and he wrote with his own hand against Muslim ibn Yasar: "not known" (la ya'raf).

Then Abu 'Umar narrated it through the route of al-Nasa'i: "Informed us" Muhammad ibn Wahb, related to us Muhammad ibn Salama, who said: Abu 'Abd al-Rahim related to me, who said: Zayd ibn Abi Unaysa related to me from 'Abd al-Hamid ibn 'Abd al-Rahman from Muslim ibn Yasar from Nu'aym ibn Rabi'ah.

Then he narrated it through the route of Sakhbara: "related to us" Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Malik ibn Waqid, related to us Muhammad ibn Salama from Abu 'Abd al-Rahim from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysa from 'Abd al-Hamid from Muslim from Nu'aym. Abu 'Umar said: The addition of one who added Nu'aym ibn Rabi'ah in this hadith is not a proof that the one who did not mention it memorised; rather the addition comes from the reliable, precise narrator.

The summary of the matter regarding this hadith: its chain is not sound, because Muslim ibn Yasar and Nu'aym ibn Rabi'ah are both unknown as bearers of knowledge. But the meaning of this hadith has been authenticated from the Prophet ﷺ through many established routes, too lengthy to mention, from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab and others, a group too lengthy to name.

What Abu 'Umar intended were the hadiths indicating the prior decree, for those are what he cited afterward. He mentioned the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar on qadar, and at its end: a man from Muzayna or Juhayna asked him, "O Messenger of Allah, then what is the point of action?" He said: "Indeed the people of Paradise are made easy for the deeds of the people of Paradise, and the people of the Fire are made easy for the deeds of the people of the Fire."

He said: This meaning concerning qadar has been reported from the Prophet ﷺ through 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Umar, Abu Hurayrah, Abu Sa'id, Abu Suraykha al-Ghifari, 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, 'Imran ibn Husayn, 'A'isha, Anas ibn Malik, Suraqa ibn Ju'shum, Abu Musa al-Ash'ari and 'Ubada ibn al-Samit. Most of the hadiths of these have many routes, and he then narrated many of them with his chain.

As for the hadith of Abu Salih from Abu Hurayrah, it only indicates the extraction of progeny and their forming into forms of tiny atoms, and among them at that time were the bright and the dark. And there is nothing in it that He, glorified is He, created their spirits before the bodies and kept them in one place, then drew each of those spirits to its body when that body came into being. Yes, He, glorified is He, assigns to each body the spirit that He decreed it would have at that time. But as for His creating the very soul of that body at that time, finishing its creation, and depositing it in a place idle from its body until, when He brings its body into being, He sends it to it from that place — none of the hadiths indicates this at all, for whoever reflects upon them.

As for the hadith of Ubayy ibn Ka'b, it is not from the Prophet ﷺ; at most, even if it were sound (and it is not sound), it would be from Ubayy's own words. This chain narrates through it very strange things, both raised and halted. Abu Ja'far al-Razi was rated reliable and weak: 'Ali ibn al-Madini said: "He was trustworthy," and said also: "He used to mix up." Ibn Ma'in said: "He is trustworthy," and also: "His hadith is written, except that he errs." Imam Ahmad said: "He is not strong in hadith," and also: "His hadith is acceptable." al-Fallas said: "Poor memory." Abu Zur'a said: "He errs a great deal." Ibn Hibban said: "He is alone in odd reports from well-known narrators."

I say: Among what makes this hadith objectionable is his saying: "The spirit of 'Isa was among those spirits upon which the covenant was taken, and that spirit was sent to Maryam when she withdrew from her family to an eastern place, and it entered her mouth." It is well known that the spirit that was sent to Maryam is not the spirit of the Messiah, but rather the spirit which was breathed into her, and she conceived the Messiah. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿So We sent to her Our Spirit, and it appeared to her as a well-formed man. She said: "Indeed I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you are fearing Allah." He said: "I am only a messenger of your Lord, to give you a pure boy."﴾ So the spirit of the Messiah certainly does not address her in this manner speaking on its own behalf. And in some routes of this hadith of Abu Ja'far, it is stated that the spirit of the Messiah is the one who addressed her and was sent to her.

Here there are four stations:

- The first: that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, extracted their forms and likenesses, and distinguished their wretched and their happy, their healthy and their afflicted.
- The second: that Allah, glorified is He, established the proof against them at that time, made them testify to His lordship, and called His angels to witness against them.
- The third: that this is the explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam from their loins their descendants﴾.
- The fourth: that He settled all those spirits after extracting them in a place and finished their creation, and that only a group of them is renewed each time, being sent after group to their bodies.

As for the first station, the reports are abundant in establishing it, both raised and halted.

As for the second station, those among the exegetes who took it from the verse thought it was its explanation, and this is the view of the majority of exegetes of the transmitted tradition. Abu Ishaq said: It is possible that Allah, glorified is He, gave the likenesses of the atoms He extracted understanding by which they reason, as He said: ﴿A female ant said, "O ants, enter your dwellings"﴾. And He subjected the mountains to David, glorifying with him, and the birds.

Ibn al-Anbari said: The view of the people of hadith and the senior scholars regarding this verse is that Allah extracted the descendants of Adam from his loins and the loins of his children, and they were in the form of atoms, and He took from them the covenant that He is their Creator and that they are created, and they acknowledged that and accepted it. This was after He placed in them intellects by which they understood what was presented to them, just as He gave the mountain intellect when it was addressed, and as He did with the camel when it prostrated, and the palm tree until it heard and submitted when called.

Al-Jurjani said: There is no contradiction, praise be to Allah, between the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Indeed Allah wiped the back of Adam and brought forth from his progeny," and the verse. For when He, mighty and majestic, took them from the back of Adam, He took them from the backs of his descendants, since the descendants of Adam are his descendants, some from others. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed we were unaware of this"﴾, meaning of the covenant taken from them. So when they say that, the angels will be witnesses against them of the taking of the covenant. He said: In this is evidence for the interpretation brought by the report, that Allah, exalted is He, said to the angels: "Bear witness," and they said: "We bear witness." He said: Some scholars claimed that the covenant was taken only from the spirits and not the bodies, because the spirits are those that understand and comprehend, and to them belongs reward and upon them falls punishment, while bodies are dead and do not understand or comprehend. He said: Ishaq ibn Rahawayh inclined to this meaning, and he mentioned that it is the saying of Abu Hurayrah. Ishaq said: The people of knowledge agreed that it was the spirits before the bodies that He questioned and made to witness. Al-Jurjani said:

They argued with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead; rather, they are alive﴾. The bodies have decayed and dissolved in the earth, while the spirits are provided for and rejoice; they are the ones who feel pain, rejoice, grieve, recognise and deny. The proof of this is present in dreams, and a person wakes up with the trace of the pleasure of joy and the pain of grief still in himself, from what the spirit encounters without the body. He said: The essential benefit of this section is that He, glorified is He, has established the proof against every soul, whether it reaches maturity or not, by the covenant He took from them; and He added to those among them who reached maturity the proof through the signs and evidences He set up in themselves and in the world, and through the messengers sent to them as bearers of good news and warners, and through admonitions and the examples whose reports were conveyed to them. Yet He, mighty and majestic, does not hold anyone of them accountable for obedience except to the extent of the proof that binds him, the power He placed in them, and the indications He gave them. He, glorified is He, has explained what He acts upon in those who attained to command and prohibition, and He has withheld from us knowledge of what He decreed concerning those who did not reach maturity; yet we know that He is just, whose judgement admits no injustice, wise, whose making admits no disparity, and powerful, who is not questioned about what He does; to Him belong the creation and the command. Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds.

[Section: The meaning of the verse: "And when your Lord took..."]

Others disputed with these people concerning the meaning of the verse, and said: The meaning of His saying ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam from their loins their descendants﴾ is: He brought them out and created them, after they had been drops in the loins of the fathers, into the world in their order of existence, and made them testify against themselves that He is their Lord, by showing them His signs and proofs which compel them to know that He is their Creator. So there is no one except that in him is something of his Lord's workmanship that testifies that He is his Originator and that His judgement is executed upon him. When they recognised that, and everything they see and witness calls them to affirm it, they were in the position of witnesses and those made to witness against themselves for its truth, as He said in another place: ﴿witnessing against themselves of disbelief﴾, placing them in the position of witnesses even if they do not say, "We are disbelievers." And as you say: "My limbs have testified to your words," meaning, "they have known it," so it is as if my limbs, if they were asked and were able to speak, would testify. And of this kind is His clarification and manifestation as well: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god but He﴾, meaning, "He informs and makes clear," so this resembles the testimony of one who testifies before judges and others. This is the statement of Ibn al-Anbari.

Al-Jurjani added explanation to this view, saying, relating from his companions: When Allah created the creation and His knowledge was executed concerning them, with what is and what is not yet but will be, that which will be is as that which is, since His knowledge of its occurrence precludes its non-occurrence. In the language's figurative usage, what is awaited and will occur afterward may be placed in the position of what has occurred, because of the precedence of His knowledge of its occurrence, as He, mighty and majestic, said in one place of the Qur'an: ﴿And the companions of the Fire will call out, and the companions of the Garden will call out﴾, and ﴿And the companions of the heights will call out﴾. And he said: So the interpretation of His saying ﴿And when your Lord took﴾ is ﴿and when your Lord takes﴾. Likewise His saying ﴿and made them testify against themselves﴾, meaning: and He makes them testify by what He placed in them of the intellect by which understanding occurs and reward and punishment are due, and every one who is born and reaches puberty and comprehends harm and benefit, and understands promise and threat, reward and punishment, becomes as if Allah, exalted is He, had taken from him the covenant regarding monotheism by the intellect He placed in him, and showed him the signs and proofs of his own origination, and that it is not possible that he created himself; and if that is not possible, there must be a creator other than him, "there is nothing like Him." And no creature reaches this level and is unobstructed by any impediment of understanding except when a matter befalls him that makes him turn to Allah, mighty and majestic, lifting his head to the sky and pointing to it with his finger, knowing that his Creator, exalted is He, is above him. And since the intellect by which understanding and conveying of understanding occur leads to and indicates the knowledge we have mentioned, then everyone who reaches this level has been taken the covenant and pledge, and it is permissible to say: he acknowledged, submitted, and surrendered, just as Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿And to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly﴾.

He said: They argued with the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "The pen is lifted from three: from the child until he reaches puberty, from the insane until he recovers, and from the sleeper until he awakes," and with the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿Indeed We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to carry it and feared it, and man carried it﴾. So the trust here is a covenant and pledge. The refusal of the heavens, earth and mountains to carry the trust was due to their lack of the intellect by which understanding and conveying understanding occur, and man's carrying it was because of the intellect in him. He said: The Arabs have various poetic uses of this, among them the saying:

*"The cliff guaranteed to Fuq'as its steadfastness, / Indeed the cliff belongs to Fuq'as and does not fail,"*

and "al-Qinan" is a mountain; he mentions that it guaranteed Fuq'as, and its guarantee for them was that when a matter of defeat or fear befell them they sought refuge in it, so this was made like a guarantee for them. From it is the saying of al-Nabigha:

*"Like the cliffs of al-Jawlan, its lord has glorified, / and its Hawarin, among them, humbly submissive."*

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 7, verse 172 (part 3 of 7):

And Ajārif, the Jawlān with its mountains, and Ḥawrān, the land beside it. The one who said this claimed that the words of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were unaware of this,"  or say, "Our fathers associated partners with Allah before, and we were offspring after them"﴾, are evidence for this interpretation (ta'wil), because He, the Mighty and Majestic, informed that this taking of the covenant from them was so that they would not say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were unaware of this." Their unawareness here cannot be free of one of two possibilities: either it is unawareness of the Day of Resurrection, or unawareness of the taking of the covenant. As for the Day of Resurrection, He, glorified is He, did not mention in His Book that He took from them a covenant and pledge to know of the resurrection and the reckoning; He only mentioned their knowing Him. As for the taking of the covenant from children and the like, if this covenant was taken from them as the opponent said, then they had not yet reached a stage at which they could be unaware of it and then deny and reject it. So when would this unawareness occur from them, while He, the Mighty and Majestic, does not hold them accountable for what did not come from them? That would be mentioning something impossible and absurd. As for His words, ﴿or say, "Our fathers associated partners with Allah before, and we were offspring after them"﴾: the shirk for which they are held accountable must either have come from themselves or from their fathers. If it came from themselves, it could only be after reaching maturity and after denial became established against them, since a child does not commit shirk or anything else. If it came from others, then the Muslim community (ummah) is in consensus (ijmā') that ﴿no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾, as the Mighty and Majestic said in the Book. This is not contrary to what has been related from the Prophet (ﷺ): that Allah wiped the back of Adam and brought forth his offspring and took the covenant from them, because the Prophet (ﷺ) was relating the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and gave an account resembling its wording, placing the past tense in the place of the future. He said: this is similar to the story of His words, ﴿And [mention] when Allah took the covenant of the prophets: "Whatever I give you of Scripture and wisdom and then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him"﴾. So He, glorified is He, made what He sent down to the prophets of the Scripture and wisdom a covenant He took from their nations after them. This is shown by His words, ﴿Then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him﴾. Then He said to the nations, ﴿Have you acknowledged and accepted My burden upon that?﴾ They said, "We acknowledge." He said, ﴿Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses.﴾ So He, glorified is He, made the arrival of His Book, revealed to their prophets, a proof against the nations, just as the taking of the covenant from them was, and made their knowledge of it an acknowledgment from them.

I say: Similar to this also is His words, ﴿Remember the favour of Allah upon you and His covenant with which He bound you when you said, "We hear and we obey."﴾ This is His covenant which He took from them after sending His messengers to them, to believe in Him and affirm Him. Its counterpart is His words, ﴿those who fulfil the covenant of Allah and do not break the pledge﴾, and His words, ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan—indeed, he is to you a clear enemy—and that you worship Me; this is a straight path?﴾ So this is His charge to them through the tongues of His messengers. Like it is His words to the Children of Israel, ﴿And fulfil My covenant, I will fulfil your covenant﴾, and like it ﴿And [mention] when Allah took the covenant of those given the Scripture: "You must make it clear to the people and not conceal it."﴾ And His words, ﴿And [mention] when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, son of Mary, and We took from them a solemn covenant.﴾ So this is a covenant He took from them after their being sent, just as He took it from their nations after their warning. This is the covenant whose breaker He cursed, and He followed it with His words, ﴿So for their breaking of their covenant, We cursed them and made their hearts hard﴾. He only punished them for breaking the covenant which He took from them through the tongues of His messengers, and He made this explicit in His words, ﴿And [mention] when We took your covenant and raised above you the mount: "Take what We have given you with strength and remember what is in it that you may be fearing Allah."﴾ And since this verse and its counterpart are in a Medinan surah, He addressed the People of the Book in it with a reminder of this covenant, for it is a covenant He took from them to believe in Him and His messengers. And since this verse of al-A'rāf is in a Meccan surah, He mentioned in it the covenant and the general witnessing of all who are responsible, of those who acknowledged His lordship, His oneness, and the falsehood of shirk. This is a covenant and witnessing by which the proof is established against them, the excuse is cut off, punishment becomes due, and destruction is deserved by opposing it. So they must necessarily be mindful of it and aware of it, and that is what He created them upon: acknowledgment of His lordship and that their Creator is their Lord, that they are created and nurtured. Then He sent to them His messengers to remind them of what is in their natural disposition (fiṭrah) and their minds, and to make them know His right over them, His command and prohibition, His promise and threat.

The wording of the verse indicates this in several respects:
- First: He said, ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam﴾ and did not say "from Adam," and the children of Adam are other than Adam.
- Second: He said, ﴿from their backs﴾ and did not say "from the back," and this is a partial substitution (badal ba'ḍ min kull) or a substitution of inclusion (badal ishtimāl), and it is the better one.
- Third: He said, ﴿their offspring﴾ and did not say "his offspring."
- Fourth: He said, ﴿and made them testify concerning themselves﴾, meaning He made them witnesses against themselves. A witness must necessarily be mindful of what he testifies to, and he only recalls his testimony after coming into this world; he does not recall a testimony before it.
- Fifth: He, glorified is He, informed that the wisdom of this witnessing is to establish the proof against them, lest they say on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿Indeed, we were unaware of this.﴾ The proof was established against them through the messengers and the natural disposition upon which they were created, as He said, ﴿messengers as bearers of good tidings and warners, so that mankind will have no argument against Allah after the messengers.﴾
- Sixth: their being reminded of this so that they would not say on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿Indeed, we were unaware of this.﴾ It is known that by bringing them out from the loins of Adam, all of them, and making them all witness at that time, none of them mentions this.
- Seventh: His words, ﴿or say, "Our fathers associated partners with Allah before, and we were offspring after them"﴾. He mentioned two wisdoms in this informing and witnessing: first, that the unawareness should not be a claim, and second, that imitation (taqlīd) should not be a claim. The unaware has no awareness, and the imitator follows others in his imitation.
- Eighth: His words, ﴿Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did?﴾ That is, if He punished them for their denial and shirk, they would say this. He, glorified is He, only destroys them for opposing His messengers and denying them. So if He destroyed them for imitating their fathers in their shirk without establishing the proof against them through the messengers, He would be destroying them for what the falsifiers did, or destroying them while they were unaware of the falsehood of what they were upon. He, glorified is He, has informed that He would not destroy the towns unjustly while their people were unaware, and that He only destroys them after excuses and warnings.
- Ninth: He, glorified is He, made each one witness against himself that He is his Lord and Creator, and He argued against them with this witnessing in more than one place in His Book, such as His words, ﴿And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say, "Allah." So how are they deluded?﴾ That is: how are they turned away from monotheism after this acknowledgment of theirs that Allah is their Lord and Creator? This is abundant in the Qur'an. So this is the proof of which He made them witness against themselves by its content, and His messengers reminded them of it by His words, ﴿Is there doubt about Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth?﴾ Allah reminded them through the tongues of His messengers of this acknowledgment and knowledge, and He never reminded them of an acknowledgment prior to their being brought into existence, nor did He establish the proof against them by it.
- Tenth: He made this a sign (āyah), which is the clear, evident indication that necessarily implies what it indicates, such that what it indicates does not fail to follow. This is the nature of the signs of the Lord, the Exalted, for they are specific proofs of a specific object sought, necessarily leading to knowledge of it. So He, the Exalted, said, ﴿Thus We detail the signs﴾, that is, in this same way of detailing and clarifying We detail the signs, ﴿so that they may return﴾ from shirk to monotheism, and from disbelief to faith.

These signs which He detailed are those which He clarified in His Book from the kinds of His creation: they are horizontal and psychological signs, signs in their own souls and selves, and signs in the horizons and regions that the Lord, blessed and exalted, brings into being, which indicate His existence, His oneness, the truthfulness of His messengers, and the return and the Resurrection. Among the clearest of them is what each one witnessed against himself: that He is his Lord, Creator, and Originator, and that he is nurtured, created, made, and originated after not having been. It is impossible for something to come into being without a cause that brought it into being, or for it to be the cause of its own origination, so there must be a creator who brought it into being: ﴿there is nothing like unto Him﴾.

This acknowledgment and witnessing is a natural disposition (fiṭrah) upon which they were created, not something acquired. This verse, ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their backs, their offspring﴾, corresponds with the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): «Every child is born upon the fiṭrah,» and with His words, ﴿So direct your face toward the religion, inclining to truth. [Adhere to] the fiṭrah of Allah upon which He has created mankind. No change should there be in the creation of Allah. That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know. [Turning] in repentance to Him﴾.

Some exegetes mentioned only this view, such as al-Zamakhsharī; others mentioned only the first view; and others related both views, such as Ibn al-Jawzī, al-Wāḥidī, al-Māwardī and others.

Al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā al-Jurjānī said: A challenger in this section objected with a report related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: «Indeed Allah wiped the back of Adam, brought forth from it his offspring, took the covenant from them, then returned them to his back.» He said: This prevents the permissibility of the interpretation you have adopted, because it is impossible for them to be returned to the back if the covenant was taken from them after maturity and full reason. It was said to him: The meaning of «then returned them to his back» is «then He returns them to his back,» just as we said that the meaning of «your Lord took» is «your Lord takes.» So its meaning is: then He returns them to his back by their deaths, because when they die they are returned to the earth for burial; Adam was created from it, and they are returned into it. So when they are returned into it, they have been returned into Adam and into his back, since Adam was created from it and returned into it, and a part of a thing is from the thing. In your interpretation of this hadith according to its outward meaning there is a discrepancy between it and what the Qur'an brought on this matter, unless its interpretation is returned to what we mentioned, because He, the Mighty and Majestic, said:
﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their backs, their offspring﴾, and did not mention Adam in the section. Here it is only added to Him to identify that they are his offspring. In the hadith: «He wiped the back of Adam», so it is not possible to reconcile what came in the Qur'an and what came in the hadith except by the interpretation we mentioned.

Al-Jurjānī said: I say: We adhere to what has been related about the verse from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and what the scholars of the pious predecessors (salaf) held is more excellent; to it I turn and in it I find comfort, and Allah is the Guardian of success toward what is more fitting and more guided.

Moreover, some of our companions from the People of the Sunnah (ahl al-sunnah) mentioned, in refuting this speaker, a meaning that is admissible and permissible in the flowing wording and the Arabic idiom with ease, without strain or force, which is that His words, ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam﴾, are a new beginning (mubtada') and a report from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, about what occurred from Him in taking the covenant from them. «When» (idh) requires an answer, and its answer is His words, ﴿They said, "Yes"﴾, and this report ended with the completion of its account. Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, began another report mentioning what the polytheists will say on the Day of Resurrection. They said, "We testify," meaning "we bear witness," as al-Ḥuṭay'ah said:
"Al-Ḥuṭay'ah testifies when he meets his Lord that al-Walīd is more deserving of excuse."
Meaning: al-Ḥuṭay'ah testifies. He says, may He be exalted: We testify that you will say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were unaware of this," that is, of what they are in of reckoning, questioning, and being held accountable for disbelief. Then He added another report, saying, ﴿or say﴾, meaning "and that you say," because "or" here means the conjunction "and," like His words, ﴿And do not obey from among them a sinner or a disbeliever﴾. Its interpretation is: "and We testify that you will say on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Our fathers associated partners with Allah before, and we were offspring after them﴾," that is, they associated partners and led us into their way of shirk in our childhood, so we followed their ways and imitated them. There is no sin upon us since we were imitators of them, and the sin in that is theirs. They said, ﴿Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, and indeed we are following in their footsteps.﴾ This is shown by their saying, ﴿Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did?﴾, that is, their leading us into shirk. So the first story is a report about all created beings regarding the taking of the covenant from them, and the second story is a report about what the polytheists will say on the Day of Resurrection of excuses.

He said: Regarding what the challenger claimed, that there is a discrepancy between the Book and the report because of the difference in their wording, he gave an answer that must be accepted by its parallels and examples, by which he supported his rebuttal of him. He said: The report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that Allah wiped the back of Adam adds an account to the story which Allah, the Exalted, mentioned in the Book, some of which He mentioned and not all of it. Had he (ﷺ) reported, besides this addition, what may have occurred at that time when the covenant was taken, of what Allah did not include in His Book, there would be no contradiction or discrepancy in that; rather, it would be an addition in benefit.

Likewise, when words differ in their form but their reference is to one matter, this does not necessitate contradiction. As the Mighty and Majestic said in His Book about the creation of Adam: He mentioned once that he was created from dust, once that he was created from black mud shaped (ḥama' masnūn), once from clay that sticks (ṭīn lāzib), and once from clay like pottery (ṣalṣāl kal-fakhkhār). These words are different and their meanings in their states are also different, since ṣalṣāl is other than ḥama', and ḥama' is other than turāb. Yet all of them ultimately return to one substance, which is dust, and from dust these states have passed in gradation.

So His words, glorified and exalted is He, ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their backs, their offspring﴾, and His words, peace and blessings be upon him, «He wiped the back of Adam and brought forth from it his offspring», have one meaning in origin. But His words, peace and blessings be upon him, «He wiped the back of Adam» are an addition to the report about Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. His, the Mighty and Majestic, wiping the back of Adam and bringing forth his offspring from it is a wiping of the backs of his offspring and bringing forth their offspring from their backs, as He, the Exalted, mentioned. For we know that not all the descendants of Adam were from his loins; but since the first generation was from his loins, then the second from the loins of the first, then the third from the loins of the second, it is permissible for all of that to be attributed to the back of Adam, because they are his branches and he is their origin.

And just as it is permissible that what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, mentioned — that He brought it forth from the backs of the offspring of Adam — be from the back of Adam, it is also permissible that what the Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned — that He brought it forth from the back of Adam — be from his offspring, since origin and branch are one thing. Furthermore, when the Mighty and Majestic attributed the offspring to Adam in the report, it is possible that the report concerns both the offspring and Adam, as the Mighty and Majestic said:
﴿So their necks remained humbled before it﴾. The report outwardly concerns the necks, and the adjective is for the implicit nouns in them, which is attributed to them, just as Adam was attributed there, and neither of them is apparently the intended object of the report. It is not possible that His words "humbled" (khāḍi'īn) refer to "necks" (a'nāq), because the plural form of the feminine would be "khāḍi'āt," and from it is the poet's saying:
"And he chokes with the word he has spread, just as the spearhead chokes from the blood."
The "ṣadr" (chest) is masculine, and his saying "shariqat" (choked) is for the feminine because the chest is attributed to the spear.

This is some of what the predecessors and later scholars said about this verse. Furthermore, it does not indicate the creation of souls before bodies as a fixed creation. Its utmost is to indicate the bringing forth of their forms and likenesses in the forms of atoms (dharr) and questioning them, then returning them to their origin, if the report is authentic in that. What is established is only the affirmation of the prior decree and their division into the wretched and the blessed.

[Section: The evidence that the creation of souls is later than the creation of bodies]

The Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on Surah 7, Verse 172 (Part 4 of 7)

The evidence that the creation of the souls came after the creation of their bodies is found in several aspects.

First: this was the manner in which the father and origin of humankind was created. Allah, glorified is He, sent Jibril (Gabriel), who took a handful of earth and kneaded it until it became clay. Then He shaped it, and then He breathed the spirit into it after shaping it. When the spirit entered it, it became flesh and blood, living and speaking.

In the Tafsir of Abu Malik and Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, and from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, from some of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ): When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, finished creating what He willed, He established Himself upon the Throne. He made Iblis a ruler over the lowest heaven. He had been among the guardians before him, from a class of angels called the jinn, and they were named jinn because they were the guardians of the people of Paradise. Iblis, along with his rule, was a guardian. Pride entered his chest and he said: "Allah has given me this only because of a merit in me."

In another wording: "a merit in me over the angels." When this pride settled in his soul, Allah became aware of it. So Allah said to the angels: ﴿Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a khalifah (vicegerent)﴾. They said: "Our Lord, what will be the condition of the khalifah, and what will they do on the earth?" Allah said: "There will be descendants of his who will cause corruption on the earth, envy one another, and some of them will kill others." They said: ﴿Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we glorify You with Your praise and sanctify You?﴾ He said: ﴿Indeed, I know that which you do not know﴾, meaning concerning the matter of Iblis. Then Jibril was sent to the earth to bring him clay from it. The earth said: "I seek refuge in Allah from you, that you take from me." So he returned without taking anything, and said: "My Lord, it sought refuge in You, so You granted it refuge." Then Mika'il was sent, and it sought refuge from him, so he granted it refuge. Then the Angel of Death was sent, and it sought refuge from him. He said: "And I seek refuge in Allah from returning without carrying out His command." So he took from the surface of the earth and mixed it. He did not take from one place, so he took from red, white and black soil. For this reason the children of Adam came out differing in colour. Then he ascended with it before the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, until it became sticky clay (tin lazib). Lazib is that which sticks parts together. Then He said to the angels: ﴿Indeed, I am going to create a human being from clay. So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, fall down in prostration to him﴾. He created him with His own hand so that Iblis would not be arrogant toward him, so that Allah could say to him: "You are proud of what I made with My hand, and I was not proud regarding him." So He created him as a human, and he was a body of clay for forty years. The angels passed by him and were frightened by him when they saw him, and the one among them most frightened of him was Iblis. He would pass by him and strike him, and the body would ring out as pottery rings, producing a clanging sound. This is the moment of the words: ﴿from clay like pottery﴾, and he said: "For what matter were You created?" He entered through its mouth and came out through its rear. He said to the angels: "Do not be afraid of this, for your Lord is Samad (the Eternal, Self-Sufficient) and this is hollow. If I were given power over it, I would destroy it." When the appointed time came that Allah, glorified is His praise, intended to breathe the spirit into him, He said to the angels: "When I breathe into him of My spirit, prostrate to him." When the spirit was breathed into him and entered his head, he sneezed. The angels said: "Say: All praise is for Allah." He said: "All praise is for Allah." Allah said to him: "May your Lord have mercy upon you."

When the spirit entered his eyes, he looked at the fruits of Paradise. When it entered his belly, he desired food. Before the spirit reached his feet, he rose hastily toward the fruits of Paradise. This is the moment of the words: ﴿Man was created of haste﴾. And he mentioned the rest of the hadith.

Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la said: Ibn Wahb informed us, Ibn Zayd narrated to us, saying: When Allah created the Fire, the angels were terrified of it, a great terror, and they said: "Our Lord, why did You create this Fire? For what purpose did You create it?" He said: "For whoever disobeys Me among My creation."

On that day Allah had no creation except the angels, and the earth had no creatures in it; Adam was created after that. He recited His words: ﴿Has there come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing worth mentioning?﴾ Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "O Messenger of Allah, I wish that were the time (of which he was not anything)." Then he said: "The angels said: 'Will there come upon us an age in which we disobey You?'" They did not see any creation other than themselves. He said: "No! Indeed I want to create on the earth a creation and place in it a khalifah." And he mentioned the hadith.

Ibn Ishaq said: It is said, and Allah knows best: Allah created Adam, then placed him, looking at him for forty years, before breathing the spirit into him, until he became clay like pottery that had not been touched by fire. It is said, and Allah knows best: When the spirit reached his head, he sneezed and said: "All praise is for Allah..." And he mentioned the hadith.

The Qur'an, the hadith and the reports indicate that He, glorified is He, breathed into him of His spirit after the creation of his body, and by that breathing the spirit came to be in him. If his spirit had been created before his body, together with the entire spirits of his descendants, the angels would not have marvelled at his creation, nor at the creation of the Fire, nor would they have said: "For what purpose did You create it?" For they would have been seeing the spirits of the children of Adam, among them believers and disbelievers, good and wicked.

And since the spirits of all the disbelievers followed Iblis, indeed the disbelieving spirits would have been created before his disbelief. Rather, Allah, glorified is He, only judged him to be a disbeliever after the creation of Adam's body and spirit, and he had not been a disbeliever before that. So how could the spirits before him be disbelieving and believing, when he was not a disbeliever at that time? Did disbelief come to the spirits except through his adornment and seduction? So the disbelieving spirits came into being after his disbelief. Unless it is said that they were all believers and then apostatized because of him. But what they have used as evidence for the priority of the creation of the spirits contradicts that.

In the hadith of Abu Hurayrah concerning the creation of the world, the reports about the species of the world mention that the creation of Adam was delayed until Friday. If the spirits had been created before the bodies, they would have been part of the world created in six days. Since their creation is not mentioned in these days, it is known that their creation follows the creation of the offspring, and that only the creation of Adam alone took place in those six days. As for the creation of his descendants, it is in the observed and witnessed manner.

If the spirit had existence before the body, while it was living, knowing and speaking, it would have remembered that in this world and been aware of it in some way.

And it is impossible for it to be living, knowing, speaking and recognizing its Lord while among a gathering of spirits, and then to transfer to this body without being aware of its condition before that in any way.

And if after separation it is aware of its condition while in the body in detail, and knows what it was here, even though it acquired through the body matters that hindered it from much of its perfection, then it is all the more fitting, by way of priority, that it would be aware of its first state while not hindered there. Unless it is said: its attachment to the body and its occupation with managing it prevented it from awareness of its first state.

It is said: Suppose that it prevented it from awareness of it in detail and completeness. Does it prevent it from even the slightest awareness of something of what it was before attachment to the body? It is known that its attachment to the body did not prevent it from awareness of its first states while in the body. So how would it prevent it from awareness of what was before that?

Furthermore, if it had existed before the body, it would have been knowing, living, speaking and rational. When it became attached to the body, it lost all of that, and then awareness, knowledge and reason came to it little by little. If that were so, it would be the most astonishing of matters that the spirit was complete and rational, then returned weak and ignorant, then returned after that to its reason and strength. Where in reason, transmission and natural disposition is there anything indicating this? Allah, Exalted is He, has said: ﴿And Allah brought you out from the wombs of your mothers, knowing nothing, and He made for you hearing, sight and hearts that perhaps you would be grateful﴾. So this state in which He brought us out is our original state, and knowledge, reason, recognition and strength are acquired by us, arising in us after they were not. We did not know anything at all before that, for we had no existence by which we could know or reason.

Furthermore, if they had been created before the bodies, while being as they are now, of good and wickedness, disbelief and faith, good and evil, that would have been established for them before the deeds. But they only acquired these qualities and states through their deeds, which they strove to attain, seeking help through the body. So they would not have been characterized by those states and attributes before they came to be in the bodies through which they performed those deeds.

If it was decreed for them before their existence, and then they came out into this abode according to what was decreed for them, then we do not deny the Book and the prior decree from Allah. And if some evidence showed that they were created as a whole and then deposited in a place, living, knowing and speaking, and then each moment they emerged into their bodies little by little, we would be the first to say it.

Allah, glorified is He, is over all things capable. But we do not report about Him any creation or command except what He has reported about Himself upon the tongue of His Messenger (ﷺ). It is known that the Messenger (ﷺ) did not report that about Him. Rather he reported what is in the authentic hadith: "Indeed, the creation of the son of Adam is gathered in his mother's belly for forty days as a drop (nutfah), then it becomes a clinging clot (alaqah) for a similar period, then it becomes a lump of flesh (mudghah) for a similar period, then the angel is sent to him and he breathes the spirit into him." So the angel alone is sent to him, and he breathes into him, and when he breathes into him, that is the cause of the spirit coming into being in him. He did not say: "The angel is sent to him with the spirit, and he places it in his body." Rather, the angel is sent to him, and he brings the spirit into being in him by breathing into him. It is not that Allah, glorified is He, sent to him a spirit that had been existing with the angel for a long time before that. So there is a distinction between the angel being sent to him to breathe the spirit into him, and a created spirit, self-subsisting, being sent to him together with the angel. Consider what the text indicates of these two meanings. And success is from Allah.

[Chapter: The Error of the Qadariyyah concerning the Meaning of Fitrah, and the Refutation Against Them]

Our Shaykh said: Know that when this hadith became a proof used by the Qadariyyah (those who deny divine predestination) for their corrupt doctrine, people began to interpret it in ways that remove it from its apparent meaning. The Qadariyyah, from among the Mu'tazilah (the rationalist school) and others, say: "Every newborn is born upon Islam, and Allah does not misguide anyone, but his parents make him go astray." The hadith is a proof against them in two respects.

The first: according to the Mu'tazilah and others among the theologians, none of them is born upon Islam at all, and Allah has not made anyone a Muslim or a disbeliever. Rather, this one brought disbelief upon himself, and that one brought Islam upon himself. Allah has not done either of them, according to them, without dispute among the Qadariyyah. Rather, He called them to Islam, removed their impediments, and gave each of them an equal capacity to accept either faith or disbelief. He did not single out the believer with a cause that necessitates the attainment of faith, for that is, according to them, not within His power, and if it were within His power it would be injustice. This is the position of the majority of the Mu'tazilah, although some of their later scholars, such as Abu al-Husayn, say that He singled out the believer with the motive toward faith, and say that when the motive and capacity are present, the existence of faith is necessary. This, in reality, agrees with the People of the Sunnah. This is the first respect.

The second: they say that the knowledge of Allah is not attained except through reflection conditioned upon the intellect. So it is impossible, according to them, that knowledge should be innate, or that it should be an act of Allah, Exalted is He. Even if the Qadariyyah argue with His words: "Then his parents make him a Jew, or a Christian, or a Magian," on the basis that He attributed the change to the parents, it is said to them: You yourselves say that Allah cannot, nor any of His creatures, make the two of them Jews, nor Christians, nor Magians. Rather, they themselves did that by their own selves, without power from anyone else, and without action from anyone else. Then there is no proof for you in His words: "Then his parents make him a Jew, or a Christian, or a Magian."

The People of the Sunnah agree that other than Allah cannot place guidance or misguidance in the heart of anyone. The Ummah has agreed that what is meant by this is the parents' calling of the child to that, their encouraging him toward it, and their raising the child upon it, as a teacher does with a young child. The mention of the parents is based on the common and customary, and otherwise it may occur through one of them or through someone else, both in reality and in ruling.

Muhammad ibn Nasr said: Ibn Qutaybah used as evidence His words: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam from their loins their descendants and made them testify concerning themselves: "Am I not your Lord?" They said: "Yes, we have testified"﴾. So they answered with words of witnesses confessing against themselves that Allah is their Lord, and then they were born upon that.

Muhammad ibn Nasr said: His saying "then they were born upon that" is an addition from him that is not in the Book, nor does it come in any of the reports.

We will mention the reports narrated in the interpretation of this verse, to show the reader that there is no proof for him in them, and that there is no evidence in any of them that children are born knowing Allah from the moment they fall from their mothers' wombs.

I say: If by his saying "then they were born upon that" he means that they were born, at the moment of their emergence from their mothers' wombs, knowing Allah, His Oneness, His names and His attributes, then he is correct in refuting it. But if he means that they were born upon the ruling of that covenant, and that if they were left they would not turn away from it when they reached understanding, then that is the correct view which cannot be rejected.

Muhammad said: Because of what has been narrated in the interpretation of this verse, there is the hadith of Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him: Yahya narrated to us, saying: I read to Malik, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn al-Khattab, from Muslim ibn Yasar al-Juhani, that Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked about this verse: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam from their loins their descendants﴾. He said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) being asked about it, and he said: 'Indeed Allah, Exalted is He, created Adam, then He wiped his back with His right hand and extracted from it descendants. He said: I created these for Paradise, and they will do the deeds of the people of Paradise. Then He wiped his back and extracted from it descendants, and He said: I created these for the Fire, and they will do the deeds of the people of the Fire.'" A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, then for what is the deed?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, when Allah creates a servant for Paradise, He makes him work by the deeds of the people of Paradise until he dies upon a deed of the deeds of the people of Paradise, and so he enters Paradise by it. And when He creates a servant for the Fire, He makes him work by the deeds of the people of the Fire until he dies upon a deed of the deeds of the people of the Fire, and so he enters the Fire by it."

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 7, verse 172 (part 5 of 7):

Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Sinan al-Ruhawi narrated to us, from his father: Zayd ibn Abi Unaysa informed us, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Muslim ibn Yasar, from Nu'aym ibn Rabi'a al-Azdi. Muslim said: "I asked Nu'aym about this verse, and Nu'aym said: 'I was with Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, when a man came and asked him about it.' Then he said... (the hadith)." This shows the defect ('illah, a hidden flaw that undermines a report) in the first hadith, and that Muslim ibn Yasar did not hear it from Umar.

He said: Ishaq narrated to us: Hakkam ibn Salm informed us, from Anbasa, from Umara ibn Umayr, from Abu Muhammad, a man from the people of Madina, who said: "I asked Umar ibn al-Khattab about the words of the Most High: ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their offspring﴾. He said: 'I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about it just as you have asked me, and he said: "Allah created Adam with His hand, and breathed into him of His spirit. Then He set a term for him, and wiped his back, and brought forth from it offspring. He said: These are for Paradise, and they will do the deeds of the people of Paradise, and I will seal for them with the best of their deeds, and I will admit them to Paradise. Then He wiped his back and brought forth offspring, and said: These are for the Fire, and they will do the deeds of the people of the Fire, and I will seal for them with the worst of their deeds, and I will admit them to the Fire."'"

I say: Malik included this hadith in his Muwatta, despite the defect in it, and we will mention its defect.

al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan (good) hadith. Muslim ibn Yasar did not hear it from Umar. Some have mentioned in this chain, between Muslim ibn Yasar and Umar, an unknown man (majhul)."

Abu al-Qasim Hamza ibn Muhammad al-Kinani said: "Muslim ibn Yasar did not hear this from Umar; he narrated it from Nu'aym, from Umar."

Ibn Abi Khaythama said: "I read to Yahya ibn Ma'in the hadith of Malik, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysa, and he wrote with his own hand against Muslim ibn Yasar: 'Not known (la yu'raf).'"

Abu Umar said: "This is a munqati' (broken-chain) hadith with this isnad (chain), because this Muslim ibn Yasar did not meet Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, and between them in this hadith is Nu'aym ibn Rabi'a. And this, even with this isnad, cannot be used as proof. This Muslim ibn Yasar is unknown (majhul); it is said he was from Madina, and he is not Muslim ibn Yasar al-Basri."

He said: "The sum of what is said about this hadith is that its isnad is not sound (la laysa isnaduhu bi-al-qa'im), because Muslim ibn Yasar and Nu'aym ibn Rabi'a are both not known as bearers of knowledge. However, the meaning of this hadith has been authenticated from the Prophet ﷺ through many firm routes, too long to mention, from the hadith of Umar ibn al-Khattab and others." End of quotation.

We will now mention some of those hadiths.

Ishaq ibn Rahawayh said: Baqiyya ibn al-Walid informed us, saying: al-Zubaydi Muhammad ibn al-Walid informed me, from Rashid ibn Sa'd, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Qatada al-Nasri, from his father, from Hisham ibn Hakim ibn Hizam: "A man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, are deeds begun (from scratch), or has the decree already been finalized?' He said: 'When Allah brought forth the offspring of Adam from his back, He made them bear witness against themselves. Then He poured them into His two palms and said: These are for Paradise, and these are for the Fire. The people of Paradise are made easy for the deeds of the people of Paradise, and the people of the Fire are made easy for the deeds of the people of the Fire.'"

Abd al-Samad narrated to us: Hammad narrated to us: al-Juraythi narrated to us, from Abu Nadra: "A man from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, called Abu Abd Allah, had his companions visit him while he was ill, and he was weeping. They said: 'What makes you weep?' He said: 'I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Allah grasped a handful with His right hand, and another with His other hand, and said: This is for this, and this is for this, and I do not care." So I do not know in which of the two handfuls I am.'"

Amr ibn Muhammad informed us: Isma'il ibn Rafi' narrated to us, from al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: "Allah created Adam from earth, then made him clay, then left him until he became mud moulded (hama' masnun), then shaped him and formed him, then left him until he became dry clay like pottery. Iblis would pass by him and say: 'You were created for a great matter!' Then Allah breathed into him of His spirit. He (Adam) said: 'O my Lord, what of my offspring?' He said: 'Choose, O Adam.' He said: 'I choose the right hand of my Lord, and both hands of my Lord are right hands.' Then Allah spread out His palm, and behold, everyone who is to be of his offspring was in the palm of the Most Merciful."

al-Nadr informed us: Abu Ma'shar informed us, from Sa'id al-Maqburi and Nafi', mawla of al-Zubayr, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "When Allah wanted to create Adam, (and he mentioned the creation of Adam), He said to him: 'O Adam, which of My two hands do you love more that I show you your offspring in it?' He said: 'The right hand of my Lord, and both hands of my Lord are right hands.' So He spread out His right hand, and behold, in it were all his offspring, whatever He would create until the Day of Resurrection. The righteous was in his (proper) form, the afflicted in his form, and the prophets in their forms. He said: 'Did You not make them all rich?' He said: 'I wished to be thanked.'" ... And he mentioned the hadith.

Muhammad ibn Nasr said: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us: Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us: al-Layth ibn Sa'd informed us: Ibn Ajlan related to me, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi, from his father, from Abd Allah ibn Salam who said: "Allah created Adam, then said (with) His two hands, and grasped them, and said: 'Choose, O Adam.' He said: 'I choose the right hand of my Lord, and both your hands are right hands.' So He opened it, and behold, in it was his offspring. He said: 'Who are these, O Lord?' He said: 'Those whom I decreed to create from your offspring, from the people of Paradise, until the Hour is established.'"

Ishaq narrated to us: Ja'far ibn Awn al-Khuza'i narrated to us: Hisham ibn Sa'd informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: "When Allah created Adam, He wiped his back, and there fell from his back every soul (nasama) that He would create from his offspring until the Day of Resurrection." ... And he mentioned the hadith.

Ishaq and Amr ibn Zurara narrated to us, saying: Isma'il informed us, from Kulthum ibn Jubayr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, concerning the words of the Most High: ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their offspring﴾ ... the verse. He said: "Your Lord wiped the back of Adam, and there came forth from him every soul that He would create until the Day of Resurrection, at Nu'man, this (valley) which is beyond Arafat. Then He took their covenant: 'Am I not your Lord?' They said: 'Yes, we bear witness.'"

Ishaq narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us: Rabi'a ibn Kulthum ibn Jabr narrated to us, from his father, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, concerning the words of the Most High: ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their offspring﴾ ... the verse. He said: "Allah wiped the back of Adam while he was in the bottom of Nu'man, a valley beside Arafat, and He brought forth from the back of Adam his offspring, and made them bear witness against themselves: 'Am I not your Lord?' They said: 'Yes, we bear witness.'"

Then Ishaq narrated it through multiple routes from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both. Then he said:

al-Makhzumi, who is al-Mughira ibn Salama, informed us: Abu Hilal narrated to us, from Abu Jamra al-Dab'i, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "Allah wiped the back of Adam, and brought forth his offspring in a drop of water (adhiyy min al-ma')."

Jarir informed us, from al-A'mash, from Muslim al-Batin, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "Allah wiped the back of Adam, and there came forth from it every offspring in scattered form until the Day of Resurrection, and they were presented to him."

al-Mala'i narrated to us: al-Mas'udi narrated to us, from Ali ibn Badhima, from Sa'id, from Ibn Abbas, concerning the words of the Most High: ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam﴾ ... the verse, he said: "Allah took from Adam his covenant that He is his Lord, and wrote his term, his provision, and his calamities. Then He brought forth from his back his offspring like the form of dhurr (tiny particles). He took their covenant that He is their Lord, and wrote their terms, their provisions, and their calamities."

Waki' narrated to us: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "Allah wiped the back of Adam, and brought forth every good one in His right hand, and in His other hand every wicked one."

Yahya narrated to us: al-Mas'udi narrated to us: Ali ibn Badhima informed me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, concerning this verse, who said: "Allah created Adam, and took his covenant that He is his Lord, and wrote his term, his provision, and his misfortune. Then He brought forth his offspring from his back like the form of dhurr, and took their covenants that He is their Lord, and wrote their terms, their provisions, and their misfortunes."

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, concerning this verse, who said: "Allah wiped over the loins of Adam, and brought forth from his loins whatever would be of his offspring until the Day of Resurrection, and took their covenant that He is their Lord, and they gave Him that. So no one asks anyone, whether a disbeliever or other, 'Who is your Lord?' except that he says: 'Allah.'"

Ma'mar said: al-Hasan used to say the same.

Ishaq said: Jarir also informed us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Abd Allah ibn Amr, concerning the words of the Most High: ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam﴾ ... the verse, who said: "He took them as a comb is drawn through the hair of the head."

Muhammad ibn Nasr said: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Za'farani narrated to us: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from al-Zubayr ibn Musa, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "Allah, the Most High, struck the right shoulder of Adam, and there came forth every created soul destined for Paradise, white and pure. He said: 'These are the people of Paradise.' Then He struck his left shoulder, and there came forth every created soul destined for the Fire, black. He said: 'These are the people of the Fire.' Then He took their pledge to belief in Him, and knowledge of Him, and obedience to His command, and affirmation of Him and His command, from all the children of Adam, and made them bear witness against themselves, and they believed, affirmed, knew, and acknowledged."

Ishaq said: Rawh ibn Ubada narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik narrated to us, from his father, from al-Zubayr ibn Musa, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, with this hadith, and he added: Ibn Jurayj said: "And it reached me that He brought them forth on His palm like mustard seeds."

Ishaq said: Hakkam ibn Salm al-Razi narrated to us: Abu Ja'far al-Razi narrated to us, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-Aliya, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, concerning the words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam﴾ ... the verse, who said: "He gathered them that day in one gathering, (comprising) all that would exist until the Day of Resurrection. He made them spirits, then shaped them, then made them speak, and they spoke. He took from them the covenant and pledge, and made them bear witness against themselves. He said: 'I call upon you to witness the heavens and the seven earths, and I call upon you to witness your father Adam, that you will not say on the Day of Resurrection: We did not know this. Know that there is no god but Me, and no lord but Me, and do not associate anything with Me. I will send to you messengers who will remind you of My covenant and My pledge, and I will send down to you My Books.' They said: 'We bear witness that You are our Lord and our God, and there is no lord but You, and no god for us but You.' So they acknowledged obedience that day. Their father Adam was raised up for them, and he looked and saw among them the rich and the poor, the handsome and those less so. He said: 'O Lord, if only You had made Your servants equal!' He said: 'I wished to be thanked.' He saw among them the prophets like lamps, upon them light, and they were singled out with another covenant concerning the message and prophethood. This is He who says: ﴿And (mention) when We took from the prophets their covenant﴾ [al-Ahzab: 7]..."

...up to his saying: "...*ghalīẓan* (severe)." He is the one who says: ﴿So set your face toward the religion, upright, the natural disposition (*fiṭra*) of God upon which He created mankind; there is no altering the creation of God﴾ [al-Rūm: 30]. Therefore He says: ﴿This is a warner of the warners of old﴾ [al-Najm: 56]. And concerning this He says: ﴿And We found most of them without fidelity to a covenant﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 102]. And concerning this He says: ﴿Then after him We sent messengers to their peoples, and they brought them clear proofs, but they were not going to believe in what they had denied before﴾ [Yūnus: 74]. He knew, on the day they acknowledged what they acknowledged, who would deny it and who would affirm it.

He said: The spirit of ʿĪsā was among those spirits over which the covenant and the pledge were taken in the time of Ādam. So He sent that [spirit] to Maryam, until ﴿she withdrew from her family﴾ [Maryam: 16]... up to his saying: "...(*ḥamalathu*) (she conceived him)..." — she conceived the one who addressed her, and he is the spirit of ʿĪsā.

In the *Tafsīr* of Asbāṭ ibn Naṣr, from al-Suddī, from Abū Mālik and from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās; "and from Murra al-Hamdānī, from Ibn Masʿūd; and from some men of the companions of the Prophet ﷺ," concerning His saying: ﴿And when your Lord took...﴾ — the verse — he said: When God brought Ādam out of the Garden, before he descended from the heaven, He wiped the right side of Ādam's back, and brought forth from it offspring white like pearls, and like the form of tiny ants (*dharr*). He said to them: "Enter the Garden by My mercy." Then He wiped the left side of his back, and brought forth from it offspring black like the form of tiny ants, and He said: "Enter the Fire, and I do not care." That is when He says: ﴿And the companions of the right﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 27] and ﴿the companions of the left﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 41]. Then He took from them the covenant, saying: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾ They said: ﴿Yes﴾. So some gave it willingly and some unwillingly. The angels said: ﴿We bear witness, lest you say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were unaware of this"; or lest you say, "Only our fathers associated others with God before, and we were offspring after them. Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did?"﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 172–173]. Therefore there is no one of the children of Ādam except that he knows that his Lord is God, and no polytheist except that he says: ﴿We found our fathers upon a community﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 22]. Therefore is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And when your Lord took...﴾, the verse. And that is when He says: ﴿And to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 83]. And that is when He says: ﴿Say, "To God belongs the conclusive argument; so if He had willed, He would have guided you all"﴾ [al-Anʿām: 149]. He said: meaning the day He took the covenant from them.

Isḥāq said: Rawḥ ibn ʿUbāda informed us, Mūsā ibn ʿUbayda al-Rabadhī related to us, he said: I heard Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazī say concerning this verse: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Ādam﴾: they acknowledged to Him with faith and knowledge — the spirits, before He created their bodies.

Isḥāq said: al-Faḍl ibn Mūsā related to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik, from ʿAṭāʾ, he said: They were brought out from the loins of Ādam when He took the covenant from them, then they were returned into his loins.

Isḥāq said: ʿAlī ibn al-Ajlaḥ informed us, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, he said: God brought forth from the back of Ādam, on the day He created him, all that will exist until the Hour is established. He brought them out like tiny ants and said: "Am I not your Lord?" They said: "Yes." The angels said: "We bear witness, lest they say on the Day of Resurrection, 'Indeed, we were unaware of this.'" Then He grasped a handful with His right hand and said: "These are for the Garden," and grasped another and said: "These are for the Fire."

Muḥammad ibn Naṣr said: Bundār related to us, Abū Aḥmad related to us, Sufyān related to us, from al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas, from Abū al-ʿĀliya concerning His saying: ﴿And to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 83]. He said: It is His taking of the covenant.

Muḥammad said: We have mentioned what reached us of the reports transmitted from the *salaf* (early pious predecessors) concerning the interpretation (*taʾwīl*) of His saying: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Ādam﴾, the verse. None of them states that the child falls from its mother's womb while knowing God, nor is there in any of them evidence for that.

I say: Abū Muḥammad did not mean that they were born knowing God with a knowledge actually present with them; rather he meant that they were born according to the ruling of that *fiṭra* and the covenant that was taken from them, such that if they were left to their *fiṭra* they would not deviate from what that requires.

Muḥammad said: It is said to him: Do you have any evidence indicating that the *fiṭra* about which the Prophet ﷺ informed — "that every newborn is born upon it" — is knowledge of God? Or is there any report from one of the *salaf* that he said so? Or does it indicate that by analogy (*qiyās*)? If he brings any of these proofs, well and good; otherwise the falsehood of his claim becomes evident.

If he returns to His saying: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Ādam from their loins﴾, the verse, and says: God's calling the offspring of Ādam to witness that He is their Lord is evidence that knowledge of that was already present with them, just as He called them to witness it — then this is the full extent of his argument in his own view.

It is said to him: Because every one called to witness regarding something whose knowledge was not previously present to him before the witnessing, the one calling him has induced him to bear witness to falsehood, and God does not command anyone to that.

It is said to him: Your answering of something other than what you were asked, and your argument for it, is itself the proof of your incapacity, and that you have no proof. We did not ask you about the time at which God called them to witness and said to them: "Am I not your Lord?", and they answered Him by saying: "Yes" — were they knowing at that time or not? Rather we asked you about the time of their falling from their mothers' wombs: do you have a proof establishing that they were knowing at that time?

If he says: The presence of knowledge in them at that time is evidence that they were born upon it, so in the time of birth they are in the state they were in before that.

It is said to him: They were also affirming at that time, because God, Mighty and Majestic, informed that He said: "Am I not your Lord?" They said: "Yes." And God, Mighty and Majestic, addresses only one who understands at the time of address, and answers only one who has understood the question. Their answer to Him in saying so is evidence that they understood from God, and comprehended from Him His calling them to witness: "Am I not your Lord?" So they answered Him after their intellect had grasped the address and understood it, by saying: "Yes." Thus they affirmed to Him lordship.

It is said to him: So do you say likewise that the child, when it falls from its mother's womb, at that very moment understands address if it is addressed, and answers it, and affirms to Him lordship, just like those who affirmed to Him lordship at the time He took the covenant from them? If he says, "Yes," his intellect has contradicted itself and direct observation refutes him. If he says, "No," I say: that is a difference between the two times, so their state at the time of birth became contrary to their state at the first time when the covenant was taken from them. It is then said to him: Likewise it is possible that they were knowing at the first time, while at the time of birth they were not knowing, as they were at the first time. For they understood the address, comprehended it, and answered affirming to God lordship, while at the time of birth they are otherwise.

I say: Everyone who holds that the covenant taken from them is that they were brought out from the loins of Ādam, addressed, and affirmed to Him lordship, and then returned into his loins — he definitely distinguishes between their state at that time and their state at the time of birth. Neither Ibn Qutayba nor anyone else says that they were born knowing, understanding, grasping the question and returning the answer.

The divisions are four. The first: their state at the time of taking the covenant and at the time of their falling is equal in knowledge and cognition. The second: both times are equal in the absence of that. The third: knowledge is present at the falling and absent at the taking of the covenant. These three divisions are false, and no one holds any of them. The fourth: their knowing and understanding at the time of taking the covenant, but not at the time of falling. This is held by everyone who says that He brought them out from the loins of their father Ādam, spoke to them, addressed them, called His angels to witness against them, had them witness against themselves, and then returned them into his loins.

This is the view of the majority of the *salaf* and the *khalaf* (later generations), and they rely upon the reports we have mentioned, both those traced to the Prophet (*marfūʿ*) and those traced to companions (*mawqūf*).

The best of them is the hadith of Muslim ibn Yasār, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may God be pleased with him, and we have mentioned the statements of the imams concerning it. Moreover, Isḥāq narrated it from Ḥakkām ibn Salm, from ʿUmāra ibn ʿUmayr, from Abū Muḥammad, a man of the people of Madīna, who said: "I asked ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may God be pleased with him, about this verse, and he said: I asked the Messenger of God ﷺ about it, and he said: 'God created Ādam with His hand, and breathed into him of His spirit. Then He seated him, wiped his back, and brought forth offspring. He said: "These offspring I have created for the Garden, and they will act with whatever deeds I will; then I will seal for them with the best of their deeds, and I will admit them to the Garden." Then He wiped his back and brought forth offspring, and said: "These offspring I have created for the Fire, and they will act with whatever deeds I will; then I will seal for them with the worst of their deeds, and I will admit them to the Fire."'" In this there is no mention of His addressing them, questioning them, or making them speak. It is consistent with the rest of the hadiths, and it seems that it is the one preserved from ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him.

As for the rest of the hadiths, the authentic one traced to the Prophet contains only the affirmation of the two handfuls and the distinguishing of the people of happiness from the people of wretchedness before their being brought out into the abode of obligation. Such as the hadith that Aḥmad narrated from ʿAbd al-Ṣamad, who said: Ḥammād related to us, al-Jurayrī related to us, "from Abū Naḍra, that a man of the companions of the Prophet ﷺ, called Abū ʿAbd Allāh, whose companions came to visit him while he was weeping. They said to him: 'What makes you weep?' He said: 'I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: "God grasped a handful with His right hand and another with His other hand, and said: 'This for this, and this for this, and I do not care.'"' So I do not know in which of the two handfuls I am!"
