**(A Subtle Point)**

Yahya ibn Ayyub said: In Madinah there was a young man whom ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (raḍiya Allahu ʿanhu) admired. One night, after the ʿIshaʾ prayer, he left, and a woman appeared before him and displayed herself to him, and he was captivated by her. She walked on, and he followed her until he stood at her door. He saw her, and the awareness of God was removed from his heart, and this verse came to him: ﴿Indeed, those who fear God, when a passing impulse from Satan touches them, remember, and then they see clearly.﴾

He fell unconscious. The woman looked at him and saw he was like a dead man. She and a servant girl of hers kept working together on him until they threw him down at the door of his house. His father came out and found him lying at the door, in a state of distress, so he carried him in. He regained consciousness, and his father asked him, "What has befallen you, my son?" He did not tell him, and his father kept at him until he told him. When he recited the verse, he gave a great gasp, and his soul departed. The story reached ʿUmar (raḍiya Allahu ʿanhu), and he said, "Why did you not inform me of his death?"

So he went and stood at the young man's grave and called out, "O so-and-so, ﴿And for one who fears the standing before his Lord there are two gardens.﴾"

A voice was heard from inside the grave: "My Lord has given me that, O ʿUmar."

Al-Hasan mentioned this story from ʿUmar (raḍiya Allahu ʿanhu) in a different form. He said: In the time of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (raḍiya Allahu ʿanhu) there was a young man who was constant in the mosque and in worship. A girl fell in love with him, and he entertained the thought of her. Then he remembered, and he saw clearly, and he gave a gasp from which he fainted. An uncle of his came and carried him to his home. When he regained consciousness, he said, "O uncle, go to ʿUmar, convey my greetings to him, and say to him: What is the reward of one who feared the standing before his Lord?"

The uncle informed ʿUmar, who came to him, but he had died. ʿUmar said, "For you are two gardens."

**(Section)**

God, Exalted, has censured in His Book the one who forgets what his hands have sent forward. He said: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the signs of his Lord and turns away from them and forgets what his hands have sent forward?﴾ [al-Kahf: 57]. When he looks at his wrongdoing, he exerts himself to make up for what he has missed, through knowledge and action. He frees himself from the bondage of wrongdoing through seeking forgiveness, through regret, and through seeking *tamhis* (purification, i.e., the cleansing of what is impure), which is the purging of his faith and his knowledge from the impurity of wrongdoing, like the refining of gold and silver, which is their separation from their impurities. Entry into Paradise is not possible without this purification, for it is pure, and only the pure enter it. For this reason the angels say to them: ﴿Peace be upon you; you are good, so enter it, abiding eternally.﴾ [al-Zumar: 73]. And God, Exalted, said: ﴿Those whom the angels take in death while they are pure, saying, "Peace be upon you; enter the Garden for what you used to do."﴾ [al-Nahl: 32]. Therefore there is not a particle of impurity in Paradise.

This purification takes place in the life of this world through four things: repentance, seeking forgiveness, good deeds that erase, and afflictions that expiate. If these four purify him and cleanse him, he will be among ﴿those whom the angels take in death while they are pure﴾ [al-Nahl: 32], who give them the good news of Paradise, and he will be among those upon whom the angels descend at death: ﴿Do not fear and do not grieve, and receive good news of the Garden which you were promised. We are your allies in the life of this world and in the Hereafter, and for you therein is whatever your souls desire, and for you therein is whatever you ask for, as a welcome from the Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.﴾ [Fussilat: 30–32].

If these four do not fulfill this purification and cleansing, then the repentance was not sincere (*nasuh*), which is comprehensive, all-encompassing, and truthful, and the seeking of forgiveness was not beneficial. This is not the forgiveness of one who holds a cup of intoxicant in his hand, saying, "I seek forgiveness from God," and then raises it to his mouth. The good deeds, in their quantity and quality, were not sufficient for expiation, nor were the afflictions. This is either because the wrongdoing is great, or because the one being purified is weak, or because of both. He is then purified in the *barzakh* (the intermediate state between death and resurrection) through three things:

The first: the funeral prayer offered for him by the believers, their seeking forgiveness for him, and their intercession for him.

The second: his purification through the trial of the grave, the terror of the questioning angel, the squeezing of the grave, the rebuke, and what follows from these.

The third: what his Muslim brothers send to him as gifts of acts of worship, such as charity on his behalf, Hajj, fasting on his behalf, recitation of the Qur'an on his behalf, prayer, and conferring the reward of these upon him. People have agreed on the arrival of the reward of charity and supplication. Imam Ahmad said: "They do not differ regarding that. As for other acts, there is disagreement concerning them. Most scholars say that the reward of Hajj arrives. Abu Hanifa says that only the reward of spending reaches him. Ahmad and those who agree with him have the broadest position among the schools: they say that the reward of all acts of nearness to God reaches him, both physical and financial, and the combining of both." They argue that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to one who asked him, "O Messenger of God, is there any kindness that remains for my parents that I can show them after their death?" He said, "Yes," and then mentioned the hadith. And the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever dies owing fasting, his guardian shall fast on his behalf."

If this does not suffice for purification, he is purified before his Lord at the place of standing (on the Day of Judgment) through four things: the terrors of the Resurrection, the severity of the standing place, the intercession of the intercessors, and the pardon of God, Mighty and Majestic.

If these three do not suffice for his purification, then he must enter the furnace (*kir*), as a mercy on his behalf, so that he may be freed and purified, and cleansed in the Fire. The Fire will be a purification for him and a cleansing of his impurity. His duration in it will be according to the abundance or scarcity of his impurity, its intensity or weakness, and its accumulation. When his impurity has come out and his gold has been refined, and he has become pure and unadulterated, he will be taken out of the Fire and admitted into Paradise.

He said: The third, meaning among the stages of wakefulness, is attentiveness to knowing the gain and loss of days, disowning the wasting of them, and looking at their remaining value in order to make up for what has passed and to make the remainder fruitful.

That is, he knows what he has of gain and loss, so he makes up for what he has missed in the rest of his life, which has no price. He is stingy with his hours, indeed with his breaths, lest they go to waste on something that does not bring him closer to God. This is the true meaning of the loss that is common among people, though they differ in its extent, little or much. Every breath that goes out in something that does not bring one closer to God is a regret for the servant on his return, a halt for him on the path of his journey, a setback if it continues, or a veil if it cuts him off.

He said: As for knowledge of blessing, it becomes clear through three things: the light of the intellect, the removal of the veil by the sight of favours, and considering the people of affliction.

That is, the reality of witnessing blessing becomes clear through these three. They are the light that brings about wakefulness, so that the heart is illumined by it to see awareness. According to its strength or weakness, the witnessing of blessing becomes clear to him. For whoever does not see God's blessing upon him except in his food, his clothing, his bodily health, and the esteem of his person among people, has no share of this light at all. The blessing of God through Islam and faith, and the drawing of His servant to turn toward Him, to delight in remembering Him, and to find pleasure in obeying Him, is the greatest of blessings. This is perceived only through the light of the intellect and the guidance of success.

Likewise, the "removal of the veil" is by the sight of God's favours upon him: looking at them and contemplating them through the clouds of nature and the darkness of the soul. And looking at the people of affliction, who are people heedless of God and innovators in the religion of God. These two categories are truly the people of affliction. When he sees them and knows their condition, the blessing of God upon him becomes great in his heart, it becomes clear to him, and he knows its worth. The opposite shows the goodness of its opposite, and by its opposite things are distinguished.

Indeed, among the perfection of the bliss of the people of Paradise is their seeing the people of the Fire and what they are in of punishment.

He said: As for contemplating wrongdoing, it is correct through three things: magnifying the Truth, knowing the self, and affirming the threat.

That is, whoever has the greatness of the Truth, Exalted, perfected in his heart, his opposition to Him becomes great in his sight, because opposing the Great is not like opposing one who is less. Whoever knows the measure of his own self and its reality, and its essential poverty before its Master, the Truth, at every moment and breath, and its great need for Him, the wrongdoing of opposing one upon whom it is most dependent at every moment and breath becomes great in his sight.

Also, when he knows its insignificance together with the greatness of the one he opposed, the wrongdoing becomes great in his sight, and he exerts himself to be freed from it. In proportion to his affirmation of the threat and his certainty about it, his exertion to be free from the wrongdoing that will overtake him will be proportionate.

The axis of happiness and the pivot of its millstone rest upon affirming the threat. When affirming the threat is absent from his heart, it is ruined in a ruin in which no success is hoped for at all. God, Exalted, informed us that the signs and warnings benefit only those who affirm the threat and fear the punishment of the Hereafter. These are the ones addressed by the warning and who benefit from the signs, not others. God, Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign for whoever fears the punishment of the Hereafter.﴾ [Hud: 103]. He said: ﴿You are only a warner to those who fear it.﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 45]. He said: ﴿So remind by the Qur'an those who fear My warning.﴾ [Qaf: 45]. And God, Exalted, informed us that the people of salvation in this world and the Hereafter are those who affirm the threat and fear it. He said: ﴿And We will surely settle you in the land after them. That is for whoever fears My standing and fears My warning.﴾ [Ibrahim: 14].

He said: As for knowing the gain and loss of days, it becomes upright through three things: hearing knowledge, answering the call of sacredness (*hurmah*), and companionship with the righteous. The foundation of all of that is shedding habits.

That is, the wayfarer, according to his knowledge of the levels of deeds and the precious gains, will know his gain and loss in his state and his faith. Likewise, he should check whether his heart responds quickly to the call to honour the sacred things of God, or is slow to respond. According to the swiftness or slowness of his response to the call, his gain and loss will be determined.

Likewise, companionship with those of resolve, and those who strive to catch up with the Exalted Assembly, by which he knows what he has of gain and loss.

What enables him to acquire all of this is his departure from habits and familiar things, accustoming the soul to leaving them, and being a stranger among the heedless and those who turn away. Nothing is more harmful to the servant than habits taking possession of him. The disbelievers opposed the messengers only with established habits inherited from their ancestors who had passed on. Whoever does not accustom his soul to leaving them and departing from them, and to preparing for what is required of him, is cut off and barred from his success and triumph. ﴿And had they intended to go out, they would have prepared for it some equipment; but God disliked their being sent forth, so He held them back, and it was said, "Remain with those who remain."﴾ [al-Tawbah: 46].

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 7, verse 205:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And remember your Lord within yourself, humbly and in fear﴾

On this there are two opinions. The first: in your secret self and your heart. The second: with your tongue, such that you make yourself hear.

So Allah, exalted is He, commanded His Prophet to remember Him within himself.

Mujahid and Ibn Jurayj said: he was commanded to remember Him inwardly, with humility and submissiveness, without raising the voice or shouting. And it has already been mentioned.

The hadith of Abu Musa: "We were with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey, and our voices rose with the takbir. He said: 'O people, be gentle with yourselves, for you are not calling upon one who is deaf or absent. You are calling upon One who is All-Hearing and near, nearer to one of you than the neck of his mount.'"

Consider how He said in the verse of remembrance: ﴿And remember your Lord within yourself, humbly and in fear﴾, and in the verse of supplication: ﴿Call upon your Lord humbly and secretly﴾. So He mentioned humility in both together. It is abasement, self-effacement and brokenness, and it is the spirit of remembrance and supplication. He specified supplication with secrecy for the wisdom we have mentioned and others.

He specified remembrance with fear because the one who remembers has need of fear. For remembrance necessarily entails love and bears its fruit, without doubt. Whoever remembers Allah much, this brings him His love, and love that is not joined with fear does not benefit its possessor; rather it may harm him. For it produces presumption and familiarity, and it has often led many ignorant deluded people to consider themselves independent of the obligations, and they say:

"The purpose of acts of worship is only the worship of the heart, its turning to Allah, its love for Him and its devotion to Him. When that purpose is achieved, then occupying oneself with the means is void."

A man related to me that he rebuked one of these people for a retreat in which he abandoned attending Friday prayer. The shaykh said to him:

"Do not the jurists say that if one fears for some of his wealth, the Friday prayer is waived for him?"

He said: "Yes." He said: "Then the heart of the disciple is more precious to him than the loss of ten dirhams," or as he said. And if he goes out, his heart is lost, so guarding his heart is an excuse that waives the Friday prayer for him.

He said to him: "This is delusion. Rather, the obligation upon him is to go out to the command of Allah and to guard his heart with Allah."

So the guiding, knowing shaykh commands the disciple to go out to the command and to observe the guarding of his heart, or as he said.

Consider this great delusion, how it led these people to the complete stripping away from Islam. For whoever travels this path is stripped of general Islam as a snake is stripped of its skin, while he thinks he is among the elite of the elite. The cause of this is the absence of fear of Allah joined with love for Him and seeking Him. For this reason some of the early Muslims said: whoever worships Allah with love alone is a heretic (zindiq), whoever worships Him with fear alone is a Kharijite (haruri), and whoever worships Him with hope alone is a Murji'ite.

Whoever worships Him with love, fear and hope is a believer. Allah, exalted is He, combined these three stations in His saying: ﴿Those whom they call upon seek the means of access to their Lord, as to which of them would be nearest, and they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment﴾.

So seeking the means of access is His love, which calls to drawing near to Him. Then He mentioned hope and fear after it. This is the way of His servants and friends.

Often the matter leads those who worship Him with pure love to permitting what is forbidden, and they say: "The lover is not harmed by sin." Some of them have composed a work on this and mentioned a fabricated report: "When Allah loves the servant, sins do not harm him." This is certainly a lie and contrary to Islam. For sins harm every person in their very nature, like the harm of poison to the body. Even if it were supposed that this saying was reported from some of the shaykhs, as for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, far be it from him to say such a thing; yet it may be given an interpretation: that when Allah loves His servant, His love does not lead him to persist in a sin. For persisting in sin contradicts being a lover of Allah. And when he does not persist in sin, but hastens to sincere repentance from it, its trace is erased and the sin does not harm him. Whenever he sins, repents and turns back to Allah, the trace and harm of the sin depart from him. This meaning is sound.

The point is that stripping love and remembrance of fear exposes one to these dangers. But when it is joined with fear, it gathers him onto the path and returns him to it whenever he strays. Fear is like the whip with which one strikes his mount so it does not leave the road; hope is the driver's song that makes the journey pleasant for it; and love is its leader and its rein that guides it. When the mount has neither whip nor stick to turn it back when it swerves from the road, and it is left to ride off in wild wandering, it departs from the road and gets lost, and it does not guard the limits of Allah and His prohibitions.

Those who arrived at Allah reached Him by no means other than their fear, their hope and their love. Whenever the heart is empty of these three, it becomes corrupt with a corruption whose rectification is never hoped for, and whenever any of these weakens within it, its faith weakens to that degree.

Consider the secrets and wisdom of the Qur'an in joining fear with remembrance and secrecy with supplication, while it also indicates the joining of fear with supplication and secrecy with remembrance as well. For He said: "remember your Lord within yourself," and so He did not need after it to say "secretly." And He said of supplication: ﴿Call upon Him in fear and hope﴾ (7:56), so He did not need to say in the first: "call upon your Lord humbly and secretly." Thus each of the two verses is arranged in the best arrangement for what it contains, and they indicate this with the most complete indication.

He mentioned hope, which is expectation, in the verse of supplication because supplication is founded upon it. For the one who calls upon Allah, unless he hopes for what he asks and seeks, his soul does not stir to seek it, since seeking what one does not hope for is impossible. And He mentioned fear in the verse of remembrance because of the great need of the one who fears for it, as has preceded. So in each verse He mentioned what is fitting and most appropriate for it, of fear and hope. Blessed is He who sent down His speech as a healing for what is in the breasts, and as guidance and mercy for the believers.

(Benefit)

Every person of intellect knows that Satan has no way into him except from three directions:

The first: excess and extravagance, so that one exceeds the measure of need, and it becomes surplus, and that is Satan's portion and his entrance into the heart. The way of guarding against it is to refuse the self the full measure of what it seeks of food, sleep, pleasure or rest. Whenever this door is closed, safety from the enemy's entry is attained.

The second: heedlessness. For the one who remembers is within the fortress of remembrance. Whenever he is heedless, he opens the gate of the fortress, and the enemy enters, and it becomes difficult or hard to expel him.

The third: burdening oneself with what does not concern him in all things.

[Section: The difference between heedlessness and forgetfulness]

He said: Remembrance is the freeing of oneself from heedlessness and forgetfulness.

The difference between heedlessness and forgetfulness is that heedlessness is abandonment by the choice of the heedless, while forgetfulness is abandonment not by his choice. For this reason Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And do not be among the heedless﴾ and did not say: "do not be among the forgetful," for forgetfulness does not fall under obligation, so one is not forbidden from it.

(Section)

Remembrance is of two kinds. The first is the remembrance of the names and attributes of the Lord, blessed and exalted is He, and praising Him by them, and glorifying Him and sanctifying Him above what does not befit Him, blessed and exalted is He.

This too is of two kinds:

(The first) the composing of praise of Him by them by the one who remembers. This is the kind mentioned in the hadiths, such as "Subhan Allah," "al-hamdu lillah," "la ilaha illa Allah," "Allahu akbar," "Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi," "la ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lahu, lahu al-mulku wa lahu al-hamdu wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir," and the like.

The best of this kind is the most comprehensive in praise and the most general, such as "Subhan Allah, the number of His creation." This is better than merely "Subhan Allah." And your saying "al-hamdu lillah, the number of what He created in the heavens, and the number of what He created in the earth, and the number of what is between them, and the number of what He will create," is better than merely your saying "al-hamdu lillah."

This is in the hadith of Juwayriyya, that the Prophet ﷺ said to her: "I have said after you four words three times, which if weighed against what you have said since this morning, would outweigh them: Subhan Allah, the number of His creation; Subhan Allah, the pleasure of His self; Subhan Allah, the weight of His Throne; Subhan Allah, the ink of His words." Related by Muslim.

In al-Tirmidhi and the Sunan of Abu Dawud, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, that he entered with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ upon a woman before whom were date stones or pebbles with which she was counting tasbih, and he said: "Subhan Allah, the number of what He created in the heavens; and Subhan Allah, the number of what He created in the earth; and Subhan Allah, the number of what is between that; and Subhan Allah, the number of what He will create. And Allahu akbar, likewise; and la ilaha illa Allah, and la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah, likewise."

(The second) the informing about the Lord, exalted is He, of the rulings of His names and attributes, such as your saying: Allah, mighty and majestic, hears the voices of His servants and sees their movements, and no hidden thing of their deeds is concealed from Him; He is more merciful to them than their fathers and mothers; He is powerful over everything; He is more pleased at the repentance of His servant than one who has lost his mount, and the like.

The best of this kind is praising Him with what He praised Himself, and with what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ praised Him, without distortion or negation, and without likening or modelling. This kind too is of three types: hamd (praise), thana' (commendation) and majd (glory). So al-hamd lillah is the informing about Him by the attributes of His perfection, exalted and glorified is He, together with love for Him and contentment with Him. Thus the silent lover is not a praiser, nor is one who commends without love a praiser, until love and commendation are gathered in him. If he repeats praises one after another, it becomes commendation. If the praise is by attributes of majesty, greatness, magnificence and sovereignty, it becomes majd. Allah, exalted is He, gathered for His servant the three kinds at the beginning of al-Fatiha. When the servant says: ﴿Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, Allah says: "My servant has praised Me." When he says: ﴿The Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate﴾, He says: "My servant has commended Me." When he says: ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾, He says: "My servant has glorified Me."

(The second kind) of remembrance is the remembrance of His command, His prohibition and His rulings, and this too is of two kinds:

(The first) remembering it by informing about Him: that He commanded such and such, forbade such and such, loved such and such, was angered by such and such, and was pleased with such and such.

(The second) remembering Him at His command, so that one hastens to it, and at His prohibition, so that one flees from it. Remembering His command and prohibition is one thing, and remembering Him at His command and prohibition is another. When these kinds are gathered in the one who remembers, his remembrance is the best and most exalted and greatest of remembrance.

(Benefit)

This remembrance is part of the greatest understanding, and what is below it is the best remembrance when the intention in it is sound.

Whoever remembers Him, exalted is He, remembers His blessings, His favours, His kindness, His bounties and the places of His grace toward His servants, and this too is among the finest kinds of remembrance.

These are five kinds, and they may be with the heart and tongue together at times, and that is the best remembrance.

And with the heart alone at times, which is the second rank, and with the tongue alone at times, which is the third rank.

The best remembrance is that in which the heart and tongue agree. The remembrance of the heart alone is better than the remembrance of the tongue alone, because the remembrance of the heart produces knowledge, stirs love, arouses shame, inspires awe, calls to watchfulness, and restrains from neglect in acts of obedience and laxity in sins and misdeeds; whereas the remembrance of the tongue alone causes none of these, so its fruit is weak.
